pages.content_md:
You have had this happen before. You are cruising down the road or interstate when a sound like a gunshot hits your windshield. Luckily, in that case, it was a pebble and all of the damage you suffered was a cracked windshield.

Now, think if you are cruising down an interstate or road when a tractor trailer loses part of its cargo. It could be a piece of plastic pipe, a box of who knows what, or maybe even an entire passenger vehicle from a car carrier. Semi-trucks frequently carry loads such as lumber, logs, boulders, metal coils, concrete pipes, and massive industrial machinery and equipment. A vehicle usually strikes the debris from the commercial truck that now litters the roadway. Amazingly, an object weighing 20 pounds moving at 55 mph strikes the vehicle weighing almost half a ton! The consequences can be deadly and life-changing. If you have been involved in an accident because of unsecured truck cargo, contact a skilled truck accident attorney today.

In 2012, Congress funded the Government Accountability Office to conduct a study on crashes involving vehicles carrying unsecured loads. The study found that all 50 states and the District of Columbia have statutes pertaining to unsecured loads on commercial trucks; however, most of the states have exemptions for certain commercial activities. The exemptions mostly relate to agricultural loads.

When a commercial trucking load shift or does something unusual causing an accident involving injuries, an experienced Tractor Trailer Wreck Lawyer should investigate both the trucking company and the business shipping the products on the truck. Who loaded the truck? Which warehouse? Can an exact piece of freight be pinpointed as causing the shift? All of this evidence needs to be preserved to ensure proper investigation.

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration regulates the security of cargo on commercial trucks. The federal agency drafted the �Driver�s Handbook on Cargo Securement� in 2002. The broad requirement is that cargo must be secured in such a way that it must be secured in such a way that it stays in place �under all conditions that could reasonably be expected to occur in normal driving.� What are normal conditions? They include braking, accelerating, under windy conditions, taking turns, and in wet conditions.

Under the Federal Regulations, cargo on a commercial truck must also stay secure when the driver is making maneuvers to avoid an emergency such as another wreck or flooded road. The federal regulations require that the load be secured to the point that it will not leak, spill, blow off the vehicle, fall from the vehicle, fall through the vehicle, or shift upon or within the vehicle to such an extent that it will affect the vehicle�s stability or maneuverability.

There are a lot of products out there used to secure cargo on commercial trucks. Under federal regulations, the straps, chains, and other fasteners must sustain at least eighty percent of the full cargo weight when braking forward; fifty percent of weight when turning, accelerating, climbing a hill, or braking in reverse; and twenty percent of weight when going over a hill or bump.

Have you or a loved one been injured in an accident where a commercial truck had an improperly secured load? If so, we encourage that you contact a Metro Atlanta unsecured cargo truck accident lawyer at The Parian Law Firm, LLC to help you claim your damages and hold the at-fault party accountable.

pages.description: Seek financial recovery for injuries sustained on the job by consulting with a Carrollton workers' compensation lawyer immediately following your injury.
pages.content_md:
People�injured while on the job�in Georgia are entitled to medical benefits payments and a portion of their weekly earnings. �It does not matter whether the employee or the employer is responsible for the accident. �Because Georgia is a no-fault state when it comes to workers compensation, if you are injured on the job, you are entitled to the worker�s compensation benefits. �There could be a separate claim for your injuries if the accident was caused by an individual that did not work for your employer. You should consider hiring a Carrollton workers� compensation lawyer�with experience.

When the doctor caring for your work-related injuries takes you completely out of work or places you on light duty and the employer does not have light duty work available, you are entitled to temporary total disability benefits or TTD. �Under this benefit level, you are entitled to two-thirds of your average weekly wage up to $525.00 per week if injured prior to July 1, 2015. �If injured on or after July, 1, 2015, you are entitled to two-thirds of your average weekly wage up to $550.00 per week. �Temporary total disability benefits are paid for up to 400 weeks as a Carrollton workers’ compensation attorney can explain.

When placed on light duty work and your employer has a job for you to perform, you are entitled to temporary partial disability benefits or TPD. �When injured prior to July 1, 2015, you are entitled to two-thirds of the difference between your average weekly wage prior to your injury and your average weekly wage after the injury up to $360.00 per week. �If an employee suffers injuries on or after July 1, 2015, the maximum goes up to $375.00 per week.

Permanent Partial Disability

Permanent Partial Disability benefits or PPD is paid when a person loses the use of a body part due to a work-related injury. �Either your treating workers’ comp doctor or another authorized party will assign you a disability rating utilizing literature published by the American Medical Association. �The amount paid for PPD benefits depends upon you weekly income and what rating is given your loss. �Many times, the easiest way to understand PPD is that a third party will determine what percentage you are impaired due to the loss of use of the particular body part.

Under state workers compensation statute, the employer is responsible for your medical benefits if you are injured. The responsibility of the employer includes that they pay for treatment at medical appointments, transportation to and from medical care, prescriptions, surgery, and physical therapy.


Sometimes, if the employer is following the letter of the workers� compensation law in Carrollton, you should be presented with a list of doctors known as the �Panel of Physicians.� �Under law, if your employer presents you with such a panel that can treat your work-related injury, you can select a doctor off of the list of doctors. � The �Panel of Physicians� must have six independent facilities, including one minority and one orthopedic doctor listed for it to be valid. �If the �Panel of Physicians� is invalid, the employer loses control of the panel, and you are free to choose a doctor of your liking.

Nevertheless, if you are under the care of a doctor listed on your employer�s �Panel of Physicians� and are receiving one of the income benefits listed above, you are entitled to a one time independent medical exam or IME by a doctor of your choice. �An experienced Carrollton lawyer knows which doctors will provide the best second opinion and assistance with your workers� compensation claim.

Death Benefits in Carrollton Workers� Compensation

Georgia death benefits are paid to the spouse and/or minor children of a worker who dies on job. �A spouse and minor children are entitled to two-thirds of the deceased worker�s average weekly wage up to $525.00 per week. �A spouse with no dependent children can receive a maximum of $150,000 while minor children are entitled to death benefits until they reach age 18 (age 22 if they attend college). �In addition, Georgia workers� compensation laws cover funeral expenses up to $7,500.00.

What Damages Might a Plaintiff Recover?

A statute of limitations sets a limit on how long a person has to bring legal action.� After the statute of limitations period runs out, then any subsequent legal action is barred and denied. Within the state of Georgia, a person can bring a wrongful death action for two years after death.

pages.h1: Protecting Your Future: A Guide to Divorce and Child Custody in Carrollton, GA
pages.content_md:
When you drive past the Square in downtown Carrollton, life feels steady and predictable. But inside your home, a pending divorce can make everything feel like it’s shifting beneath your feet. If you are facing a separation involving children, you aren’t just fighting for assets; you are fighting for the Saturday morning soccer games at Lakeshore Park and the right to provide a stable future for your kids.

Navigating a divorce in Carrollton, GA requires more than just filling out forms. It requires an understanding of how local judges view parental responsibilities and how the newly updated 2026 Georgia legal statutes will impact your bank account and your time with your children. Whether your split is amicable or highly contested, the decisions made today will echo for a decade or more. This guide breaks down the essential local rules of Carroll County, the recent shifts in state support calculations, and the tactical steps you need to take to protect your parental rights.

Understanding Child Custody in Carroll County

The most emotional hurdle in any West Georgia divorce is the custody arrangement. In Georgia, the North Star for every decision is the “Best Interests of the Child” standard. This isn’t a vague suggestion; it is a legal framework that judges use to evaluate which parent can provide the most stable environment.

Physical vs. Legal Custody

It is a common misconception that custody is “all or nothing.” In reality, it is split into two categories:

• Legal Custody: This relates to decision-making authority. In most Carrollton cases, parents share joint legal custody, meaning they must consult one another on major decisions regarding education, healthcare, and religious upbringing.

• Physical Custody: This defines where the child actually lives. While “50/50” schedules are becoming more common in 2026, one parent is often designated as the “primary” custodian for school enrollment purposes.

The Role of the Parenting Plan

Every case in the Carroll County Superior Court requires a comprehensive Parenting Plan. This document is a roadmap for your life. It must detail exactly where the child will be for Christmas, Fall Break, and even who is responsible for transportation between homes. A vague plan is a recipe for future litigation.

[IMAGE: An infographic showing a sample 2026 Georgia Parenting Plan schedule with alternating holidays.]

Internal Link: [Learn more about our Mediation Services to help draft your Parenting Plan.]

The 2026 Georgia Child Support Calculations

As of January 1, 2026, Georgia has overhauled the way child support is calculated to better reflect the modern cost of living and the reality of shared parenting. If you haven’t looked at the guidelines recently, the old “estimates” no longer apply.

The Mandatory Parenting Time Adjustment

The biggest shift in the 2026 law is the Mandatory Parenting Time Adjustment. Previously, if a parent had significant time with the child, a judge could lower their support payment, but it wasn’t required. Now, the Georgia Child Support Worksheet automatically adjusts the obligation based on the number of overnights. This ensures that the parent providing direct care and housing for a significant portion of the month is not unfairly burdened.

Calculating “Income Shares”

Georgia uses the “Income Shares” model. This means the court looks at the combined adjusted gross income of both parents.

1. Combined Income: Calculate the total monthly income of both parties.

2. Basic Obligation: Match that total to the 2026 Georgia Basic Child Support Obligation table.

3. Pro Rata Share: If you earn 60% of the total income, you are responsible for 60% of the basic obligation, adjusted for health insurance premiums and work-related childcare costs.

According to 2025 census data for Carroll County, the median household income has risen, making these new modernized tables essential for fair rulings.

[IMAGE: A screenshot of the 2026 Georgia Online Child Support Calculator interface.]

Navigating the Carroll County Superior Court Process

Filing for divorce in Carrollton is a localized experience. Your case will likely be heard at the Carroll County Courthouse on Newnan Street. Understanding the “home field” rules can save you months of delays.

The Standing Order and Domestic Seminars

The moment a divorce is filed in Carroll County, a Standing Order goes into effect. This legally prevents either parent from moving the children out of state or dissipating marital assets. Furthermore, Carrollton judges require all divorcing parents to attend a “Seminar for Divorcing Parents.” You cannot get a final decree without a certificate of completion from this class.

Advanced Insights: Avoiding Common Mistakes

Whether it is another driver in a car accident, a business improperly maintaining their store, or a company producing a faulty product, injured people have the right to seek fair compensation. This compensation can take the form of medical bills, lost wages, and mental anguish, to name just a few.

However, the exact mechanisms are more complicated. A plaintiff must demonstrate that there was a duty placed upon the defendant to care for the plaintiff�s well-being.

If the plaintiff can prove that the defendant failed in this duty, and that the plaintiff was injured as a result, they may collect damages. This legal outline of negligence is by far the most common avenue through which injured people claim compensation.

Whether the injuries occurred as a result of a car accident, a slip and fall, or premises liability, Georgia law has created a statute of limitations within which a plaintiff must file their case.

According to GA Code, plaintiffs have only two years from the date of the accident to open a case in court. Time is of the essence here. Insurance companies are well aware of this rule and will refuse to negotiate with plaintiffs and their attorneys if the time limit has passed.

Individuals should give themselves the best chance of success and contact the Clayton County personal injury attorneys today.

All legal cases, especially those centered on personal injury, rely on documentary evidence. It is one thing to state the extent of someone’s injuries, but it is quite another to have a doctor�s opinion backing them up. These are three steps that a potential plaintiff can take to help document their case.

- Obtain consistent medical treatment: Not only is this necessary for individuals to make a full recovery, the attending physician�s notes will detail the extent of the injury and may even ascribe fault to the defendant
- Obtain a police report for any incident to which they responded: The police are required to file an official report for all incidents involving personal harm or property damage. Since this is viewed by juries as an independent statement of the facts of a case, this is a key piece of evidence for Clayton County injury lawyers
- Keep all correspondence. In cases where someone becomes injured in their rented home, there may be records of correspondence between them and the property owner. Text messages or emails outlining their requests for repairs can demonstrate that the property owner knew of a hazardous condition and did nothing to fix it

Whether you were injured in a car accident, as a customer, or while on another�s property, Clayton County personal injury lawyers are avilable to help you fight for the fair compensation that you deserve.

Under �93-3-33 of the Georgia Code, the injured victim in a car accident can file a lawsuit against a negligent or careless driver, provided they do so within two years of the date of the accident. Unlike many other states, Georgia does not place any limit on the number of damages a car accident victim can recover in a car accident lawsuit.

The types of damages that can be recovered under Georgia law include both economic damages and non-economic damages. Economic damages are damages that are easily quantifiable, such as a hospital bill or missed work because of the car accident. Non-economic damages are less easily measured and can include monetary awards for pain and suffering, or punitive damages meant to punish the driver who caused the car accident. A Clayton County car accident lawyer may be able to work with a victim to recover these damages.

If a car accident in Clayton County results from a manufacturing defect, then the victim may seek to recover their damages through a claim with the manufacturer, which Georgia Code �51-1-11.1 grants them the right to do. Unlike a negligence action, a products liability claim is a strict liability offense, which means that the intent or potentially negligent actions of the automobile manufacturer are irrelevant.

The most common vehicle defects in Clayton County are design defects, where the car was designed in an unnecessarily unsafe manner, and manufacturing defects, where the car was manufactured in a way that made it unsafe for the driver or other drivers on the road.

pages.content_md:
Suffering from a burn injury may lead to emotional and physical injuries. Burn injury plaintiffs might not only face the results of the burn�and may also experience potential complications resulting from the burn such as infection and disfigurement. A Clayton County burn injury lawyer understands the challenges burn injury plaintiffs and their families face.

A compassionate catastrophic injury attorney also understands what it takes to stand up to the parties at-fault for those injuries. An attorney could provide legal assistance to help you receive the compensation you deserve.

People typically think of burns as resulting from fires and hot surfaces. While these two factors may lead to burns, there could be a number of potential causes, which may include:

- Fire
- Hot liquids
- Chemicals
- Explosions
- Motor vehicle accidents
- Electrical burns

Whenever another party is responsible for the resulting injuries, they may be held liable. This could be true whether it is a driver who caused a crash or a restaurant who overheated a beverage. A�Clayton County burn injury lawyer may be experienced in pursuing claims for burn injuries which were caused by a variety of factors.

Burn injuries are typically categorized as first, second, or third-degree burns. While the process of healing any type of burn injury is typically painful, some are less critical than others.

First-degree burns are less serious than either second of third-degree burns. The damage caused by a first-degree burn is limited to the first layer of skin and may be healed in roughly a week.

Second-degree burns are more serious than minor inflammation. The damage caused by second-degree burns could extend below the top layer of skin and typically causes blistering. It may take several months for a second-degree burn to heal.

Third-degree burns are the most serious categorization of burns. These burns penetrate all layers of the skin and could extend further to the person�s organs. The risk of death is highest for plaintiffs with third-degree burns and these burns also may require skin grafts and put the person at a higher risk of infection.

Matters involving burn injuries typically fall into the category of negligence. The laws governing negligence in Clayton County allow injured parties to seek recovery against the at-fault party. The injured party must establish liability under negligence law to show that they are entitled to receive damages.

The party who sustained the burn must show that the party or parties who inflicted the burn owed a reasonable duty of care. If the injured party is able to prove that the burn occurred because that duty was breached and resulted in their injuries, the defendant could be liable for damages.

In Clayton County, plaintiffs of burn injuries only have two years from the date of the injury to file their claim. This is a relatively short amount of time, and may notably be true when individuals spend a large portion of that time recovering.

The statute of limitations is strict and failing to comply with the applicable deadlines may cause an individual to lose their right to file a claim and collect damages. Contacting a Clayton County burn injury lawyer immediately after suffering a burn injury may be the best way to ensure that the right to bring a claim is preserved.

Clayton County burn injury lawyers have been fighting for the rights of burn plaintiffs for several years. If you or someone close to you has suffered from a burn injury, they may be able to help you.

An attorney could help with every aspect of your case by gathering and analyzing medical evidence, interviewing witnesses, negotiating with defendants, filing lawsuits, and ensuring all deadlines are met. To starting working with a burn injury attorney in Clayton County, call now.

Symptoms of traumatic brain injuries may include dizziness, blurred vision, slurred speech, confusion, loss of consciousness, or bleeding. Medical testing and evaluations such as MRI�s, CT scans, or X-Rays may be necessary to identify and diagnose traumatic brain injuries. Individuals who suffered a hit to the head should seek medical attention to determine the extent of their injuries.

Anyone who has experienced a traumatic brain injury will likely face physical and cognitive challenges. Seizures, trouble concentrating, loss of muscle control, headaches, insomnia, mood swings and loss of memory are commonly experienced by traumatic brain injury victims. The recovery process for traumatic brain injuries can be lengthy. However, in many cases, even with therapy, surgery, and rehabilitation, victims are not able to fully recover.

If a negligent party is responsible for inflicting a traumatic brain injury, the injured party may be entitled to compensation. To determine whether another entity or person could be considered responsible, it may be beneficial to consult a Clayton County traumatic brain injury attorney.

The amount of damages a traumatic brain injury victim is awarded will vary depending on the nature of the injury and the facts of the case. Typically, damages will be paid out by an insurance company in a settlement or by the defendants in a personal injury lawsuit. These damages will usually cover expenses such as past and future medical costs.

If the brain injury has left the person unable to work, damages for lost wages may also be available. In addition to compensation for economic losses, the person may also be able to collect compensation for non-economic losses as well. This can include compensation for pain and suffering, mental anguish, and loss of consortium.

If you suffered a traumatic brain injury, you may be entitled to receive substantial compensation from the parties responsible for causing your injury. A Clayton County traumatic brain injury lawyer is here to help review the merits of your case and provide you with advice about how to proceed. If you would like to schedule a complimentary initial consultation, call today.

pages.title: Clayton County Dangerous Drugs Lawyer | Hazardous Medication
pages.description: A dedicated Clayton County dangerous drugs lawyer could fight for your right to compensation if your medication caused you an injury or illness.
pages.content_md:
The pharmaceutical company is a multibillion-dollar industry, premised on the concept that prescription drugs and medications are supposed to help heal injuries, cure infections, and prevent and stop diseases from spreading. However, sometimes, they allow dangerous drugs to be distributed to patients. These drugs can cause serious, long-lasting injuries.

If a defective and dangerous drug has caused your injury, you have a legal basis for recovering compensation for your injuries and losses. Large pharmaceutical companies make billions of dollars every year and when their products cause harm and injury, they should be held accountable.

A Clayton County dangerous drug lawyer could help explain your rights. By working together, a skilled personal injury attorney could help you hold these large companies responsible for their carelessness.

Pharmaceutical companies have a legal obligation to ensure that their products are safe for consumers. The U.S Food and Drug Administration is responsible for regulating and establishing testing standards before placing pharmaceuticals on the market.

However, despite the utility and rigorous testing pharmaceutical companies are required to undergo, thousands of people are injured every year by dangerous drugs because of a defect in the drugs chemical design, a lack of testing, or because of a lack of proper warnings.

Distinguishing between a useful medication and a dangerous drug is not always clear. Pharmaceutical companies such as Merck, Pfizer, and GlaxoSmithKline are all required to conduct extensive testing and regulation by the U.S Food and Drug Administration. In addition, these companies often engage in extensive testing prior to applying to the U.S Food and Drug Administration.

However, because of the pressure to develop and produce new medications, this may mean that a pharmaceutical company does not take the time to fully understand the dangers of their product. Therefore, a medication may be considered a dangerous drug when its risks and hazards outweigh its potential benefits. For more information, consult with a knowledgeable lawyer.

Pharmaceutical companies have a duty and obligation to ensure that their products and drugs are safe for use. If a drug causes an injury the pharmaceutical company may be held liable under a theory of product liability.

Georgia�s product liability statute codified in O.C.G.A � 51-1-11(b)(1) provides that the manufacturer of a dangerous drug can be held �liable in tort, irrespective of privity, to any natural person who may use, consume, or reasonably be affected by the property.� A Clayton County dangerous drugs attorney could help determine whether a drug company may be liable for specific injuries.

When an individual asserts that a dangerous drug has injured them, they often are asserting that a drug was �not merchantable and reasonably suited to the use intended� O.C.G.A �51-1-11(b)(1). To prove that a product was not merchantable, a person will typically be required to demonstrate:

- A defective condition caused an injury
- The product was in the same condition when it caused the injury it was in when it left the manufacturer
- The product was being used as the manufacturer intended

Large pharmaceutical companies will often try and negate any one of these elements to shift liability away from themselves and onto the injured person. It is a common defense for pharmaceutical companies to allege that a person altered a drug, or that a person was not using the drug as it was intended. A Clayton County dangerous drugs lawyer could help fight these allegations.

If a dangerous drug has caused you to suffer an injury, contact an experienced Clayton County dangerous drug lawyer. By conducting a thorough review of your case, a dangerous drug attorney could advise you on your legal options and help you pursue compensation for your injuries and losses. Call today to learn more.

pages.title: Clayton County Defective Products Lawyer | Hazardous Products
pages.description: A skilled and dedicated Clayton County defective products lawyer could fight for your right to compensation. Call today to set up a consultation.
pages.content_md:
Companies and manufacturers have a simple obligation to ensure that their product is both useful and safe. However, reports by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), indicate that manufacturers are not as cautious as they should be and defective products may cause millions of accidents and injuries every year.

While the law may provide a means of holding manufacturers accountable, products liability cases can be incredibly complicated. Therefore, you should seek the guidance of a Clayton County defective product lawyer.

One of the biggest challenges that individuals face in a products liability case is fighting with large companies with high-powered lawyers who are eager to dismiss a claim. A seasoned personal injury attorney could work to ensure your injury and claim is given the attention it deserves.

When companies fail to warn consumers of the risks of their products, they can be held liable for any resulting injuries through filing a lawsuit. Georgia law specifically provides that manufacturers can be held liable for any resulting injuries when a product is not considered �merchantable and reasonably suited to the use intended� O.C.G.A. �51-1-11(b)(1). Products liability cases include any manufactured product including medications, medical devices, cars, tools, electronics, and household appliances.

In any products liability case, the plaintiff has the burden of proving: (1) that the product was defective, (2) their injury, (3) the causal connection between the defect and the injury, and (4) that the defendant was responsible for the defect. Products Liability, Second Edition, Madden, �12.1, p. 487

An injured individual could pursue a claim based under one or more of the following theories.

Negligence serves as the foundation for products liability cases. For an individual to win a case premised on negligence they would have to prove four elements: duty, breach, causation, and damages. When a court is trying to determine whether a product is defective, they will often rely on these four elements as a framework and seek to determine whether the product is not considered merchantable and reasonably suited for its intended use. A dedicated Clayton County dangerous drugs attorney could help an injured individual prove negligence.

Under Georgia law O.C.G.A. �51-1-11(b)(1), a manufacturer is strictly liable when they put an item on the market without inspecting it for a defect and knowing the consumer will not inspect it for a defect. This means that, regardless of a person�s actions, if a company has placed a product on the market that has a defect, they can be held liable.

A breach of warranty occurs when the manufacturer makes an assertion about a product. If the product then does not meet expectations, the manufacturer can be held liable.

There is a vast array of products that can cause an injury, and some of the most common products involved in defective product litigation in Clayton County include:

- Pharmaceuticals
- Motor vehicles
- Machinery and construction materials
- Medical devices
- Electrical devices
- Household appliances

Defective product lawsuits tend to entail complex litigation often-requiring an understanding of a product and the ability to explain both the product�s utility and its flaw in a court. That is why it may be important to work with an experienced Clayton County defective products lawyer.

While people rely on products to help with daily tasks, when a defective product causes an injury, you may be entitled to compensation for your injuries and losses. A Clayton County defective product lawyer could help guide you through the complex process of proving liability in a defective product case. To find out how an attorney could help you, call today to set up a consultation.

pages.title: Clayton County Medical Malpractice Lawyer | Hospital Error
pages.description: If you or a loved one suffered an injury due to the negligence of a medical professional, contact a Clayton County medical malpractice lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
The vast majority of medical professionals may be honest people who work hard to provide sick and injured patients with the best care possible. Unfortunately, accidents and medical errors do happen, and some of them happen may be due to negligence or carelessness by doctors, nurses, and hospital staff.

Medical malpractice may occur when a healthcare provider does not behave in the manner of a qualified doctor in their position should, which may lead to serious harm to a patient. If you believe you were hurt by a negligent medical mistake, you could have grounds for a medical malpractice suit, and a Clayton County medical malpractice lawyer may be able to help you with your case. Contact a seasoned personal injury attorney today to get started on your claim.

Accidents happen, even in the medical industry, but doctors and other medical professionals spend years in school learning how to reduce the likelihood of errors. Despite this, medical professionals could sometimes make avoidable mistakes, or they may fail to act in the best interests of their patients.

Medical malpractice cases may often stem from the following types of errors:

- Misdiagnosis or failure to diagnose a condition
- Prescribing the wrong medication or treatment
- Mistakes during childbirth
- Mistakes during surgery
- Intentional neglect or abuse

In a nutshell, medical malpractice claims could be filed in cases where medical professionals dramatically veer away from normal medical routine due to negligence or carelessness. If a medication causes an illness or injury, patients may be able to take action against the company that made the drug as well. Likewise, patients who are harmed by medical devices may also need to take action against the maker of the device.

Hospitals may be obligated to provide patients with a safe and clean environment and may ensure they hire only qualified physicians, nurses, and other medical staff members. They may be legally be required to keep track of the actions of their staff members and perform thorough background checks to make sure the people they hire are properly licensed and qualified to do the job they are hired for.

Hospitals may also be required to hire enough staff members for all their patients to receive the care they need. If a hospital does not take these basic steps and a patient gets hurt as a result, the hospital management and administration could be held responsible in civil court.

In some medical malpractice lawsuits, hospitals could be held liable both directly and indirectly. A hospital could be held liable indirectly�or �vicariously��if a staff member commits an act of malpractice and the hospital management was responsible for that staff member�s actions while at work. A Clayton County medical malpractice attorney could provide more information about hospitals and individual doctors who may be held liable for malpractice.

Medical malpractice cases could be complicated, and more than likely patients may need help from a medical malpractice lawyer in Clayton County if they intend to file a claim. For instance, to prove a medical professional is guilty of malpractice, attorneys may need to have other medical professionals with a similar professional background confirm in court that the doctor who treated the injured individual was in the wrong.

The court may also consider if the patient was fully aware of all potential outcomes and side effects before they were treated. If a patient can establish their case in court, they may be entitled to receive money to compensate for their pain and suffering.

If you are in the process of recovering from an avoidable medical mistake, you may be feeling tired and overwhelmed. This is normal, but you should not have to suffer because a medical professional or hospital failed to take basic steps to ensure your safety and well-being. Reach out to an experienced Clayton County medical malpractice lawyer now if you are ready to fight for your rights.

pages.title: Clayton County Birth Injury Lawyer | Medical Mistakes During Delivery
pages.description: Speak to a Clayton County birth injury lawyer if your infant was hurt by the actions of a hospital or medical professional.
pages.content_md:
A birth injury typically occurs during labor and delivery. It may also occur either prior to or immediately after birth. When these injuries occur, they may permanently affect the newborn and their family. While some of these injuries are unforeseen and unavoidable, others could be the result of the negligence of the doctor or nurse. If your child was hurt due to the negligence of a doctor or nurse, your family may have rights.

A Clayton county birth injury lawyer understands the impact a birth injury could have on you and your child and is committed to advocating for you. By working closely with medical professionals, a practiced medical malpractice attorney could help build a comprehensive case to get the justice you deserve.

Pregnancy and delivery may be incredibly complicated for both mother and baby. While injuries could occur naturally due to the delivery process, there may be certain birth injuries that are commonly associated with medical malpractice. An experienced Clayton County birth injury lawyer could help parents identify which birth injury their child suffered.

Consisting of a group of nerves in the arms and hands, a brachial plexus injury might result in a baby being unable to flex and rotate their arms.� Typically, this type of injury is the result of using too much force during delivery.

Cerebral palsy is characterized by a marked loss in motor function. Cerebral palsy is commonly caused by a brain injury sustained while the baby�s brain is developing. These injuries may be the result of oxygen deprivation or infections.

This condition occurs when a newborn has been deprived of sufficient oxygen during the birth process. This condition could result in significant brain damage that may subsequently affect a child�s ability to properly grow and develop.

Medical professionals have a duty to provide mothers and their newborns with adequate medical care.� O.C.G.A. � 51-1-27. This requires medical professionals to carefully assess both mother and baby to look for signs of distress. When they miss signs of distress or if they fail to meet medical standards, it could result in an infant suffering. A birth injury may result in lifelong injuries and complications, or even death.

A birth injury may be devastating for a family to cope with and to understand. Once a birth injury occurs it could be important to move quickly. Under O.C.G.A. �9-3-71, a birth injury lawsuit premised on medical malpractice must be filed within two years after the date on which an injury or death arose. Parents could speak to a birth injury lawyer in Clayton County immediately.

Birth injury lawsuits may become quite complex. There could be multiple medical professionals who all exercise some judgment and control over a newborn prior to, during, and after the delivery process.

Parents may also find themselves facing significant emotional challenges. A Clayton County birth injury lawyer could provide critical guidance and support during a birth injury lawsuit.

By conducting a thorough review of a case, a birth injury attorney could help outline the course of litigation and lead negotiations with insurance companies and providers. If your child has suffered a birth injury, call today.

pages.title: Clayton County Motorcycle Accident Lawyer | Motorbike Crash
pages.description: If you were injured in a motorcycle accident, you could pursue damages for your injuries. Call a Clayton County motorcycle accident lawyer to learn more.
pages.content_md:
Many Clayton County personal injury attorneys have experience handling car accident cases, but motorcycle accidents are unique. Injuries are often more severe, and the types of incidents that can cause a motorcycle accident often differ from those associated with car wrecks. For instance, a road hazard that might pose little threat to someone in a car or truck could cause a motorcycle crash with disastrous results.

If you were involved in a motorcycle collision, it may be wise to work with an experienced Clayton County motorcycle accident lawyer who understands what makes motorcycle cases different. A knowledgeable personal injury attorney could use their expertise to help you pursue the compensation to which you may be entitled.

As with most cases where an injured party seeks to recover compensation due to another’s negligence, Georgia laws limit the length of time the victim of a motorcycle wreck has to file a lawsuit. In most cases, the limit is two years from the time of the accident, even if the injuries are not fully apparent until much later.

In some situations, particularly those involving a government entity, the time limit is even shorter. Due to these limitations, taking quick action with a Clayton County motorcycle crash attorney often helps to ensure the greatest amount of evidence can be located and preserved, even if the injured party technically has the full two years to file a claim.

Motorcycle accidents frequently result in serious injuries such as broken bones, organ and tissue damage, head trauma, and spinal injuries. Those injured are often forced to miss work, incur large medical bills, and deal with continuing effects which reduce earning potential or require long-term care.

If another party�s negligence caused a motorcycle accident, the injured party may be entitled to monetary damages. These damages may cover injuries and losses such as:

- Past medical bills
- Future medical needs, including equipment, therapy, and long-term treatment
- Lost wages
- Reduced income in the future
- Emotional distress
- Pain and Suffering

A Clayton County motorcycle accident lawyer with experience handling motorcycle accident cases could help determine future needs and expenses to accurately evaluate the fairness of any potential settlement offers.

Proving liability in a motorcycle accident can be different when only one vehicle is involved compared to situations involving collisions between two or more vehicles. When multiple vehicles are involved, a case usually involves demonstrating that another driver failed to exercise proper care when operating on the road, and that this negligence caused the accident.

When the only vehicle involved in the accident is the motorcycle, though, it generally falls to the plaintiff to prove that an outside condition caused the accident, such as debris off another vehicle or a dangerous condition along the road�s surface. If a passenger on a motorcycle suffers injury, the passenger may have a separate claim from the driver of the motorcycle.

If you were involved in a motorcycle accident, there are many potential benefits to working with an experienced Clayton County motorcycle accident lawyer. In addition to evaluating your claim, an experienced attorney could advocate on your behalf and help you obtain the full compensation to which you may be entitled. Call today for a free consultation.

pages.title: Clayton County Nursing Home Abuse Lawyer | Elderly Abuse
pages.description: If you or a loved one have been victimized while living in a nursing home, consult a Clayton County nursing home abuse lawyer that can help.
pages.h1: Clayton County Nursing Home Abuse Lawyer
pages.content_md:
More than three million aging persons reside in nursing home facilities in the United States, and that number continues to increase as the baby boomer generation ages. Many families wish they could care for their loved one at home, but due to the level of care or expertise required it may simply not be possible.

Because families go to such great lengths to find the perfect nursing home facility, it can be an especially terrible betrayal if they discover nursing home abuse has occurred there. If your loved one has been abused or neglected in a nursing home facility in Georgia, a Clayton County nursing home abuse lawyer could help you seek reparation through the civil court system. Consult a passionate and determined personal injury attorney and know that you are in good hands.

Nursing home facilities have a duty to their residents to maintain an adequate standard of care. They are responsible for inspecting their facility for safety hazards, ensuring adequate medical care, and conducting adequate screening of their staff members.

In many instances where nursing home abuse is uncovered, the abusive staff member turns out to have a criminal background, inadequate or fraudulent experience, or is poorly trained, overworked, or given too much responsibility.

Courts consider these factors when determining the degree to which a nursing home facility is liable for abuse of a nursing home resident. As part of the litigation process, a knowledgeable Clayton County nursing home abuse lawyer may investigate a nursing home’s practices and the backgrounds of its staff members.

There are numerous signs and symptoms of nursing home abuse that family members should be aware of, in case they notice alarming, or subtle, changes in their loved one. Some of the most common signs and symptoms include but are not limited to:

- Bruises, contusions, finger marks, or scratches in unusual places
- Anger, depression, anxiety, fear, or self-harm
- Rapidly declining health
- Bedsores, infections, untreated medical issues, and sexually transmitted diseases
- Inappropriate isolation, restraint, or lack of access to the outside world
- Fear of particular staff members

Additionally, it is important to take a resident’s concerns and reports seriously. Even if the resident is experiencing dementia or their reports and stories do not make sense, it is still important to investigate whether some form of nursing home abuse or neglect has taken place.

Nursing home facilities should not be allowed to prey on the vulnerabilities of aging seniors and their families, and it is important that they are held accountable for abuse and neglect of the residents entrusted to their care. While initiating a personal injury claim can be intimidating, it can also be empowering to work towards preventing or deterring future abuse of residents, thereby sparing other families similar pain.

Working with an experienced nursing home abuse attorney can give family members peace of mind throughout the legal process. No matter the circumstances surrounding your loved one’s abuse, or whether you are even certain abuse has taken place, consider working with an experienced Clayton County nursing home abuse lawyer who can investigate and find out what, if anything, has occurred.

pages.title: Clayton County Pedestrian Accident Lawyer | Human-Automobile Collision
pages.description: If you were hit by a car, you may be able to hold the driver liable for damages. Talk to a Clayton County pedestrian accident lawyer about your options.
pages.content_md:
Accidents involving pedestrians are a source of some of the most serious personal injuries in Clayton County. When a car, truck, or bus collides with an unprotected individual who is walking on a sidewalk, waiting to cross a street, or exiting a vehicle, the results can be disastrous.

Even a strike from a non-motorized vehicle such as a bicycle can cause serious injuries, and the full consequences of those injuries may not be apparent until well after the accident. Fortunately, an experienced personal injury attorney should be able to help you take stock of your damages and seek monetary recovery for them.

If you or a loved one sustained injuries as a pedestrian, it is important to seek proper medical care first. After that, you should consult a Clayton County pedestrian accident lawyer to find out whether you could be entitled to compensation for medical bills, pain and suffering, and other consequences of your wreck.

Many different types of injuries could result from a pedestrian accident, including emotional trauma, spinal injury, or even death. These injuries can often cause victims to incur significant medical expenses or require long-term and future treatments.

A knowledgeable Clayton County pedestrian accident lawyer could help you calculate future expenses, including costs such as modifications needed to the home, assistance with daily activities, lost future income and earning potential, and more. Some of the compensable injuries that may result from pedestrian accidents in Clayton County include:

- Spinal injuries
- Internal organ damage
- Broken bones
- Traumatic brain injuries
- Head and neck injuries

In addition to expenses such as medical fees and equipment, an injured pedestrian may be entitled to compensation for the non-tangible results of the accident, such as pain and suffering, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life.

In many pedestrian accident cases, the party allegedly at fault may argue that the victim�s own conduct was to blame for the accident. For instance, in a crash involving a pedestrian who was crossing the street, the driver of the car might insist that the pedestrian was not in the crosswalk or crossing against traffic. Very often, more than one action contributes to an accident.

If the court concludes that a pedestrian’s negligence did contribute to an accident, that pedestrian would not be barred from recovering compensation as long as they are less than 50 percent responsible for the crash. However, the amount of money they ultimately receive would be reduced relative to the amount of comparative negligence the court assigned to them.

Therefore, if a motorist was considered 80 percent at fault for an accident and the pedestrian was considered 20 percent at fault, the pedestrian�s final damage award would be reduced by 20 percent. If the pedestrian is found more than 50 percent at fault for the accident, they would not be entitled to recover compensation under Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33.

If you suffered serious injury in a pedestrian accident, your first priority should be making a full recovery. However, the stress that medical bills, insurance claims, and providing statements to lawyers and law enforcement can produce may make the healing process difficult, to say the least.

A dedicated Clayton County pedestrian accident lawyer could answer questions and handle paperwork on your behalf, so that you can focus on what matters most during a difficult situation. To learn how a compassionate attorney could help, call today to schedule a consultation.

pages.title: Clayton County Premises Liability Lawyer | Hazardous Properties
pages.description: If you were injured due to a hazard on someone else's property, speak with a Clayton County premises liability lawyer about your situation.
pages.content_md:
Individuals are entitled to live and work within safe spaces, and premises liability is a concept that can hold property owners responsible for injuries or death suffered by those on the property. In Clayton County, premises liability claims can be made against a landlord, property manager, homeowner, or business that neglects to maintain the property it controls or owns in a reasonably safe manner for those invited onto the premises.

If you were harmed while on the property of another, it may be important for you to contact a Clayton County premises liability lawyer. An experienced personal injury attorney could work to address damages, protect your rights, and pursue a positive outcome on your behalf.

When someone suffers injury due to dangerous conditions that were improperly addressed by the property owner, Georgia law allows the harmed person to file a tort lawsuit for premise liability. If the injury causes death, a lawsuit may be brought on behalf of family members.

By establishing liability, the injured party could be entitled to receive monetary compensation known as �damages�. These damages may provide relief for economic harm related to the incident, such as medical bills, therapy, or time lost from work. Damages for intangible�or �non-economic��harm such as emotional distress or loss of enjoyment could also be awarded.

Premises liability cases can potentially involve a wide variety of circumstances, not all of which are accidental in nature. If someone is harmed by a criminal act and the property manager or owner failed to provide adequate security, they could be held liable for their negligence in civil court by a Clayton County premises liability lawyer.

Other situations for which a property owner or manager could potentially be liable include:

- Dog attacks
- Slips and falls
- Elevator malfunction or unmaintained escalators
- Fire code violations and inadequate smoke detectors
- Falling merchandise in a store
- Water-borne injury and illness

If it is found that a property manager was�or reasonably should have been�aware of a dangerous condition and failed to take adequate measures to address the problem, their negligence could be grounds for an injured victim to seek a settlement from them or file a lawsuit. Those suffering due to the negligence of a property manager may be entitled to recover damages under the premise liability theory.

Clayton County follows the modified comparative negligence rule enumerated in Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33. This statute specifies that if someone seeking recovery for injuries is found to be partially responsible for their damages, the court should “determine the percentage of fault” of the party seeking damages and decrease their damage award by that percentage.

For example, if a falling display of canned peas in a grocery store injured a shopper, that shopper could seek damages under premise liability law. However, the court might find that the shopper is ten percent responsible for their injury because they were reading a label while walking and brushed against the shelf. Accordingly, their final damage award would be reduced by ten percent.

If the party seeking to recover is found to be 50 percent or more at fault, they would be ineligible to recover any damages. A premises liability lawyer in Clayton County could work on a potential plaintiff�s behalf to contest any counterclaims a defendant makes that try to shift liability onto the plaintiff.

Certain courts approach premises liability cases differently than others, and premises liability can be defined somewhat broadly depending on the situation. Therefore, it is usually a good idea to work with an experienced Clayton County premises liability lawyer who could help you understand premise liability and comparative negligence, and who knows the best approach to take in local courts. Call today to schedule an initial consultation and start exploring what may be possible in your case.

pages.title: Clayton County Sexual Abuse Lawyer | Sexual Battery Claim in Civil Court
pages.description: Work with a compassionate Clayton County sexual abuse lawyer that could help hold your abuser accountable and fight for you.
pages.content_md:
Sexual abuse in Clayton County could incorporate a variety of offenses, which may include assault, battery, rape, child molestation, and improper touching. Many cases of sexual abuse involve a person in a position of power who takes advantage of a subordinate, or someone who is younger than themselves.

While sexual abuse can be charged as a criminal offense, the criminal system may not properly compensate those who suffered because of sexual abuse. Under the civil system, you may be able to recover compensation for both your physical injuries and the emotional injuries that are often associated with sexual abuse.

An experienced Clayton County sexual abuse lawyer understands the highly personal aspects of these cases as well as the legal nuances. A compassionate injury attorney is prepared to address your questions and help you through this challenging process.

It is critical to understand the difference between the criminal system and the civil justice system in a sexual abuse case. In a criminal case, ultimately the state is prosecuting an individual for committing a crime under Title 16, Chapter Six of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated. These offenses may include:

- Rape
- Child molestation
- Sexual battery
- Sexual assault

Typically, the goal of criminal prosecution is to protect the community as a whole as well as to punish an individual with imprisonment and fines to deter them from committing future crimes. Under the civil system, a person is filing a lawsuit to protect their own personal rights.

There are many differences between the criminal and civil system. It could be important to understand that a civil lawsuit can permit someone to recover compensation for their physical and emotional injuries.

In a criminal case, the prosecution must prove their case beyond a reasonable doubt, which may be an incredibly difficult standard to meet. In a civil sexual abuse case, they must prove their case by a preponderance of the evidence. O.C.G.A � 24-14-4.

To prove a case by this standard, a jury must be presented with sufficient evidence to rule in the plaintiff�s favor. This may not mean that whoever has the most evidence will win; The side that presents the most compelling evidence would typically have an advantage.

When investigating a sexual abuse case, a Clayton County sexual abuse lawyer may consider many factors. They may be able to do this by collecting information by gathering and assessing medical records and reports, witness testimony, and personal testimony by both the claimant and their alleged abuser.

A person who has suffered from sexual abuse may choose to file a civil lawsuit to recover compensation for economic injuries. This could include medical expenses, lost wages, and any other resulting costs such as the cost to move to a different house or area, if applicable.

These expenses could be minimal compared to the emotional injuries associated with sexual abuse. A person may pursue compensation for their emotional injuries, counseling, and pain and suffering with the help of an attorney.

Sexual abuse cases could be incredibly complex and are highly sensitive. A Clayton County sexual abuse lawyer may understand that these cases need to be approached with a degree of sensitivity and could help sexual abuse claimants hold those responsible accountable for their actions. If you have been sexually abused, a dedicated attorney is prepared to meet with you and discuss your case. They may be able to help you pursue the justice you deserve.

pages.title: Clayton County Slip and Fall Lawyer | Trip and Fall Accidents
pages.description: If you have been injured in a slip and fall accident, reach out to a seasoned and dedicated Clayton County slip and fall lawyer today.
pages.h1: Clayton County Slip and Fall Lawyer
pages.content_md:
Have you been hurt in a slip and fall accident? Did the accident occur on property owned by someone else? If you answered yes to both these questions, you may be able to file a personal injury claim with the help of a Clayton County slip and fall lawyer.

Injuries resulting from a serious fall could be surprisingly serious, and without the responsible party providing compensation, you could be held accountable for your own medical expenses even though your injury was not your fault. If you are currently recovering from such an injury, a skilled personal injury attorney may be able to help you obtain the financial recovery you need to move on with your life and provide for your family.

Property owners have a responsibility to ensure their land is safe for visitors, guests, customers, and anyone else who might be on it. This may involve removing dangerous hazards and warning visitors of any hazards that they know about but have not been able to take care of yet. If a property owner fails to do this, they could be held liable in court if a guest or visitor slips, falls, and gets hurt. Slips and fall accidents are caused by a variety of factors, but the following are some of the most common may include icy parking lots and sidewalks, unmarked spills, and broken or uneven flooring.

Bad lighting also could be a major problem in offices and apartment buildings, primarily because these buildings could have multiple steep staircases. Accidents in restaurants and retail stores, meanwhile, may be caused more by spills and slippery floors. If an employee notices a spill, they should either clean the area or seal it off until it can be properly cleaned, or they could open themselves or the property�s owner or manager up to a lawsuit.

Falls often occur in a work environment, particularly in the manufacturing and construction industries. Many of these falls are may be�covered by workers� compensation insurance, but injured employees may be able to sue other parties in certain cases. Non-employers, such as vendors, equipment manufacturers, and subcontractors may be held liable if their actions result in or contribute to an accident.

If this occurs, an injured worker may need to call upon a Clayton County slip and fall attorney if they want to receive payment for their damages. Large companies are usually represented by insurance companies that hire their own lawyers. Taking on these insurance companies alone could be difficult, but with help from a skilled lawyer, injured workers might even the playing field and obtain the compensation they deserve.

By taking legal action with help from a slip and fall lawyer in Clayton County, injured people could hold the party responsible for their fall accountable and could make them cover the costs of their injuries and losses. Slips and falls could cause serious injuries, especially to older people and people who are in poor health. While the SSDI system may be in place to provide individuals and their families with benefits and compensation up to $1,197 per month, a substantial percentage of applications are typically denied. The Social Security Administration�has found that of all people who applied, only 35 to 40 percent were approved and were granted disability benefits. To qualify for Social Security disability benefits, a person must meet certain criteria. The criteria for determining whether a person qualifies for SSDI may be incredibly complex and confusing. An adult must have a physical or mental impairment that condition prevents them from obtaining any substantial gainful employment and is expected to last for a period of at least 12 months to qualify.

An attorney could help you through the review and appeal process in the event you are denied benefits. Call today to get the help you need.

The Workers� Compensation Act includes broad coverage for employees who are injured in the workplace. Under the workers� compensation system, employees are entitled to certain benefits for injuries occur during the course of their employment. The workers� compensation system could cover traumatic injuries that may include falls and injuries that occur over time that may include carpal tunnel. O.C.G.A. � 34-9-1(4).

The workers� compensation laws also provide employees with certain rights and impose�certain obligations on employers that may include:

- The right to choose a doctor � Employers are required to post a list of at least six doctors that an employee may choose from
- Medical benefits � A worker who is injured on the job is entitled to certain benefits covering medical expenses, doctors� bills, prescription costs, and rehabilitation costs
- Weekly income benefits � A worker who is injured and unable to work for more than seven days is entitled to weekly income benefits
- Death benefits � In the event that a worker dies as a result of a workplace injury their dependents are entitled to receive burial expenses up to $7,500 and up to two-thirds of an employee’s average weekly salary up to $575 per week

An injured worker could consult a�Clayton County lawyer to learn what�worker’s compensation rights they may have.

While the workers� compensation act covers almost all work-related injuries there are some notable exceptions and exclusions. These may include:

Certain medical conditions are all also typically excluded from the definition of an injury.�These may include heart disease, heart attack, failure or occlusion of any coronary blood vessel, stroke, and thrombosis.

pages.content_md:
The death of a loved one can be incredibly traumatic if it happens suddenly or due to the negligence of another person or company. If you believe the death of your family member was caused by the careless or reckless behavior of another person, you may be able to hold them liable to some extent through a wrongful death lawsuit.

With help from a seasoned Clayton County wrongful death lawyer, you may be able to receive monetary compensation for some of your losses and damages related to your loved one�s death.�Filing a wrongful death claim could be difficult, but a dedicated personal injury attorney�may be able to help.

A variety of circumstances can serve as reasons to file a wrongful death claim. In Georgia, wrongful death claims may only be brought forth by �representatives of the estate,� who would be�in order of priority�spouses, children, or parents of the individual who died. If the claim is successful, whoever filed the claim could receive payments from the responsible party to cover costs and losses associated with their family member�s death.

To win a wrongful death case, the estate representative must prove:

- A person has died
- The death of that person was caused by the carelessness or negligence of another person
- The surviving family members of the deceased person suffered a financial loss
- The person bringing forth the claim is an estate representative

If monetary compensation is awarded, it could be used to cover the medical bills of the deceased, funeral expenses, emotional turmoil, and lost wages that would have been earned by the deceased person. A wrongful death attorney in Clayton County could help estate representatives and their families take stock of all their losses and ensure they demand appropriate compensation.

There is simply no way to put a price tag on human life, but in reality, surviving family members of a wrongful death victim generally need some form of compensation if they wish to maintain their standard of living. This may be especially true when the deceased person was the primary source of income for that family.

When calculating the worth of a wrongful death claim, the court may consider the deceased person�s age, income as well as potential earnings, moral character, general health, and life expectancy.� In general, younger victims with higher salaries may justify higher damage awards in wrongful death cases. When a child or older person dies, however, their families may usually recover fewer damages. This is because most children may not have regular incomes and most elderly individuals may have retired and no longer earn a steady wage from employment. An accomplished lawyer has experience calculating damages for families who have lost a loved one.

In some wrongful death cases, surviving family members could be awarded punitive damages. Unlike other types of damages, which may be based on specific costs and losses that could be calculated and added up, punitive damages may be awarded solely to punish the guilty party and discourage them from engaging in similar behaviors in the future.

Some courts may place limits on the compensation a jury could award a surviving family, which means they may not allow punitive damages to be awarded at all. If a surviving family member wishes to receive punitive damages, they should work closely with a Clayton County wrongful death lawyer to see what their options might be.

Dealing with the death of a loved one could take time, and filing a lawsuit may be the very last thing on your mind. But losing a loved one might place a profound financial strain on a family, and compensation from a successful lawsuit could be used to provide for them as well as yourself.

If you are entitled to monetary compensation because of your loss, it may be beneficial to further inquire about the possible recovery you may receive. When you are ready, call a Clayton County wrongful death lawyer for additional information.

pages.content_md:
Were you recently hurt in an accident or assault? Were your injuries someone else�s fault? If so, you may be entitled to financial compensation for your injuries and other damages.

Struggling to cope with your physical and emotional injuries can make life seem overwhelming especially if you are dealing with high medical costs. Do not delay any further. A personal injury is a physical or emotional injury someone suffers, often as the result of an accident. State personal injury laws dictate when an injured victim can sue someone else for compensation related to their injuries. The law allows victims to sue when someone�s negligence or criminal actions caused their injuries.

For example, a victim of assault can sue their assailant for injuries they sustained in the attack. Similarly, patients or nursing home residents, with the help of a Columbus injury lawyer, can sue healthcare providers when those providers engage in medical malpractice, causing injury or illness.

In most cases, personal injury victims make negligence claims. That is, they claim that someone else acted negligently, and that misconduct caused their injuries and other damages.

Proving negligence can be difficult because victims must generally prove several factors. First, they must show the responsible party had an obligation to act reasonably in order to prevent harm befalling the victim.

Then, the victim must show the other party failed to act reasonably, and that failure caused their injuries. Finally, the victim must show how they suffered, including financial losses they suffered related to their injuries.

A common example of negligence is the distracted driver who causes a car crash. All drivers have a duty to act reasonably and avoid accidents. A distracted driver acts unreasonably given their high-risk behavior.

When a distracted driver causes an accident, perhaps because they were focusing on their phone instead of the road, other people may get hurt. If the distracted driver�s vehicle strikes another driver, passenger, cyclist, or pedestrian, the victim can sue that driver for any injuries they sustain.

Most commonly, injured victims and their injury attorneys in Columbus attempt to get compensation for their:

- Medical bills
- Lost wages
- Lost future earnings in some cases
- Pain and suffering

Compensation for their physical, emotional, and financial losses can help victims move forward from the accident. An experienced Columbus personal injury lawyer can help an injured victim fight for the compensation they need.

Sadly, accidents can turn fatal for the victims involved. In those cases, the victim�s surviving family members can file a wrongful death claim. A wrongful death is one caused by another�s negligent or criminal conduct.

Surviving family members can sue the party responsible for the death with the help of a personal injury attorney. Surviving families may seek compensation for loss of companionship, their own pain and suffering, end-of-life medical costs, and other damages.

If you or a loved one has suffered injury or illness due to someone else�s negligence, contact a Columbus personal injury lawyer now. You could be entitled to financial compensation for the damages you suffered. Your lawyer will fight for the money you deserve while you continue to recover.

It is also important to seek medical attention following an accident. Failure to do so could negatively impact your injury claim. By seeking medical attention, the victim creates a legal record of their injuries which could be presented as evidence of injuries sustained. Lastly, a person should contact a Columbus car accident involving bad weather lawyer for help with filing an injury claim.

A Columbus�car accident involving bad weather lawyer could collect information from websites that record historical data based on weather radars and weather beacons placed all over America. That data is usually compiled by state highway departments. In other areas, radars and weather data are kept by the National Weather Service and the National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

A person can protect themselves from weather-related accidents by maintaining the tires on their vehicle. Any tire defect or lack of maintenance in the tires could lead to a deadly situation. People should use caution when driving during a downpour of snow and ice. The best way to prevent weather-related accidents is by not driving during horrid weather conditions. When someone is injured in a car crash where they hydroplaned or slid off the road due to snow and ice, they may think it was simply a single-car accident. With the help of a Columbus car accident involving bad weather attorney, you can hold the at-fault parties liable for their negligence. pages.content_md:
A plaintiff in a drunk driving accident can seek general damages and special damages. When the injuries are severe enough, the injured person can seek punitive damages. It is strongly recommended to schedule a consultation with a compassionate attorney before taking any legal action. A Columbus drunk driving accident lawyer can help you calculate the damages you are owed and fight on your behalf to see that you are awarded the correct compensation you are entitled to.

Driving under the influence by an at-fault driver almost always leads to an argument for punitive damages for injuries the DUI driver caused. Punitive damages are awarded on top of general and special damages in circumstances where the at-fault driver acted recklessly or wantonly without regard for anybody’s safety.

Punitive damages are awarded to hold the person civilly liable for the harm. For example, if the at-fault driver is convicted of a DUI, they may go to prison for the criminal offense. However, on the civil side, they must pay more for the injuries the person received. For more information, about filing a claim, get in touch with a�Columbus drunk driving accident lawyer.

Historically, drunk driving accidents in Columbus occur late at night. However, with the opiate problem running rampant in the Southern United States, these kinds of accidents happen at all times of the day, seven days a week. Most DUI car crashes tend to be a failure to maintain the lane by the drunk driver crossing the centerline. Other times, the impaired driver runs red lights and things of that nature. Accidents caused by impaired drivers happen 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and 365 days a year.

Columbus is a modified comparative negligence state.�This means that if the plaintiff was also found to be drunk at the time of the accident, that may be taken into account. When the majority of the fault belongs to the drunk driver, the injured party can still be compensated. Under Columbus law, if someone is awarded $10,000 by a jury and found to be 20 percent at fault, that jury’s award is reduced by 20 percent. Therefore, the injured party would only get $8,000.

When substantial injuries occur because of a drunk driver, the drunk driver is charged with a DUI and some type of aggravated assault. Victims assistance programs in the criminal justice system contact the injured party after the accident to line up interviews with police officers to find out the true extent of their injuries. Should a drunk driver not plead guilty to any of their crimes, it is possible their case goes to a criminal trial. At that time, the injured party is usually subpoenaed to testify before the court as to how the accident occurred.

Injury cases and the associated DUI case are handled separately. Keep in mind that the DUI case is a criminal matter. The injury case is a civil matter. They are two separate areas of law. It is impossible to go to jail or be imprisoned by a civil court. However, criminal courts can lock someone up.

A person injured as a result of a drunk driving accident should be sure to get in contact with a Columbus drunk driving accident lawyer. An attorney can help with calculating total damages, as well as the collection of evidence used to prove the defendant’s negligence. An experienced attorney can also use their knowledge to help with interviewing any witnesses, as well as obtaining evidence which may be in law enforcement’s possession. All other uses of a cell phone are outlawed.

Injuries sustained from this type of car crash could be serious due to the lack of reaction from the negligent driver. If you or someone you love has sustained injuries as a result of this form of negligent driving, contact a compassionate attorney. A Columbus texting while driving accident lawyer may be able to provide you with professional assistance.

There is a relatively new Columbus statute that addresses the use of a cellphone while driving. The statute, which is criminal in nature, says that it is illegal for someone to use a mobile device while operating a motor vehicle. Using a mobile device can include changing songs on iTunes or Spotify, texting, and dialing phone numbers. A driver in Columbus who is under 18 and has a Class D license or a learner�s permit cannot use any wireless device while driving. That includes cell phones, computers, and all texting devices.

Plaintiffs or injured victims are placed under oath during depositions and asked if they were using their cellphone at the time of the accident. They should always tell the truth because the authorities can obtain cell phone records and find out what the person was doing at a specific time up to the exact second.

The plaintiff�s attorney can find out what someone was doing at the time of the accident. They can look at cell phone data reports and call and text reports to find out up to the second what somebody was doing when the accident occurred.

Columbus is a modified comparative negligence state. If a claim goes to a jury trial, the jury is asked what�the jury may be asked about the percentage of fault that should be placed on the plaintiff and how much fault is assigned to the defendant. If both drivers are found on their phones during an accident, fault may be assigned to both drivers. Cell phone used is not guaranteed to aggressively affect the value of the damages in a case where there is a clear liability such as the at-fault driver running into the back of the plaintiff, running a red light, or running a stop sign.

Attorneys can pull cell phone records from providers such as Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile and identify exactly what someone was doing at the time of the wreck. To seize phone records of drivers involved in a car accident in Columbus, law enforcement and insurance companies must obtain a consent form. However, they usually back down and provide the information to the plaintiff�s lawyer. A Columbus texting while driving accident lawyer can help protect the plaintiff from aggressive actions taken by insurance companies.

If you or someone you love has sustained injuries after an auto wreck where the negligent driver was on the cell phone at the time of the accident, it is best to consult with a Columbus texting while driving accident lawyer.
