pages.h1: Dallas Car Accidents Caused by Texting and Driving
pages.content_md:
**�**Every driver in Dallas assumes a duty to act responsibly while behind the wheel of a motor vehicle. Unfortunately, many motorists fail to uphold this duty, especially when they text and drive.

Not only is this behavior reckless and dangerous, but it is also illegal. Police officers can arrest an individual if they suspect this person of texting while behind the wheel. Because using a cellphone while driving is illegal, people injured in collisions caused by these distracted drivers may pursue claims against these individuals.

If you were involved in a Dallas car accident caused by texting and driving, a seasoned lawyer could help you demand compensation. A dedicated car wreck attorney could help you understand the state�s law concerning texting, how these regulations may affect your civil claim, and accurately measure your losses.

Studies have long shown that texting while driving decreases a driver�s reaction time and serves as a potent distraction. Despite this common knowledge, the rise of smartphones has led to many people texting, reading their e-mail, or searching the internet while driving.

Because of this problem, the State Legislature moved to outlaw this behavior. According to Official Code of Georgia Annotated �40-6-241, it is illegal for a person to use any wireless communication device while operating a vehicle. This same statute makes it a misdemeanor-level crime for a person to read, write, or send any electronic communication while driving. Additionally, the law does provide an exception for people using a hands-free device or for those using their phones for navigational purposes.

Because this violation is a misdemeanor crime, an arrest following suspected texting while driving may lead to a full criminal trial. The outcome of this trial can have a substantial impact on an injured party�s claims for damages. A Dallas lawyer could determine if someone texting while driving was the cause of an accident and build a case on this informations.

While texting behind the wheel is illegal, a criminal conviction does not do much to help an injured individual move on with their life. Criminal courts can force a guilty party to pay a fine. However, these courts cannot require a defendant to provide compensation to an injured plaintiff.

To accomplish this goal, injured parties must pursue related but separate civil lawsuits. With this in mind, a criminal conviction can still significantly increase the chances of success in these civil cases.

Plaintiffs in civil cases must prove that a defendant was responsible for the act that resulted in their injuries. If a Dallas attorney can base a texting while driving case on negligence per se, proof of a criminal conviction may be all the evidence that a plaintiff needs to recover compensation. Negligence per se allows courts to presume defendant liability if they violated the law and caused an injury as a result. In other words, a criminal conviction is proof of wrongdoing beyond a reasonable doubt, and as a result, proves that a defendant was responsible for a wreck.

A driver who chooses to look at a cellphone places all other people on the road at a significant risk of harm. This kind of reckless behavior is illegal in Dallas and throughout the state. Sadly, Dallas car accidents caused by texting and driving are common.

These wrecks may result in severe physical injuries, intense emotional trauma, and significant financial losses. Therefore, drivers who commit these violations may be liable to provide payments to injured parties. An attorney could help you pursue your case. To learn how we could help you and your case, schedule an initial consultation.

pages.title: Dallas Catastrophic Injury Lawyer | Permanent Injury Claims
pages.description: An experienced Dallas catastrophic injury lawyer could help you recover compensation if you or a loved one suffered a severe injury.
pages.content_md:
Catastrophic injuries are defined by the long-lasting and permanent damage that they create. These types of injuries can lead not only to lifelong physical impairments but long-term psychological damage as well.

If you or a loved one has suffered severe bodily harm, you may wish to consult with a Dallas catastrophic injury lawyer. Such a significant injury generally leads to substantial medical bills, lost wages, and lost future earning potential, and an injured party deserves to receive compensation for these losses. While a seasoned personal injury attorney cannot undo your losses, they may be able to inform you of your legal rights, advocate on your behalf, and pursue compensation.

A catastrophic injury is generally one that has a life-altering effect on an individual. Some injuries that may fall into this category of bodily harm include:

- Spinal cord damage that causes partial or full paralysis
- Traumatic brain injuries
- Third-degree burns
- Amputations or loss of limb
- Spinal injuries that require fusion surgery
- Broken bones that result in screws, pins, plates, or rod implants

If someone sustained a catastrophic injury in an accident, they should speak with an attorney in Dallas. A catastrophic injury lawyer in Dallas could work one-on-one with a plaintiff to determine the extent and severity of their injuries and how best to pursue a claim for damages.

Generally, a plaintiff may bring a claim against the individual or company that they allege acted negligently and caused their accident. The types of losses that a plaintiff may pursue, separately or in combination, are economic, noneconomic, and punitive damages. A Dallas lawyer with experience in litigating catastrophic injury cases could determine how much in damages a claimant may be able to obtain.

Economic damages relate to the actual out-of-pocket costs caused by an injury. These generally encompass medical bills, lost wages, and future lost earnings. Because of the permanent nature of some catastrophic injuries, a plaintiff’s capacity to work may no longer exist or be at the same level.

Non-economic damages account for more intangible physical injuries such as pain and suffering, and psychological effects like loss of enjoyment of life, loss of consortium, and humiliation. A plaintiff left partially or entirely paralyzed may seek these types of damages.

Punitive damages can be the most difficult to obtain. Rather than to compensate the plaintiff for expenses related to their physical and emotional trauma, punitive damages are intended to punish the defendant for their actions. Generally, a court will not award these damages if the defendant was merely negligent, but reckless and far outside the bounds of the actions of a reasonable person.

Those who have sustained a catastrophic injury can be physically and psychologically affected for the rest of their lives. Fortunately, if you or a loved one are suffering from such bodily harm, a Dallas catastrophic injury lawyer may be able to help.

Our caring and dedicated attorneys could explain your legal rights, build your case, and advocate on your behalf before a court or in settlement negotiations. Contact our office today to see what we could do for your case.

pages.title: Dallas Burn Injury Lawyer | First-Degree | Second-Degree | Third-Degree
pages.description: If you sustained a severe burn, a Dallas burn injury lawyer to discuss your legal options and your eligibility to pursue compensation.
pages.content_md:
Few injuries can be as traumatizing and outwardly visible, as a burn. While first-degree burns can generally heal on their own, second and third-degree burns often require surgical procedures just as skin grafting. These procedures can not only limit an individual physically, but they can leave lifelong scars.

If you or a loved one have endured such an injury, you may need to consult with a Dallas burn injury lawyer. Depending on the specifics of your case, you may have legal rights that could entitle you to pursue damages. Whether in court or settlement negotiations, an experienced attorney could act as an advocate on your behalf, clearly present your case, and pursue a fair outcome.

Burns can happen in many different ways, the most typical of which is due to fire or exposure to hot liquids such as boiling water or coffee. Additionally, product malfunctions, explosions, or exposure at plants or on construction sites can lead to chemical burns. The three main categories of burn injuries include:

- First-degree: these injuries are the least severe and typically only result in redness and minor inflammation
- Second-degree: this type of injury damages the top layer of skin and may penetrate to deeper layers, causing extremely red skin and blisters.
- Third-degree: these are the most severe and dangerous type of burn. These injuries may penetrate to the bones and organs, require skin graft surgeries, and may cause lifelong scarring.

The statute of limitations gives a potential plaintiff a limited time to file a lawsuit for their injuries. Under Official Code of Georgia Annotated �9-3-33, an individual who suffered injuries in a burn incident must bring their suit within two years from the date of their accident.

If a plaintiff were to bring their case after this statutory period, the court may dismiss their claim, and they could lose their opportunity to recover compensation. As such, the sooner a claimant brings their burn injury case to a Dallas attorney, the sooner they can begin discussing and meet this deadline.

In general, there are two primary forms of financial compensation that a lawyer may pursue on a plaintiff’s behalf. One category of damages include all of the economic costs a plaintiff incurs as a result of their injury, such as medical expenses, lost wages, and future lost earnings. The total dollar amount of all of these losses gives the value of economic damages in a case.

Emotional losses, the other form of compensation, can be more difficult to precisely calculate because they incorporate intangible injuries such as pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, humiliation from disfigurement, and more. Because burn injuries can be particularly impactful on an individual’s outward appearance, an injured claimant may be able to pursue compensation for these emotional damages.

A severe burn can cause painful bodily harm, complicated surgeries, and lifelong disfiguring scars. If you have sustained a severe burn, you should consult with a Dallas burn injury lawyer. Depending on your case, an attorney may be able to pursue a claim on your behalf in the courts or through settlement negotiations. Reach out today and learn how we could help you.

Additionally, someone may only experience paralysis in one portion of their body or they may lose the ability to control movement from the neck down.

Recovering for emotional losses also may be an option for an injured party. These damages may include pain and suffering, mental anguish, and other psychological harm. A Dallas paralysis injury attorney could assess an individual’s losses and identify what their case may be worth.

Becoming paralyzed following a serious accident can lead to many challenges in the future. pages.title: Dallas Spinal Cord Injury Lawyer | Back Trauma Injury Claims
pages.description: If you or a loved one suffered a spinal cord injury due to the negligence of another party, contact a Dallas spinal cord injury lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
Spinal cord injuries can be particularly painful, debilitating, and cause an individual to incur significant medical bills. Additionally, these injuries often require surgical procedures, long-term rehabilitation, and still, a person may never fully recover.

If you were in an accident and sustained spine damage, a Dallas spinal cord injury lawyer could help. The severity of these injuries may have lasting physical, psychological, and financial effects. In a civil lawsuit, a plaintiff typically alleges that their injuries occurred as a result of some negligent act by the defendant. In these situations, a defendant may make an argument that the plaintiff is partially responsible for their injury. This is called comparative negligence.

If a plaintiff is found to be partially responsible for their accident, the court determines what percentage the claimant is at fault, and then reduce their damages award by that amount. For example, if a plaintiff is 20 percent at fault for their vertebrae injury, they may only obtain 80 percent of their total losses from the defendant.

It is important to note that a claimant may only be able to recover compensation if they are 49 percent or less at fault for their injuries. If a defendant could use the comparative negligence argument to reduce their liability, a Dallas attorney who is familiar with spinal cord injury cases could determine how to best fight against these allegations.

Spinal cord injuries can begin as minor, dull pains that worsen over time. However, they could also cause immediate and devastating effects, such as paralysis. No matter where you fall on this spectrum, a dedicated Dallas spinal cord injury lawyer may be able to help.

A spinal cord lawsuit may require a professional who has knowledge about both medical terminology and the complex legal nuances of these cases. A local personal injury attorney who is well-versed in this area of litigation may be able to lessen the financial severity of your situation and achieve a favorable resolution. A TBI attorney in Dallas could work to ensure that an injured claimant demands compensation for all of their losses.

pages.title: Dallas Dangerous Drugs Lawyer | Undisclosed Side-Effects | Mislabelling
pages.description: If you were harmed by a prescription or over-the-counter medication, reach out to a Dallas dangerous drugs lawyer for advice and advocacy.
pages.content_md:
To put their products on the market, pharmaceutical companies must submit their drugs to intensive Food and Drug Administration (FDA) testing and approval processes. If a company fails to provide proper information to the FDA or deliberately hides serious side effects, this manufacturer may be liable for any resulting damages sustained by users.

A Dallas dangerous drugs lawyer could help you take legal action if you have suffered injuries from taking unsafe medications. A skilled personal injury attorney could evaluate the company�s role in your injuries and measure your losses to demand proper compensation.

Pharmaceutical companies must produce medications that work as intended and do not cause any undue harm to consumers when taken properly. Additionally, drug manufacturers have a legal obligation to inform a consumer about the potential side effects. Failure to meet any of these standards may result in a company being liable for any losses that occur.

During a dangerous drugs case, a lawyer in Dallas may argue that a medication�s defective design made it inherently unsafe. This means that an attorney may have to prove that the medication�s chemical formula was dangerous and that an alternative, viable design could have prevented the injury. This argument often involves hiring an expert pharmacologist to prove the case.

An attorney also may try to argue that the defendant did not provide proper warnings about the dangers of using the drug in question. A lawyer could investigate the cause of a claimant�s losses and build a legal argument depending on the circumstances of the case.

The goal of a dangerous drug case is to make a claimant whole again after a negligent defendant causes them to suffer losses. When a consumer takes an unsafe drug, may affect their physical and mental health. For example, if a drug manufacturer mislabels the dosage for a blood pressure mediation, a consumer may suffer serious adverse effects as a result of an overdose.

Additionally, being sent to the hospital can be a distressing experience that causes some individuals to suffer severe emotional trauma. Finally, that time in hospital or spent making a recovery may force a plaintiff to miss work and lose valuable wages. Therefore, a Dallas lawyer could help a claimant in a dangerous drugs case recover compensation for their medical bills, emotional trauma, lost wages, and other damages.

As a general rule, a plaintiff in a personal injury case has two years from the date of their losses to file a case under the Official Code of Georgia Annotated �9-3-33. However, it is important to note that there is a special rule that governs time limits for product liability claims, such as those involving dangerous medications. Under O.C.G.A. �51-1-11, in no case may a plaintiff bring a claim after more than ten years have passed since the product left the company�s control.

Drug companies have a duty to produce medications that do not cause any undue harm. This includes the drug companies that make both over the counter and prescription medications. These medications must perform their stated function after FDA testing, provide specific instructions for safe use, and disclaim all potential side effects. A manufacturer that fails in any portion of this duty may be liable for any resulting damage.

A Dallas dangerous drugs lawyer could help you pursue a case if a pharmaceutical company fails to meet any of these obligations. Contact our firm today to learn how our team could help you and your case.

pages.title: Dallas Defective Products Lawyer | Faulty and Hazardous Items
pages.description: Were you injured after safely handling a faulty item? Consult a Dallas defective products lawyer to discuss your legal rights for filing a claim.
pages.content_md:
Producers have a legal obligation to their consumers to design and create safe products. When consumers suffer injuries and other losses due to a dangerous or malfunctioning product, they may have a viable claim for damages.

A Dallas defective products lawyer could help you file a claim if you sustained injuries when using an item as intended. A skilled personal injury attorney could become your legal advocate as you fight against large manufacturing companies.

Defective products can be any item that does not work as intended due to its design or the manufacturing process. If a company makes a mistake during one of these processes, it could be liable for any injuries that result.

A court also may find a producer liable if they fail to adequately warn its consumers about the possible dangers or side effects of using its product. It is important to note that individuals may only have a viable claim if they got injured because they were using an item as the producer intended.

An individual should contact a lawyer if they are thinking about filing a defects products claim in Dallas because a legal professional could help them determine if a company may be liable for their injuries. Additionally, an attorney could identify how a producer may be at fault, whether it was during the manufacturing process r by failing to warn consumers of its product�s dangers.

Claimants have a limited amount of time to file their cases after sustaining injuries from a faulty item. Under Official Georgia Code Annotated �9-3-33, an individual has two years from the date of their injuries to file a claim. However, there are a few exceptions to this statutory deadline. For instance, according to O.C.G.A �51-1-11, if a claimant only suffered property damage, the statute of limitations is four years.

If an injured party fails to meet this deadline, they may risk losing their opportunity to recover any compensation. A Dallas defective products attorney could help a claimant meet all legal deadlines pertinent to their claim.

The amount of monetary compensation that a plaintiff may be able to receive depends on the totality of their losses. The severity of the claimant�s injuries and property damage may be examined as well as how their losses may impact their life in the future. For instance, if an individual becomes permanently disabled after using a defective item, their compensation could be substantial.

Additionally, if a court finds that a plaintiff is partially to blame for their injuries, a judge may reduce a claimant�s compensation by their assigned percentage of fault. This may occur when a consumer did not use a product as intended and suffered bodily harm as a result. A lawyer in Dallas who is familiar with faulty items claims could review a plaintiff�s circumstances and determine what their compensatory award may look like.

If you suffered bodily harm as a result of a malfunctioning product, you may be entitled to take legal action against the producer. A Dallas defective products lawyer could provide the support and legal protection necessary to sue a corporation. To get started on your case, schedule an initial consultation today.

pages.title: Dallas Dog Bite Lawyer | Canine Attack Claims | Negligent Pet Owner
pages.description: If a negligent pet owner caused you to suffer injuries in a canine attack, speak with a Dallas dog bite lawyer who could help you hold them accountable.
pages.content_md:
While most dog bite injuries range in severity, they share one aspect in common, which is they may result in significant consequences. The aftermath of a canine attack could lead to substantial medical bills, long-term mental trauma, and lost income.

If you suffered injuries in a canine attack, a Dallas dog bite lawyer could assist you during your journey toward legal recovery. With all of the stresses you may already be facing, it could be beneficial to retain a dedicated personal injury attorney to help handle your legal recovery efforts.

Because state law does not establish a particular dog bite statute, plaintiffs may seek recovery based on a traditional negligence claim, or in some cases, strict liability. A Dallas dog bite attorney could asses an injured party�s situation and determine which course of legal action best fits their case.

In cases of negligence, state law follows the Restatement of Torts, which uses basic principles of negligence and the one-bite rule to determine if a party is liable in a dog attack case. Someone injured by a dog may hold the owner liable under negligence if:

- The owner knew of the dog�s past aggression
- The dog had bitten someone in the past
- The owner failed to use reasonable care to control their dog or prevent the attack from occurring
- The plaintiff was bitten and injured as a result of the owner�s failure to reasonably prevent the attack

Although there is no dog bite statute, pet owners may still be held strictly liable for someone�s injuries under certain circumstances. For instance, if the court determines that the dog was dangerous, and the owner knew of their viciousness, they could be held strictly liable. In these situations, the plaintiff may not have to prove that the owner failed to use reasonable care. Instead, the dog owner would have to rebut the presumption that they were at fault.

The main defenses that a Dallas lawyer may have to refute in a dog bite case are trespassing and a lack of knowledge. A defendant may claim that they did not know that their dog had a history of aggressive or dangerous behavior. Additionally, if a plaintiff is trespassing at the time of the attack, the defendant may not be liable for their injuries.

If a plaintiff is partially at fault for causing their injuries by either provoking the dog or trespassing on the owner�s property, the court may reduce their damages or bar them from recovering completely.�Official Code of Georgia Annotated �51-12-33, states that if a plaintiff is 49 percent or less at fault, they may still recover compensation that is reduced by their percentage of liability. Otherwise, they may not recover.

Taking on an injury claim can be overbearing without proper legal guidance. Fortunately, a Dallas dog bite lawyer could help you negotiate and fight for the recovery you deserve. To learn more about how an attorney could help you, call today.

pages.title: Dallas Medical Malpractice Lawyer | Physician's Error
pages.description: If you sustained losses after visiting a medical professional, speak with a Dallas medical malpractice lawyer to discuss your legal options.
pages.content_md:
Seeing a physician for help with your injuries and illnesses involves a great deal of trust. Unfortunately, medical professionals sometimes do not give their patients the care and attention they deserve, resulting in mistakes that could lead to devastating outcomes.

If you sustained losses from a medical error, you may be entitled to seek compensation. However, fighting against insurance companies and malpractice defense firms on your own can be a daunting task without an experienced personal injury attorney by your side. A Dallas medical malpractice lawyer could become your legal advocate and protect your rights when going against these entities.

In medical malpractice cases, the court applies a different level of care than other types of negligence claims. In a basic negligence claim, the plaintiff must show that the defendant breached their duty of care, causing them to sustain harm. Under this standard, a defendant is considered negligent if they do not act like a reasonably prudent person would under the circumstances.

However, in medical malpractice cases, the court holds health care professionals to a heightened standard of care. The medical standard of care holds a physician liable for malpractice if they fail to administer the same type of care that a prudent health care professional, with the same experience and training, would administer within the same community under the circumstances.

Some common types of medical malpractice cases that our Dallas attorneys have worked on include:

- Failure to warn patients of known risks of treatment
- Improperly treating a patient�s injury or illness
- Failure to properly diagnose
- Surgical errors

Our attorneys could help a plaintiff prove that their health care provider failed to meet this heightened standard of care following an instance of malpractice.

Those suffering from medical malpractice injuries in Dallas may seek compensation through an insurance claim and by filing a lawsuit. To bring a successful claim, a plaintiff must demonstrate that a doctor-patient relationship existed at the time of the injury, that their physician failed to meet the medical standard of care, and caused them specific losses as a result.

Plaintiffs may seek economic and emotional damages to compensate them for their losses. Noneconomic damages may include pain and suffering and emotional anguish. A judge and jury may look at factors such as the severity of their losses and other similar cases to determine the value of a claimant�s emotional damages.

Economic damages may include monetary losses such as lost wages, reduced future earning capacity, medical bills, and out-of-pocket expenses. A Dallas lawyer with experience in litigating medical malpractice cases could prove an injured party�s economic losses through documentation, including invoices and receipts.

If your medical care provider caused you to sustain damages, a Dallas medical malpractice lawyer could be of assistance. By reviewing your case, an attorney could identify the value of your claim and work to help you obtain fair compensation. To start exploring your legal options for recovery, schedule an initial case consultation.

pages.title: Dallas Birth Injury Lawyer | Harm to a Newborn | Trauma to an Infant

pages.content_md:
Birth injuries occur when a newborn suffers harm right before, during, or immediately after delivery. A newborn can experience birth injuries or trauma when they were not delivered head-first, were born prematurely, or the mother experienced difficulties while in labor. In these situations, the doctor may try to deliver a baby via a C-section or using a medical vacuum or forceps, which could put the infant at risk of suffering injuries.

Many parties could be held responsible for a baby�s injuries. A doctor or nurse may be liable if they did not use proper judgment when delivering the baby. Additionally, the hospital may be responsible if there was improper training or supervision that resulted in the infant�s harm. A knowledgable Dallas lawyer could review a birth injury case to identify the at-fault party.**�**

In a birth injury case, claimants may be able to recover the medical bills and expenses associated with the infant�s bodily harm. Also, a claimant could recover legal costs, travel expenses, and damages for the pain and suffering of the child.

In certain cases where the defendant�s misconduct was extremely negligent, a court may award punitive damages to the plaintiff to discourage such actions in the future. There is a wide range of potential compensation available to families harmed by birth trauma, and a compassionate Dallas lawyer could work to maximize a claimant�s potential damages.

**Statute of Limitations for Birth Trauma Claims**

Potential claimants should be aware of the statute of limitations for bringing birth injury lawsuits. In general, state law sets a two-year deadline for some medical malpractice cases. However, state law establishes an exception for those who suffer injuries under the age of five. Claims involving these minors have until two years after their fifth birthday to bring a personal injury suit on the child�s behalf, according to Official Code of Georgia Annotated �9-3-73(b). A birth injury attorney in Dallas could work to ensure that a claimant meets the applicable statutory deadline to their situation.

If your newborn suffered a traumatic injury during delivery, you may be entitled to seek legal action against the responsible party. However, it is beneficial to have a legal advocate during these difficult and stressful times.

A well-versed Dallas birth injury lawyer could assist you in building a case for damages in addition to guiding you throughout the claims process. �To consult a caring and dedicated attorney about your child�s injury, call today.

pages.title: Dallas Motorcycle Accident Lawyer | Motorbike Injuries

pages.title: Dallas Nursing Home Abuse Lawyer | Elderly Abuse
pages.description: If you or a loved one has been abused by others, seek the services of a skilled Dallas nursing home abuse lawyer that could help you hold them accountable.
pages.content_md:
Nursing homes are expected to provide considerate and thorough care to our loved ones at all times. If you learn that the Dallas facility you trusted with this responsibility instead neglected or abused your loved ones, it could be crucial to address the situation legally as soon as possible.

If you suspect a loved one suffered or is suffering abuse or neglect in their assisted care facility, talk to a compassionate Dallas nursing home abuse lawyer. While it may be impossible to change the past, a dedicated personal injury attorney could help you and your family seek compensation for the harm you endured, so you can achieve some semblance of justice and protect yourselves and others from future harm.

Abuse in nursing homes can come in a variety of forms. While signs of physical abuse may be evident during a physical examination, others forms of abuse�such as financial exploitation or emotional abuse�may be undetectable even to loved ones.

Some common signs of abuse in Dallas include:

- Bed sores or malnutrition
- Unexplained injuries, such as fractured bones, sprains, and bruises
- Sudden changes in legal documents
- Frequent or unusual ATM or bank withdrawals
- Evidence of physical restraint
- Childlike behavior, such as rocking or thumb-sucking
- Fear or apprehension around staff or other residents
- Any sudden change to a person�s demeanor or behavior

It should be noted that elderly residents of assisted care facilities may easily bruise or become frightened, so certain symptoms may not always be cause for concern. However, changes in the frequency or severity of bruises could be an indicator of abuse. Individuals who suspect abuse should contact a Dallas nursing home abuse attorney and outline any concerns they have.

In some cases, nursing home abuse and neglect may not be deliberate and may instead be the result of negligence on the nursing home�s part. However, nursing home staff and administrators can still be liable for harm inflicted even if it was unintentional. Generally, successful negligence-based cases hinge on demonstrating what the reasonable standard of care should have been in a particular situation and showing how a nursing home failed to uphold its duty to provide that care.

From there, a nursing home abuse lawyer in Dallas could work to reinforce the direct connection between this breach of duty and harm sustained by the plaintiff or their elderly family member. If these elements are proven, a resident�or their family filing on their behalf�could recover monetary damages to cover expenses like medical bills, as well as compensation for intangible harm such as pain and suffering and loss of enjoyment of activities.

Many families may not be sure if a lawsuit is appropriate in their situation or whether taking legal action is in the best interests of their loved one. Regardless of whether you file suit or not, though, seeking legal counsel could help you ensure your loved one is safe and that their nursing home lives up to their obligations.

A Dallas nursing home abuse lawyer could assist not only with filing a lawsuit but also in conducting investigations to determine whether maltreatment occurred. If you are concerned that a loved one in your family may be suffering from nursing home abuse, call today to schedule a consultation and learn how an attorney could help in your particular situation.

pages.title: Dallas Pedestrian Accident Lawyer | Collisions with Foot Traffic
pages.description: If you or someone you love has sustained damages while acting as a pedestrian, get in touch with a Dallas pedestrian accident lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
When a motor vehicle collides with a pedestrian, the pedestrian may sustain serious injuries or even death. If the motor vehicle driver was at fault for causing the accident, the injured individual may be able to file a claim for damages. If the pedestrian died in the crash, the decedent�s estate representative may be able to file the claim in their place.

If you or a loved one sustained injuries in a pedestrian accident, you may need the assistance of a Dallas pedestrian accident lawyer who could help you review the facts of your accident and develop a plan to obtain a fair settlement. A capable attorney is ready to stand by your side to potentially present your personal injury case to the defendants and hold them accountable.

There are some steps all pedestrians can take to lessen the likelihood of an accident. These include:

- Using a designated crosswalk when one is available
- Crossing the street when and where it is safe to do so
- Abiding by traffic control devices and other pedestrian signals
- Never attempting to beat traffic or run through a crosswalk or intersection

Motorists have a duty to act with reasonable care towards others when on the roads. Whenever a pedestrian is walking in a designated crosswalk at an intersection in accordance with proper traffic signals, motor vehicle drivers must give the pedestrian the right of way. Failing to do so is typically deemed a violation of their duty of care and may result in liability.

To prove a driver is negligent, the injured pedestrian must show that the driver acted in a careless, negligent, or reckless manner. The injured pedestrian must also be able to show the wreck was the direct cause of their injuries. For help with proving negligence, it is highly recommended to retain the services of a Dallas pedestrian accident lawyer today.

With external protection, pedestrians are much more vulnerable to injuries than car or truck drivers. This may be especially true if the motor vehicle is moving at a high speed at the time of the impact.

Pedestrian injuries can range in severity, depending on the force of the impact and where the accident occurred. Injuries can include:

- Cuts and burns
- Bone fractures
- Spinal cord injuries
- Traumatic brain injuries
- Soft tissue injuries

Injured pedestrians may sometimes share the blame for a crash. For example, at the time of impact, the pedestrian may have been walking slightly outside the crosswalk lines or may have started crossing the intersection when it was not safe to do so.

In this situation, Texas uses the doctrine of comparative negligence. Under comparative negligence, if the accident victim�s level of fault is half or less than half, the accident victim could still recover damages. However, the final settlement will be reduced by the percentage attributable to the plaintiff.

No matter what the extent of your injuries or whether you believe you share the fault, you may want to consult with a Dallas pedestrian accident lawyer to review your legal options. Skilled local attorneys could help you negotiate with the insurance company, prove damages, and pursue a fair settlement to cover your injuries and losses. You may be entitled to compensation for another party�s careless or negligent acts, so do not hesitate to call today.

pages.title: Dallas Premises Liability Lawyer | Hazardous Property Conditions
pages.description: If you suffered an injury due to a dangerous condition on another's property, you may have a viable civil claim. Call a Dallas premises liability lawyer.
pages.content_md:
Property owners have a legal obligation to take reasonable care of their premises and to warn some visitors of potential dangers. If a proprietor fails to meet this standard, they may face legal consequences.

If you suffered injuries on someone else�s property, you should seek the services of an experienced a Dallas premises liability lawyer. A skilled personal injury attorney could determine if you have a viable legal claim and help you pursue fair compensation.

Someone may have a viable premises liability claim if they get hurt while on another person�s or entity�s property. However, simply getting hurt on another�s property is not sufficient to bring a premises liability claim. Plaintiffs may only obtain damages if they can prove that the defendant was negligent.

This means that an injured party must demonstrate that a proprietor failed to reasonably maintain their property, and therefore, created the dangerous condition that caused the plaintiff�s injuries. For example, if a property owner does not clean up a spill on their floor in a timely manner and someone slips and falls as a result, this proprietor may be liable for their injuries.

Property owners owe different levels of care to their visitors depending on their reason for being on the premises at the time of their injury. Property owners owe the greatest amount of protection and care to invitees, who are visitors that benefit the property owner financially.

Proprietors are required to maintain their premises and keep it reasonably safe for invitees. Property owners must warn licensees, or social guests, of known dangerous conditions on their premises that a licensee would not likely discover.

Property owners do not owe trespassers any duty of care. However, children are still afforded some protection even if they are trespassing. Property owners must use reasonable care to remove or secure any dangerous conditions that could attract and injure a child trespasser. These conditions may include tools or a swimming pool. A Dallas premises liability attorney could determine what classification of visitor a claimant falls into and what protections they were entitled to based on their category.

Those suffering from a premises liability injury may seek economic and noneconomic damages. Economic damages may compensate a plaintiff for any medical bills or other monetary losses they may have accrued as a result of the injuries.

Noneconomic damages may include emotional losses such as pain and suffering, mental anguish, and loss of enjoyment of life. These losses may be more difficult to prove. Therefore, an injured party should consult with a Dallas lawyer who has experience in litigating premises liability claims for help establishing all of their losses in court or settlement negotiations.

Property owners have a duty to their visitors to keep them safe from potentially hazardous conditions on their premises. When they fail to do so, and you suffer injuries, they should be held accountable.

A Dallas premises liability lawyer could give you the support you need to carry your claim forward. They could help you navigate through the process and become your legal advocate. Call today to get started on your claim for recovery.

pages.title: Dallas Slip and Fall Lawyer | Falling Due to Property Owner Negligence
pages.description: If you or someone you love has been injured after slipping and/or falling on somone's property, get in touch with a Dallas slip and fall lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
Slip and fall accidents often occur when people least expect them. Some accidents occur indoors, such as in a grocery store or shopping mall, while others occur outdoors in parking lots and on sidewalks. One thing slip and fall accidents have in common is that they can cause serious injuries and side effects. The injuries an individual sustained may be the result of a property owner�s carelessness, so a victim may be able to receive compensation for injuries and losses.

If you sustained injuries in a slip and fall accident that you suspect arose from someone else�s negligence, you may need to call a Dallas slip and fall lawyer to help you build a personal injury case. A compassionate injury lawyer could help you build a strong case and negotiate with the defendant for a fair settlement.

A person�s status on the premises can determine their ability to obtain monetary compensation for slip and fall injuries. For example, if the injured person is a store patron or customer, they are considered an invitee and are owed the highest duty of care.

If the visitors to the premises are invitees, the premises owner or manager must inspect and ensure the premises are reasonably safe for them. Moreover, they must take reasonable steps to warn invitees of known hazards on the premises. A similar duty of care is owed to those considered licensees, who are social guests or a salesman. These people are entering for their own benefit and the owner must warn of or make safe conditions they are aware of.

If the premises owner or manager fails to take these precautions, the accident victim may be able to file a legal claim against the premises owner or manager for damages. The owner does not, however, have to take precautions for the last type of visitor: a trespasser. This is someone who is on the property without permission and for which the property owner does not owe a duty of care. The owner generally cannot be held liable for a trespasser�s injuries.

Fractures and broken bones are common with slip and fall accidents. This is because the accident victim may fall unexpectedly and forcefully onto their backsides. The bones in their back, hipbones, or posterior may receive the force and consequently, break or fracture.

In addition to breaks or fractures, accident victims may also sustain soft tissue injuries or more permanent injuries such as a traumatic head injury. In the event of a permanent injury, the accident victim may require long-term care and physical or vocational rehabilitation.

Factors used to determine whether an injury is permanent include the following:

- Whether medical procedures can resolve the condition
- Amount and extent of medical care and treatment needed
- Post-accident ability levels compared to pre-accident ability levels
- Physical activity levels before and after the slip and fall accident

A Dallas slip and fall lawyer could use their connections to consult with a medical expert and determine whether the claimant is suffering from a permanent injury. With the help of the medical expert, the lawyer could estimate the amount of potential financial compensation based on the costs of future medical procedures, care, and treatment.

Many slip and fall injuries are preventable, but occur because property owners and managers do not provide the necessary care and attention to property maintenance issues. If you sustained injuries on a poorly maintained premise, you may be able to obtain compensation for your injuries.

A Dallas slip and fall lawyer could assess your situation to see if it has a basis for a personal injury claim and provide you with support to move forward with your legal options. A seasoned lawyer could help you hold the responsible party accountable for their negligence by seeking fair compensation from them.s

pages.title: Dallas Truck Accident Lawyer | Tractor Trailer Claims

pages.title: Dallas Workers� Compensation Lawyer | Worksite Injuries
pages.description: If you or a loved one were injured while at work, reach out to an experienced Dallas workers' compensation lawyer today. Let an attorney fight for you.
pages.content_md:
When someone suffers a workplace injury, they can lose valuable income, making it even more difficult to pay their mounting medical bills. A skilled personal injury attorney could help you file a claim for benefits if you sustained injuries while on the job. Additionally, an experienced and dedicated Dallas workers� compensation lawyer could provide legal advocacy if the insurance company denies your claim or your employer becomes uncooperative.

Workers� compensation insurance offers medical care assistance and monetary compensation for lost wages if an employee gets hurt in a worksite accident. Compensation may be used for medical expenses or funeral arrangements if the employee died. Some of the benefits that an injured employee may receive include:

- Death benefits
- Medical benefits
- Temporary total disability
- Temporary partial disability
- Permanent total disability
- Permanent partial disability

To qualify for the temporary partial disability, a worker must be unable to perform routine occupational tasks. However, this is under the assumption that they may be able to return to work once they recover.

An injured party may receive temporary total disability when their injuries reach maximum medical improvement, and they can no longer work at the capacity they did prior to their accident.�Permanent partial disability may go to workers who can still complete some of their occupational tasks but are unable to accomplish others.

Lastly, permanent total disability status occurs when medical improvement cannot happen, and an employee is unable to ever return to work. A Dallas workers� comp attorney could assess a claimant�s injuries and determine the benefits to which they may be entitled.

To file a workers� comp claim, an injured employee must complete a WC-14 form and file it with the State Board of Workers� Compensation. Their employer should receive one copy, and the company�s insurance carrier should receive another. Once an employer and their insurance company receive notice of a worker�s injury, they assess the claim and establish the benefits that they may be entitled to based on the severity of their losses. A Dallas lawyer could assist an individual in filing their workers� compensation claim.

Although an employer cannot fire a worker for receiving workers� compensation payments, Georgia is an at-will state, which means a business owner can terminate someone any time for any reason and without notice. Additionally, if an employer retaliates against an employee by giving them a negative performance review, changing their schedule without notice, or denying them a promotion after they file a workers� comp claim, this could create substantial complications. A seasoned lawyer could guide this individual through their options to take legal action.

Work-related injuries can create significant complications and stress in your life. Fortunately, a Dallas workers� compensation lawyer could help you file for benefits and work to ensure that you receive payments that cover the entirety of your losses and expenses. pages.h1: Dangerous Intersections for Car Accidents in Bremen and Carrollton
pages.content_md:
If you drive regularly in Bremen or Carrollton, you know some intersections are far riskier than others. These danger zones have seen their fair share of crashes, Whether due to high traffic volume, poor visibility, or reckless driving.

If you drive through these intersections, stay alert, knowing the risks could prevent a serious accident.

- **U.S. Highway 27 & Bankhead Highway (Carrollton)**

This busy intersection connects two major roads and sees heavy traffic all day long. With multiple lanes, vehicles turning, and drivers rushing to beat traffic lights, it’s no surprise that accidents happen here frequently.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

- High-speed traffic from U.S. 27 meets local traffic from Bankhead Highway.
- Drivers often misjudge the speed of oncoming cars while making left turns.
- Sudden lane changes and merging cause rear-end collisions.

🚦 **Safety Tip:** When making turns, wait until you have a fully clear path. If the light turns yellow, don’t rush—speeding through could lead to a T-bone accident.

- **Alabama Avenue & U.S. Highway 78 (Bremen)**

This intersection often sees fender benders and side-impact crashes, especially during rush hour. Many drivers fail to yield properly when entering U.S. 78, leading to dangerous collisions.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

- High traffic volume, especially during school and work commutes.
- Limited visibility when making turns.
- Confusion over right-of-way rules.

🚦 **Safety Tip:** Always assume the other driver might not stop. If you’re entering from Alabama Avenue, double-check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.

- **Maple Street & South Street (Carrollton, Near UWG)**

Located near the University of West Georgia, this intersection is a hotspot for student traffic. Pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles all share the road, increasing the risk of accidents.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

- Heavy pedestrian crossings.
- Distracted driving (students often use their phones while driving).
- Sudden braking due to unexpected foot traffic.

🚦 **Safety Tip:** If you’re driving here, stay extra alert for pedestrians, especially at night. For walkers and cyclists—make eye contact with drivers before crossing to ensure they see you.

- **Buchanan Street & Pacific Avenue (Bremen)**

Though smaller in scale, this intersection has seen an increase in accidents due to speeding and rolling stops.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

- Many drivers fail to come to a full stop at stop signs.
- Speeding through residential areas creates risks for nearby pedestrians and cyclists.
- Limited lighting at night makes it hard to see approaching vehicles.

🚦 **Safety Tip:** If you’re approaching a stop sign, make sure to come to a **complete stop** and check all directions before proceeding.

- **Carrollton Bypass & Newnan Road (Carrollton)**

This intersection connects a major bypass with a local road, leading to frequent crashes caused by sudden lane changes and speeding.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

- Many drivers fail to merge properly.
- Speeding from the bypass increases crash severity.
- Red-light runners cause T-bone accidents.

🚦 **Safety Tip:** If you’re merging onto the bypass, pick your lane early and stick with it—last-minute lane changes are a leading cause of crashes here.

**What to Do If You’re in an Accident at One of These Intersections**

Even if you’re a cautious driver, accidents still happen. If you find yourself in a crash at one of these locations:

- **Check for injuries**and call 911 if needed.
- **Move to safety**if the vehicle is drivable.
- **Take photos**of the accident scene, including street signs and vehicle damage.
- **Exchange information**with the other driver and any witnesses.
- **Contact a local personal injury lawyer**before speaking with insurance companies.

pages.title: Dangers on I-20, I-285, and U.S. 27 - Parian Lawyers
pages.h1: Dangers on I-20, I-285, and U.S. 27
pages.content_md:
Truck and car accidents are a major concern in Georgia, especially on high-traffic highways like Interstate 20 (I-20), Interstate 285 (I-285), and U.S. Highway 27. These roads run through Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta, making them some of the most dangerous routes for collisions involving passenger vehicles and large commercial trucks.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve seen firsthand how devastating these accidents can be. If you or a loved one has been injured in a truck or car crash, understanding the risks and legal options is crucial.

**Why Are Truck Accidents So Dangerous in Georgia?**

Truck accidents are far more severe than regular car crashes because of the size and weight of 18-wheelers. A fully loaded semi-truck can weigh 80,000 pounds, compared to a typical passenger vehicle that weighs around 4,000 pounds. This size difference leads to:

- Severe injuries like broken bones, spinal cord damage, and traumatic brain injuries.
- Longer stopping distances, making it harder for trucks to avoid sudden traffic slowdowns.
- Increased risk of jackknife accidents when truck drivers brake suddenly.
- Deadly underride collisions, where smaller cars get trapped underneath trucks.

**Most Dangerous Highways for Truck and Car Accidents in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta**

*Interstate 20 (I-20) – High-Speed Trucking Dangers*

I-20 is one of the busiest trucking routes in Georgia, connecting Bremen, Carrollton, and Atlanta to Alabama and beyond. High speeds, heavy commercial truck traffic, and frequent congestion make it a hotspot for serious crashes.

Common I-20 Accident Causes:

- Truckers speeding to meet tight delivery deadlines.
- Drowsy driving—long-haul truckers often push past legal driving limits.
- Aggressive lane changes by passenger vehicles trying to overtake slow-moving trucks.

*Interstate 285 (I-285) – The “Perimeter” Trucking Nightmare*

Known as Atlanta’s Perimeter, I-285 is a top-ranked deadly highway in the U.S. It encircles Atlanta and is heavily used by commercial trucks avoiding downtown traffic.

Why I-285 is Dangerous:

- High volume of 18-wheelers, leading to frequent truck-car collisions.
- Merging and exit confusion, especially at major interchanges.
- Rear-end crashes from stop-and-go traffic.

*U.S. Highway 27 – Rural Road Risks in Carrollton and Bremen*

U.S. 27 runs through Carrollton and Bremen, serving as a major trucking corridor for local and regional deliveries. While not as busy as the interstates, it has high truck traffic combined with rural road hazards.

**Common U.S. 27 Accident Causes:**

- Limited passing lanes, leading to risky overtaking.
- Sudden stops at traffic lights, causing rear-end collisions.
- Blind curves and rolling hills, making it difficult to see oncoming vehicles.

**Who is Liable in a Truck vs. Car Accident in Georgia?**

Determining liability in a truck accident is complex. Multiple parties may be responsible, including:

- The truck driver (for speeding, distracted driving, or fatigue).
- The trucking company (for overloading cargo or forcing drivers to work long hours).
- The truck manufacturer (for defective brakes or mechanical failures).
- Another driver (if they caused a chain-reaction crash).

Important: Georgia follows comparative fault laws, meaning if you’re partially at fault, your compensation may be reduced. That’s why having an experienced truck accident lawyer in Carrollton, Bremen, or Atlanta is crucial.

**What to Do After a Truck or Car Accident in Georgia**

If you’re in an accident with a truck, follow these steps to protect your rights:

Call 911 – Always report the accident and request medical attention.

Take Photos – Capture vehicle damage, skid marks, and road conditions.

Get Witness Statements – If anyone saw the crash, get their contact info.

Do NOT Admit Fault – Even saying “I’m sorry” can be used against you.

Call a Personal Injury Lawyer – Trucking companies have aggressive legal teams. You need an experienced truck accident attorney fighting for you.

**Why Choose Parian Lawyers for Your Truck Accident Case?**

At Parian Lawyers, we specialize in truck and car accident cases in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta. Our team understands the complexities of Georgia trucking laws, and we fight to get our clients the maximum compensation for medical bills, lost wages, and pain & suffering.

**Have You Been Injured in a Truck or Car Accident? Call Us Today!**

If you or a loved one has been in a serious truck accident, don’t wait. Contact Parian Lawyers for a free consultation.

Suffering any kind of injury can have a significant impact on a person�s life. On top of the tangible losses such as costly medical bills and lost time at work, people also suffer in a psychological way, due to pain and suffering.

Regardless of whether the injury was caused by an intentional action or happened due to an accident, the injured person has the right to seek compensation from the responsible party. Depending on the circumstances, this party can be an individual or a corporation.

DeKalb County personal injury lawyers represent injured people in their fights to obtain fair compensation for their injuries from the responsible party. By pursuing claims with both compassion and diligence, dedicated injury attorneys fight to provide plaintiffs with their best chance of success.

The vast majority of personal injury cases arise out of accidents. Because of this, Georgia law has created a framework whereby injured people can demand that the at-fault party pay for any damages that they caused. This framework is the tort known as negligence.

Regardless of the category of personal injury claim in DeKalb County that an injured person makes, it will likely be viewed through the lens of negligence. In short, negligence is when the law requires that a person protect others. When that protection fails, and another becomes hurt, the person with the responsibility can be held liable.

Examples of personal injury cases in DeKalb County that typically rely on the theory of negligence include:

- Car accidents
- Motorcycle accidents
- Slip and falls
- Premises liability
- Dog bites
- Product liability

In all of these examples, a plaintiff must prove that the defendant owed a duty to protect them and that when this duty was breached, the plaintiff came to harm. For example, in car accident cases, all motorists have a duty to protect other drivers, pedestrians, and passengers.

If a driver breaks that duty, by running a red light for example, and causes an accident, they should be liable for all of the damages that result.

One other thing to keep in mind for all civil cases is the concept of the statute of limitations. This is a law passed in Georgia that limits when a plaintiff can file a suit for personal injury.

Plaintiffs have only two years from the date of the accident to open a case in court. If this deadline passes, the court will refuse to hear the case and the plaintiff will not be able to obtain compensation. For this reason, time is of the essence.

When people are injured due to the actions of another, their world can be turned upside down. On top of the required medical treatment and associated bills, people often miss time at work and suffer mental anguish that can leave them confused and frightened. People often do not know where to turn.

DeKalb County personal injury lawyers are here to fight by your side for maximum compensation. They understand the effect that your injuries have had on your life and the right that you have to pursue damages. Take a positive step towards getting your life back to normal, contact today.

pages.h1: Do You Need a Lawyer After a Minor Car Accident in Georgia?
pages.content_md:
After a minor car accident in Georgia, many drivers are unsure whether they need legal representation.

While some accidents may seem straightforward, the decision to hire a lawyer often depends on the

circumstances and potential consequences of the crash. Understanding your rights and the legal process

can help you make the best choice for your situation.

**The Hidden Complexities of Minor Car Accidents**

What might seem like a simple “fender bender” can sometimes turn into a more complicated issue. For

example, injuries may not become apparent until days or even weeks after the accident. Soft tissue

injuries, whiplash, or even mild concussions often develop over time and can lead to medical bills and

lost wages that weren’t immediately obvious.

Additionally, minor accidents can still result in disputes with insurance companies. Insurers may

downplay the severity of the damage, offer lowball settlements, or deny claims altogether. Without

legal guidance, it can be challenging to advocate for the full compensation you deserve.

**When Should You Consult a Lawyer?**

While not every minor accident requires legal intervention, there are specific situations where

consulting a personal injury attorney is strongly recommended. If you or anyone else involved in the

accident has sustained injuries, even seemingly minor ones, an attorney can help you assess the

potential value of your claim and protect your rights. In Georgia, the comparative fault rule means your

compensation may be reduced if you are found partially responsible for the accident. A lawyer can help

gather evidence to minimize your liability. If the insurer is uncooperative or offers a settlement that

doesn’t cover your expenses, an attorney can negotiate on your behalf. Sometimes, minor accidents

lead to lingering medical issues or property damage disputes. An attorney can help you prepare for and

address these unexpected complications.

**The Benefits of Legal Representation**

Hiring a lawyer after a minor car accident can provide peace of mind and practical advantages. Attorneys

bring expertise in navigating Georgia’s personal injury laws, handling paperwork, and negotiating with

insurance companies. They also have access to resources like accident reconstruction specialists and

medical experts who can strengthen your case.

**How Georgia’s Laws Impact Your Case**

Georgia operates under a fault-based system, meaning the driver found responsible for the accident is

liable for damages. However, determining fault isn’t always straightforward, especially in minor

accidents where evidence like traffic camera footage or eyewitness accounts may be limited.

Additionally, Georgia’s statute of limitations gives accident victims two years from the date of the crash

to file a personal injury lawsuit, emphasizing the importance of acting promptly.

**Making the Decision**

Deciding whether to hire a lawyer after a minor car accident depends on your specific circumstances. If

there are no injuries, damages are minimal, and the insurance process is proceeding smoothly, you may

not need legal assistance. However, when in doubt, it’s always wise to consult an attorney for a free evaluation of your case. This initial consultation can provide clarity and ensure you’re not leaving money

on the table.

**Protect Your Rights**

Even a minor car accident can have significant consequences for your health, finances, and legal

standing. By understanding your options and seeking professional advice, you can make informed

decisions that protect your rights and future.

If you’ve been involved in a minor car accident in Georgia and have questions about your case, Parian

Lawyers is here to help. Contact us today for a free consultation.

- Cause � The plaintiff�s injuries need to have been caused by the breach of the duty of care. For example, a driver who is rear ended at a stop sign needs medical evidence to prove that the collision caused their injuries
- Scope � The injuries suffered by the plaintiff need to have been foreseeable from the facts of the case. Since even low speed car accidents can cause life-changing injuries, this element is rarely in dispute
- Damages � The plaintiff needs an actual physical harm. Other damages, such as lost wages or mental anguish can certainly be a large part of a claim, but cannot stand alone

In the eyes of the law, there are four different types of visitors to a private or public property. They are as follows:

- An invite is a person who is invited to visit the property of another person. When the property owner extends an invitation, the visitor can usually assume the owner will take reasonable steps to assure their safety
- A person who enters a property with the consent of the owner, usually as a social guest, is known as a licensee
- A welcome visitor to a property is known as a social guest
- Individuals who enter a property without any type of consent from the owner is known as a trespasser

Even if a person enters a property without the permission of the owner, they may still be able to take legal action against the owner of the property, especially if the owner could foresee individuals visiting the property. If this occurs, an injured individual should contact a Douglasville premises liability lawyer.

When a person files suit against the owner of a property, the court will examine a wide variety of factors. Property owners have a legal obligation to ensure the safety of their visitors to a reasonable extent, and if they do not, they can be held liable if a visitor is injured on their property. In such a case, the court will examine:

- The circumstances under which the injured person entered the property
- How the property is used
- Whether the accident could have been prevented or foreseen
- The extent the property owner went to in order to warn victims of any potential dangers

Laws regarding premises liability can be complex, and more than likely, injury victims will need help from a Douglasville premises liability lawyer at some point in time.

As mentioned above, premises liability laws can be complex. The court cannot always decide who is at fault, and at times, it may decide that both parties are at fault. Visitors have an obligation to ensure their own safety to a reasonable degree, and if they behave recklessly or do not exercise common sense, the court may decide they are at fault.

This is known as comparative fault, and when both parties are held liable, they may not share an equal amount of fault. Victims should consult a Douglasville premises liability attorney if they want compensation for their injuries.

If you were injured while visiting the property of another person, you will need to take legal action if you want compensation. Call a Douglasville premises liability lawyer today to discuss your case.

Most collisions between trucks and�cars are accidents. While there are absolutely examples of truckers intentionally ramming other drivers, most truck collisions are exactly that accidents. Because of this, the law allows people injured in these accidents to hold the at-fault person responsible. This is commonly done through the legal theory known as negligence. Negligence is utilized when a person is injured not through an intentional act, but rather as the result of someone acting carelessly.

There are five things that a plaintiff must be able to prove to the court�in order to�win a negligence case. They are:

- Duty ��The law sometimes places a responsibility on a person to care for the well-being of others. This is known as a duty of care.�All drivers of all vehicles always have a duty to care for other drivers, pedestrians, and passengers.�Therefore, the element of duty is always present in a truck accident case, no matter who the injured person is
- Breach ��A breach of the duty of care occurs when the person with the duty takes an action that causes a protected person to come to harm. This can be done by doing something, such as speeding, or by failing to do something,�such as not stopping at a red light. The question of whether a breach of the duty of care occurred is the most commonly contested question in truck accident cases
- Cause � The injuries need to have been caused by the breach of the duty of care. Any preexisting injury, that cannot be directly traced to the accident,�cannot be claimed.
- Scope ��The physical harm�needs�to be foreseeable from the facts of the accident. Since truck accidents can cause�serious injury or even death, most injuries suffered are within the realm of foreseeability
- Damages � The�injuries need to be based on a physical harm. Negligence cases�also�commonly�claim other damages, such as lost wages or anguish. While these are certainly valid, the case must have a foundation rooted in a physical harm

Lastly, people injured in truck accident cases should be aware of the statute of limitations. This is simply a time limit placed on plaintiffs within which they must file their case in court.

GA Code 9-3-33�gives plaintiffs two years from the date of the accident to start their lawsuit. Time is of the essence as negotiations with insurance companies can be lengthy. pages.title: Driver Fatigue and Truck Accidents: What Georgia Victims Need to Know - Parian Lawyers
pages.description: Learn how driver fatigue causes truck accidents in Georgia, how it impacts your claim, and what victims should do after a crash.
pages.h1: Driver Fatigue and Truck Accidents: What Georgia Victims Need to Know
pages.content_md:
Truck accidents are often more serious than typical car accidents, and one of the most

common—and dangerous—causes is driver fatigue.

Despite federal regulations designed to limit how long truck drivers can stay on the road,

fatigue-related accidents still happen far too often, including on major routes like Interstate 20

through Georgia.

Driving while fatigued can be just as dangerous as driving under the influence. A tired truck

driver may have slower reaction times, impaired judgment, and difficulty staying focused.

In some cases, fatigue can even lead to “microsleep”—brief moments where the driver falls

asleep without realizing it. When you’re operating a vehicle that weighs tens of thousands of

pounds, even a few seconds can have devastating consequences.

Truck drivers are subject to federal Hours of Service regulations, which limit how long they can

drive without taking breaks. These rules are designed to reduce fatigue and improve safety.

However, real-world pressures can interfere. Tight delivery schedules, long routes, and financial

incentives may push drivers to stay on the road longer than they should. In some cases,

logbooks may be inaccurate or manipulated.

When driver fatigue is a factor, a truck accident case can become more complex—but also

potentially stronger. Unlike a typical car accident, truck accident claims often involve multiple parties. In addition to the driver, the trucking company may be responsible for unrealistic scheduling, poor oversight, or failing to enforce safety regulations.

Evidence in these cases may include driver logs, electronic logging device (ELD) data, dispatch

records, and even company policies. This type of evidence can be critical in showing that fatigue

played a role in the crash.

While it’s not always obvious at the scene, certain details can point to driver fatigue. Accidents

that occur late at night or in the early morning hours are more likely to involve drowsy driving.

Crashes where there was no attempt to brake or avoid impact can also be a red flag.

Because this evidence can be lost or overwritten, it’s important to act quickly if you suspect

fatigue may have contributed to the accident.

Truck accident cases are rarely straightforward. When fatigue is involved, it raises important

questions about responsibility—not just for the driver, but for the company behind them.

Understanding what happened requires a thorough investigation and access to records that

aren’t always easy to obtain.

If you’ve been involved in a truck accident in Georgia, it’s important to take the situation

seriously from the start. These cases often involve severe injuries, significant damages, and

aggressive insurance defense.

Taking early steps to preserve evidence and understand your legal options can make a

meaningful difference in the outcome of your case.

In Griffin, many car wrecks happen on highways and roadways. One of the most common types of car accidents is a rear-end collision. These crashes may occur at traffic intersections or on the highway in stop-and-go traffic.

Although rear-end impacts are not always forceful, they could cause the driver who is rear-ended to move violently in the car. Moreover, they may cause the driver�s head to strike the steering wheel or headrest, potentially causing serious head injuries and soft tissue neck and back injuries.

Other car accidents may involve head-on collisions. These accidents may occur when a driver crosses a median strip, a solid yellow line, or a white line on the roadway. Additionally, such accidents may occur at high speeds and could also result in significant injuries, damages, and even death.

In cases where an automobile driver violates a statute listed in the Official Code of Georgia Annotated � 40-6-1 through 40-6-397, the driver may be deemed �per se negligent.� Under this theory, liability may only need to be proven by demonstrating that the defendant violated a law, such as by speeding or running a red light.

This threshold of proof is typically lower than proving negligence by breach of the �standard of duty,� which is the failure to show a reasonable amount of consideration and care to other drivers. An injured party may be able to bring a claim under the theory of per se negligence, which could allow them to recover damages if they can prove the other party violated a law.

To obtain financial recovery for damages, the accident complainant typically must have sustained injuries as a direct result of the violated statutes. A person may also be able to recover damages if the accident worsens a preexisting condition or illness. In this instance, the testimony of a medical expert may be advantageous as they could help confirm and demonstrate the potentially deteriorated health of the complainant.

If a case is not brought under the theory of per se negligence, a complainant could potentially demonstrate that the other driver breached the standard of care under the standard theory of negligence. This could mean the other driver acted unreasonably under the circumstances of the collision by failing to do something that a reasonable person may have done. Additionally, it could refer to when another driver acted in a way that a reasonable person typically would not in an accident.

Under this theory, to show the other driver was at fault for the accident, the complainant’s injuries must generally have resulted directly from the crash. It may also need to be proven that the other driver breached the duty of care and caused the collision for a claim to succeed in court. pages.content_md:
Large trucks can be regularly seen on American highways, and most truck drivers are very responsible and take the safety of others very seriously. Unfortunately, a minority of truck drivers and trucking companies do not prioritize safety and only care about saving time and money.

If you or someone you care about was hurt in a wreck involving a tractor-trailer or any other kind of commercial truck, it may be smart to hire a Griffin truck accident lawyer to help sue the driver and their employer for damages. Depending on the nature of your case, you may be entitled to payments for medical bills, lost wages, and general pain and suffering. Call today and set up a consultation with a skilled personal injury attorney.

Large trucks may pose a special threat to other drivers on the road. On top of their massive sizes, these vehicles also have a much longer stopping distance and larger blind spot than smaller vehicles. As a result, car wrecks involving trucks tend to be more devastating than crashes which do not.

Large trucks may be prone to jackknifing as well, which happens when a truck stops suddenly, causing its cab and trailer to turn in different directions. Trucks are especially prone to jackknifing on slippery surfaces and during bad weather.

Turning accidents may common with large vehicles as well, especially tractor-trailers. Despite their large sizes, trucks should never use more than one lane on the road to turn. When trucks occupy multiple lanes, they may accidentally swerve into another car�s path. Finally, trucks that carry flammable cargo could have that cargo ignite if they collide with another vehicle.

When a truck crash occurs, it may be tempting to place all the blame on the driver of the truck. In reality, accident survivors could be able to seek compensation from multiple parties with the help of an experienced Griffin truck accident attorney.

Trucking companies generally have a responsibility to hire only the most qualified and safe drivers. Before allowing a truck driver behind the wheel of one of their vehicles, trucking companies typically should be sure they have the experience necessary to operate such a large truck. Drivers with multiple safety violations on their record and drivers with an insufficient amount of knowledge may not be the best candidates to drive commercial trucks.

It is generally the responsibility of the trucking company to regularly inspect their trucks and hire experienced cargo loaders. Finally, if a truck crashes due to a mechanical error, crash survivors may be able to hold the maker of the truck or its mechanic accountable in court.

After a serious truck wreck, crash victims may have to deal with the insurance company. This can be difficult to manage without help from a seasoned lawyer since insurance companies may only be interested in getting their client off the hook for their actions and not giving fair treatment to crash victims.

Often, insurance companies might try to prove the victim in a truck crash is the one responsible for the accident by using any available evidence to avoid paying out fair compensation. If a crash victim elects to represent themselves, they may find themselves overwhelmed because the trucking company would more than likely have a team of lawyers and insurance representatives to work with.

If you are currently recovering from injuries you suffered in an accident a truck driver caused, the concept of hiring an attorney and going after a trucking company for damages may be the last thing on your mind.
