pages.title: Griffin Wrongful Death Lawyer | Negligent Death Claims
pages.description: If you have suffered the loss of a loved one due to the negligence of another, get in contact with a Griffin wrongful death lawyer for help in your case.
pages.content_md:
One of life�s worst possible tragedies is when a loved one dies in a tragic accident. Certainly, it is a life-altering event. There is typically a heavy burden of emotions, as well as financial stressors. In the state of Georgia, a wrongful death claim can arise when a loved one is killed in an accident which resulted from another person�s negligence.

Under Georgia law, a wrongful death claim seeks damages equal in value to the life of the deceased. Without a doubt, however, the loss of a loved one cannot be measured monetarily.

No matter the intent of the wrongdoer, survivors have the right to seek a certain degree of justice. If you have lost a loved one in a tragic accident, Griffin wrongful death lawyers are here for you during this extremely difficult time. Experienced wrongful death lawyers will zealously fight for your interests, to hold the wrongdoer accountable for their conduct and/or failures.

An important legal principle for wrongful death cases is called the statute of limitations. It governs how long a person has to bring legal action against another. Under Georgia law, loved ones have two years from the time of death to bring a wrongful death lawsuit. However, individuals should not wait too long to file an action in the interests of preserving evidence, so the sooner they engage a Griffin wrongful death attorney, the better.

Who can file a wrongful death lawsuit depends on who the survivors are. Georgia law establishes a hierarchy that determines who may sue for the death of a loved one. If the decedent had a spouse, then the spouse can sue for wrongful death. When compensation is received, the spouse is required to share the amounts received with the children, in accordance with state law. The spouse would receive one-third of the payment, and the children would split the remaining two-thirds.

If the decedent did not have a spouse, then the decedent�s children would have the right to bring an action for wrongful death. The children would share any award received equally. If the decedent had no spouse, nor children, then the decedent�s parents could file a claim. Should there be no spouse, children, nor parents, then the decedent�s estate would have the right to bring a wrongful death action. The estate would hold the award for the next of kin, pursuant to Georgia state law.

All states permit the filing of a wrongful death lawsuit by the family of the decedent, in the event of a wrongdoer�s negligence causing a death. Factors courts consider when they are reviewing a wrongful death case include the following:

- Loss of companionship
- Extent that survivors were financially dependent on the deceased
- Amounts the decedent earned
- Savings of the deceased
- Expenses borne by the decedent�s survivors
- Medical and funeral costs
- Future potential earnings of decedent

Obviously, there is no amount of money that could ever compensate for the loss of a loved one. Some peace of mind, however, may be experienced by family members when the responsible party is held accountable, and there is some financial security presented by a wrongful death action in Griffin.

Serious accidents occur every single day. Sadly, at times these accidents can be tragic, where another is negligent to the extent of causing the death of a loved one. Griffin wrongful death lawyers fully understand the extreme difficulties you face.

Skilled lawyers are compassionate, and they are prepared to diligently battle for you and your case. Call today for a free consultation.

pages.title: Halloween Safety in Carrollton and Bremen: Keeping the Night Fun and Injury-Free - Parian Lawyers
pages.h1: Halloween Safety in Carrollton and Bremen: Keeping the Night Fun and Injury-Free
pages.content_md:
Halloween in West Georgia is a special time. Families decorate their homes, kids put on costumes, and

neighborhoods come alive after dark. But behind the fun, it’s also one of the busiest nights of the year

for emergency rooms and police departments. More foot traffic, darker evenings, and distracted drivers

can easily turn a fun night into a dangerous one.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve seen firsthand how quickly accidents can happen, especially when drivers and

pedestrians aren’t paying attention. The biggest risks on Halloween usually come from visibility and

traffic. As the sun goes down, it becomes harder for drivers to see kids walking between parked cars or

crossing the street. If you’ll be out trick-or-treating around Carrollton or Bremen, make sure your kids

wear something bright or reflective and carry a flashlight or glow stick. Stick to sidewalks whenever

possible and cross only at corners or marked crosswalks.

Drivers also have to do their part. Slow down in neighborhoods, stay off your phone, and expect children

to run out unexpectedly. Traffic tends to pick up between 5:30 and 9:30 p.m. as families head to events

or rush home from work, so a little extra patience can go a long way.

Homeowners should take a few minutes to make sure their property is safe before the night begins.

Clear walkways, check for tripping hazards, and keep your porch well-lit. Replace real candles with

battery-powered ones, and make sure pets are kept inside. A simple safety check can prevent a serious

fall or other injury—and may protect you from a premises liability issue later on.

If you’re looking for safe, family-friendly events this year, Carrollton is hosting Trick-or-Treat Downtown

on October 25th and The Great Pumpkin Movie Night at The Amp on October 27th. Bremen families can

find several trunk-or-treats at local churches and schools, which provide a safer alternative to going door

to door.

Halloween should be about fun, not fear. But if you or your child is injured due to someone else’s

negligence, whether it’s a distracted driver, unsafe property, or another preventable situation, our team

at Parian Lawyers is here to help. We’ve represented injury victims throughout West Georgia and know

how to protect your rights when things go wrong.

If you need help after a Halloween accident, call Parian Lawyers today.

pages.title: Haralson County Criminal Defense Lawyer | Accused of a Crime
pages.description: A Haralson County criminal defense lawyer could help you prepare for trial if you have been accused of a crime.
pages.content_md:
The Parian Law Firm, LLC has lawyers on the ground to represent criminal defendants in this area. We have the experience and skill to get the bet outcome possible for your case. If you have been charged with a crime, contact our Haralson County criminal defense lawyers today. We have represented clients facing all kinds of criminal charges. Whatever the criminal offense, we could work tirelessly to develop a defense for your case. Contact our offices today for a free, no obligation case evaluation.

The criminal justice system is almost the same across the states. There are certain differences in how the judicial system processes and proceeds with criminal defendants. It can be overwhelming to deal with if you are not represented by an experienced criminal defense attorney in Haralson County. The Parian Law Firm, LLC has the experience in criminal law and is ready to fight for your rights every step of the way.

Arrest � In Georgia, you can be arrested with or without a warrant. Being arrested is scary even for the most emotionally hardened people. You do have rights though. Don�t forget that!

Preliminary Hearing � This is your first appearance in Court after your arrest. The Court looks at the evidence against you and decides whether there is enough to force you to stand trial for what you have been charged. An experienced Haralson County attorney knows what to look for to fight for dismissal at this stage in the criminal defense process.

Bond � Simply put, your bail is set by the Court. This is the amount you must pay to be released from jail. Your �bond� is the percentage an outside bondsman requires to pay the remainder of the money to get you out of jail. They sometimes require cash or a piece of collateral, such as your house or car.

Arraignment � This usually marks the start of someone�s court case after his or her arrest. It is sometimes called an initial hearing or appearance. Arraignment and what is said during arraignment can be the most important words out of an accused�s mouth.

Discovery Motions � Discovery is the legal term for getting all the evidence the other side has against you. Georgia law is clear that prosecutors cannot use ambush tactics to convict a person of a crime. They must hand over all the evidence they intend to use to try to convict you of the crime they contend you committed.

Bench Trial � This is a type of trial where the Judge decides your case. Under the United States Constitution, you have the right to a jury trial, but sometimes it can help to fight for a bench trial instead. This is not an easy decision. Only an experienced criminal defense lawyer can help with this.

Jury Trial � You have the right to a jury trial under the 7th Amendment of the United States Constitution. A jury is a group of people from the community in which you live.

Plea Bargain � This is an agreement between the accused defendant and the prosecutor. You should definitely consult an experienced criminal defense attorney before agreeing to a plea bargain. They usually have lots of strings attached.

Our lawyers know Haralson County. We are local. Contact our Haralson County criminal defense lawyer today if you are accused of a crime.

pages.title: Haralson County DUI Lawyer | Drunk Driving Attorney
pages.description: If you have been accused of driving under the influence, speak with a Haralson County DUI lawyer to discuss your case.
pages.content_md:
In�Haralson County, DUI laws are governed by OCGA � 40-6-391, and similar sections of state code. It is important to know about these laws, as they were recently altered to reflect the current legislative changes that were passed. To properly understand your rights when meeting with a Haralson County DUI lawyer after you have been charged with drunk driving, you should go over these code sections to see what violations could apply to your situation and what penalties could be issued. Our defense�attorneys�could guide you through what sections of the law in our state apply to your situation.

If a driver is over the age of 21, it is illegal to operate any type of motor vehicle even if your blood alcohol content is less than 0.08%. This is known as DUI Less Safe. This includes personally owned vehicles, work vehicles, and small vehicles, such as mopeds and the like. If a driver is under 21, under OCGA � 40-6-391 they may be charged with Driving under the influence (DUI Per Se) if the driver�s blood alcohol content is greater than 0.02%. Upon conviction, the driver will be guilty of a misdemeanor for the first and second convictions. Upon a third or subsequent conviction a driver will be guilty of a high and aggravated misdemeanor.

Under OCGA 40-6-391(i), commercial drivers can be charged with DUI for a blood alcohol content of 0.04% or higher. It is important to remember a commercial driver can still be charged with DUI Less Safe if the commercial driver�s blood alcohol content was under 0.04%. A lawyer in Haralson County could help someone who has been charged with DUI.

Our Haralson County attorney could help you understand the potential penalties that you could be facing after you are stopped and given a DUI. These penalties change depending on the number of similar or related offenses that you have been convicted of in the past. When you are first charged with a DUI, you could be given both a fine and time in jail. However, the fine cannot be less than $300 and cannot exceed the amount of $1,000, and the term in jail not less than 10 days cannot exceed 12 months. The judge hearing your case is allowed under OCGA 40-6-391(1)(B) to suspend imprisonment, stay imprisonment, or allow the driver to serve the time on probation instead of imprisonment. It is important to note that under OCGA 40-6-391(c)(1)(B), if the driver�s blood alcohol concentration at the time of the offense was 0.08 grams or more, 24 hours of imprisonment will be imposed.

If a lawyer is working with you after a second offense DUI in the Haralson County area, �you should know that you could face a fine that is between $600 and $1,000. OCGA 40-6-391(g)(1) allows for installment payments if the fine will impose an economic hardship on the convicted driver. Additionally, the judge has discretion to suspend up to half of the fine if the convicted driver undergoes (and completes) a substance abuse treatment program.

Under OCGA 40-6-391(c)(2)(B), the imprisonment for a second conviction of driving under the influence is a period not less than 90 days and cannot exceed more than 12 months. The judge must probate a period of the term of imprisonment – the minimum period of imprisonment, however, will not be fewer than 72 hours of actual incarceration. Additional penalties include: not fewer than 30 days of community service; completion of DUI Alcohol or Drug Use Risk Reduction Program within 120 days following a driver�s conviction. If the driver has been incarcerated and unable to complete the program within 120 days following the date of their conviction, the driver has 90 days from the date of release from custody to complete the program.

A third conviction for DUI within a ten-year period (from date of convictions or pleas of solo contendere) carries:

- a fine of no less than $1,000 and cannot exceed $5,000 (unless economic hardship will be imposed)
- Mandatory 120 days imprisonment but cannot exceed 12 months. The judge is required to probate a part of the term of imprisonment, however, the convicted driver will be required to serve no fewer than 15 days imprisoned.
- At least 30 days of community service
- Completion of DUI Alcohol or Drug Use Risk Reduction Program within 120 days following a driver�s conviction. If the driver has been incarcerated and unable to complete the program within 120 days following the date of their conviction, the driver has 90 days from the date of release from custody to complete the program.

A driver convicted of a fourth or subsequent conviction with a 10-year period of time under OCGA 40-6-391(c)(4) faces punishment consisting of:

- A fine not less than $1,000 and not to exceed $5,000 (unless economic hardship imposed as noted above) and cannot be suspended, stayed or probated;
- Imprisonment not less than 1 year and not to exceed 5 years- However, the judge MAY suspend, stay or probate all but 90 days of the term of imprisonment
- The judge is required to probate at least a portion of the term of imprisonment;
 
- At least 60 days of community service (exception: if the convicted driver is sentenced to an imprisonment term of 3 years, the judge is allowed to suspend the 60 days community service – not required.
- Completion of DUI Alcohol or Drug Use Risk Reduction Program within 120 days following a driver�s conviction – if the driver has been incarcerated and unable to complete the program within 120 days following the date of their conviction, the driver has 90 days from the date of release from custody to complete the program; a clinical evaluation and potential completion of a substance abuse treatment program.
- Probation for 5 years (convicted driver to receive credit for days the convicted driver is actually imprisoned).

Driving under the influence can plague you for years to come. Always remember, you are innocent until proven guilty. Just because you are arrested for driving under the influence does not mean you will be found guilty in a court of law. Our law firm understands and fights for this every day. We outwork the prosecution by attention to detail from day one. It can be the difference between a life of continued issues with insurance and employers using a DUI conviction as a millstone around your neck or you hire capable, hardworking counsel to defend you and protect your liberty.

Our Haralson County DUI lawyers have the experience you need to defend against drunk driving charges. Let us protect your constitutional rights. Call us today. One of our lawyers could review your case and advise you on what steps you need to take going forward.

pages.title: Henry County Personal Injury Lawyer | Negligent Accident Attorney
pages.description: If you have suffered injuries due to the negligence of another, contact a Henry County personal injury lawyer for help pursuing damages.
pages.content_md:
Becoming injured due to the intentional acts or negligence of another person is never easy. First, there is the rest and recovery you need to get back to physical and mental health. Unfortunately, mounting medical bills, lost time at work and accumulating paperwork make this recovery process difficult.

On top of that, the insurance companies, the very people who are supposed to make the process easier, can delay your claim with drawn out investigations and misdirection.

Henry County personal injury lawyers fight by your side to get you the compensation that you deserve. Compassionate injury attorneys deal with the details from the insurance companies so that you can focus on getting your life back on track.

Personal injury claims are not defined by the legislature of the state of Alabama. While the underlying act that leads to the claim may be punishable by the criminal code, such as in cases of assault or drunk driving, any civil action that arises out of these acts will be governed by the common law.

Simply put, the common law is a collection of court decisions handed down over the years. Since courts are required to follow past precedent, people can extrapolate legal patterns from these decisions.

One of the most utilized torts extrapolated from common law is the theory of negligence. Since most personal injuries come about from acts that would be considered accidents, the law gives injured people a route to recover damages using negligence.

A person is considered to be negligent if they have a legal duty to protect another person, and by breaking that duty, the protected person comes to harm. Examples of cases that utilize negligence theory include:

- Car Accidents
- Truck Accidents
- Slip and Falls
- Motorcycle Accidents

However, there are a number of other personal injury cases in Henry County that do not rely on the defendant being negligent. Most often, these cases involve personal injury that results from an intentional act.

For example, if a person is assaulted and needs to go to the hospital, they may sue the assailant for medical costs as well as pain and suffering. While assault is a crime under Alabama law, only the District Attorney can pursue a criminal case.

Regardless of the outcome of any criminal proceedings, or even if a criminal charge is never filed, an injured party retains the right to initiate a civil claim and work with a Henry County personal injury attorney. Criminal cases and civil cases are always separate, even if the underlying facts are identical.

One other aspect of the law that all potential plaintiffs should keep in mind is the statute of limitations. The Alabama legislature has enacted a law placing time limits on civil claims involving personal injury.

According to AL Code 6-2-38(l), all civil claims alleging personal injury must be filed within two years of the incident. If more than two years have passed since the injury, a plaintiff�s case will be barred and no recovery will be possible.

Whether you have been injured in a car accident, truck accident, slip and fall, or by a violent act, skilled attorneys are available to help you fight for the fair compensation you deserve. Regardless of the circumstances in which you became injured, if it is someone else�s fault, they may be liable for damages.

Henry County personal injury lawyers will analyze your case, determine if another person is responsible for your injuries, and pursue your case with diligence and vigor.

By gathering all of the evidence, consulting with experts, and forming strong demand packages, many of cases settle without ever going to court.

However, if a trial is necessary, skilled litigators will guide you every step of the way. Do not let the insurance companies intimidate you into settling for a token sum; contact Henry County personal injury attorneys today to see how they can aid in your fight for fair compensation.

pages.title: Henry County Bicycle Accident Lawyer | Bike Crash Injuries
pages.description: If you were hit by a car while riding your bike, you may be entitled to compensation. Reach out to a Henry County bicycle accident lawyer for help.
pages.content_md:
Many Henry County residents find bicycling to be an enjoyable method of transportation. However, it can become dangerous if other drivers fail to properly share the road. A cyclist may suffer broken bones, fractures, or devastating spinal injuries when they hit by a car.

Although bike crashes are usually not the cyclist�s fault, it is possible they may have played a minor role�or more likely, that a defendant or their insurance company may attempt to shift blame towards the victim. Fortunately, a proactive personal injury attorney may be able to help protect you from this in your case. Talk to a Henry County bicycle accident lawyer today to get help fighting for compensation and pursuing a positive outcome.

Usually, a successful bicycle accident claim centers around the theory of negligence, which establishes that everyone legally owes a duty of care to reasonably protect other people around them and, if they fail to do so, could be held liable for any injuries that result. For example, if a driver looks at their cell phone rather than the road ahead, that driver could be breaching their reasonable duty of care to pay attention and ensure they do not hit other drivers�or, in this case, bicyclists.

Generally, a plaintiff in a bike wreck case must show that this failure�or breach of duty�was the direct cause of any harm sustained. In these cases, the driver may be required to pay damages for harm such as physical injuries or property damage. An experienced bike crash attorney in Henry County could explain how a driver�s actions may or may not qualify as legal negligence.

When it comes to bike crashes, multiple parties order soma online prescription could share fault depending on the circumstances. If a driver struck a cyclist and gets accused of negligence, they or their lawyer may argue that the accident was at least partially due to the bicyclist�s negligent behavior.

If the court finds that a cyclist�s actions partially caused an accident, the bicyclist may be held liable as well. This rule, called comparative negligence, could alter the compensation an injured bike rider could receive.

The amount recoverable is typically reduced by the percentage of fault attributed to the accident victim�so, for example, someone found 20 percent at fault for their own wreck could recover 80 percent of their total damages at most. However, if a plaintiff is found to be 50 percent or more responsible for an accident, they may be unable to recover any money at all.

If liability is proven, an injured bicyclist may be entitled to recover monetary damages for various injuries and losses. Experienced Henry County bike accident lawyers may help plaintiffs seek recovery for economic losses like medical bills, lost wages, or damaged property, as well as for more intangible harms like emotional stress or pain and suffering.

If you are struck by a car while riding your bike, your first priority should be a full physical recovery. Often, entering a lawsuit may be your last thought. However, a Henry County bicycle accident lawyer may be able to help you explore your options and minimize stress over complicated legal matters.

A knowledgeable attorney could evaluate your situation, work to collect evidence on your behalf, and help protect you against unfounded claims of partial negligence. Reach out today to get started on your case.

pages.title: Henry County Boat Accident Lawyer | Martime Injuries
pages.description: Speak to a Henry County boat accident lawyer if you suffered injuries due to a martime accident. An attorney could fight diligently on your behalf.
pages.content_md:
Boat drivers have a legal duty to maneuver their watercraft in a manner that ensures the safety of themselves and others on the water. Boating could become dangerous when boat operators do not take necessary precautions.

When boaters fail to meet the standard of care applicable to them, it may result in a boat wreck that causes severe injury or even death. You may be able to recover financially with a Henry County boat accident lawyer�s help. If you have been involved in an accident on the water, a seasoned personal injury attorney could help you meet your legal needs.

There are a few consistent reasons boating accidents occur. Equipment failure is a common culprit, typically either due to defective parts or a failure by the boat operator to maintain the watercraft. Reckless behavior and inexperience on the part of operators could play a significant role in causing boat accidents.

Boaters who consume excessive amounts of alcohol or use drugs illegally are typically more prone to accidents than sober operators, as are those who engage in excessive horseplay on a boat. In the same vein, some boat operators are inexperienced and may not even be aware of basic safety rules for traversing waterways in Georgia.

While there are many potential causes for a boating accident, negligence is the most common legal basis for a personal injury lawsuit related to one. Similar to operators of motor vehicles, operators of boats and water-crafts have a duty to handle their vessels in a way that protects the safety of others.

Boaters could breach this duty when they operate boats in a reckless or careless manner, increasing the likelihood of accidents and injuries. A knowledgeable boat accident attorney in Henry County could help identify if negligence occurred and proceed with a potential case accordingly.

Damages that are available after a boating wreck in Henry County may differ based on the severity and nature of the accident. Recoverable damages might include but are not necessarily limited to:

- Medical, surgical, and hospital expenses
- Lost wages
- Personal property damage
- Pain and suffering

There are potential time limits on filing this type of action. Official Code of Georgia � 9-3-33 states that injured individuals must file a personal injury claim within two years of the date of the accident which led to their injury.

There are exceptions to these rules for actions involving minors and individuals who are legally incompetent. Failing to abide by this statute of limitations could leave a plaintiff unable to recover any damages whatsoever, a risk which further underscores the critical role a Henry County boat accident lawyer could play in preparing and filing a case.

Injuries sustained in a boat accident could be severe and in some cases even life-altering. When these damages result from the negligence of a boat driver, plaintiffs may be entitled to compensation for their losses.

An experienced Henry County boat accident lawyer could assist you in determining your legal rights. Call today to find out how you may be able to recover damages to help you move past the accident and on with your life.

pages.title: Henry County Bus Accident Lawyer | Public Transit Injuries

pages.content_md:
Bus accidents in Henry County can lead to serious injuries for riders, pedestrians, and other drivers alike. If you are involved in a bus wreck, your focus should be on healing, but this can be difficult to prioritize over dealing with medical bills, insurance companies, and financial stress.

A Henry County bus accident lawyer could help protect your legal rights. Securing an experienced legal representative gives you access to a knowledgeable ally who could work to examine your case and help mount a proactive claim for damages on your behalf.

Bus accidents and any resulting claims can be very complicated, especially since buses are rarely owned or operated by the driver involved in the crash. The bus in question may be owned by a private company or operated by a government entity, either of which may bear some legal liability for a crash. Many different parties can be involved�and injured�in a bus accident as well, including but not limited to:

- Passengers riding the bus
- Passengers riding in other vehicles involved with the crash
- Pedestrians or bicyclists struck by the bus
- Passengers injured while entering or exiting the bus

The standards for fault in bus accidents could differ depending on the circumstances surrounding a crash. For example, special rules and statutes of limitations may apply to crashes involving government-operated buses. For this reason, it may benefit anyone involved in a Henry County bus crash to contact an attorney as soon as possible afterwards.

If the negligence of another party directly causes a bus accident, that party may be required to pay monetary damages to victims for the harm they suffered. These damages are generally broken into two categories: economic and non-economic.

Economic damages can help offset objective losses that have an established dollar value, such as medical bills or lost wages. A thorough attorney may also be able to help estimate future costs for things like therapy or lost earning potential. Additionally, damages may also be awarded for non-economic harm. These damages could help compensate for intangible suffering such as pain and distress.

Physical injuries suffered in a bus accident can be severe, and even minor injuries could lead to long-term consequences. For this reason, people involved in crashes should always immediately seek a medical evaluation and treatment for any immediate injuries. If a bus wreck lawyer in Henry County advises filing a claim, medical reports from physicians and other test results could provide additional evidence to help build a strong claim.

Healing can be difficult if you are worried about bills, struggling to understand insurance claims, or concerned about your future or that of your family. In these instances, seeking a legal representative may be the best move you could make.

When you work with a knowledgeable Henry County bus accident lawyer, your attorney could handle questions and negotiations on your behalf to help you pursue the full amount to which you may be entitled. Reach out today to schedule a free consultation and start discussing your potential claim.

pages.title: Henry County Car Accident Lawyer | Recovery and Compensation
pages.description: If you have been in a car wreck, contact a Henry County car accident lawyer so you could receive the recovery and compensation you deserve.
pages.content_md:
As frequently as most people get behind the wheel, they rarely do much to actively prevent car accidents. While buckling your seatbelt and driving defensively are always good practices, so much of what can be done to prevent a collision is done instinctually. You may not realize how dangerous driving can actually be until you find yourself in a wreck�especially if that wreck is someone else�s fault.

For those walking away from car accidents with serious damage to their vehicle and serious injuries, the future can seem hazy. By working with a Henry County car accident lawyer, the troubles of today can be addressed by tomorrow�s actions. Schedule a confidential consultation with a compassionate attorney to begin planning for your future, establishing your rights, and seeking compensation from negligent drivers.

There are more causes for distractions behind the wheel than ever before. With society�s reliance upon cell phones, it is no surprise that some drivers brush off warnings about distracted driving, opting instead to chat, text, and check notifications. Even when motorists leave their phones alone, the radio they are listening to, the passenger they are chatting with, or the burger they are munching on can all create very real distractions.

Distracted driving is just one of the most common causes of car wrecks. Drunk drivers and motorists under the influence of drugs are also frequently to blame for serious accidents. Like distracted drivers, drunk drivers may struggle to pay attention to the road and can find themselves braking moments too late. In extreme cases, drunk drivers may even inadvertently travel in the wrong direction on a road and collide head-on with another vehicle.

Speed, malfunctioning vehicles, and drowsiness are other contributing factors that are frequently cited in accident reports. Ultimately, however, most accidents have one thing in common: a driver at the wheel who acts recklessly or negligently. When other motorists and passengers are hurt because of such behavior, they may be entitled to compensation.

Car crashes can result in serious financial damage, not to mention the physical and emotional pain often endured by victims. Though car insurance may cover some of the damages, companies sometimes look for any reason not to pay a claim. In such cases, a Henry County car accident attorney can go to bat for victims�and, if negotiations are unsuccessful, file a lawsuit on their behalf.

Car accident settlements may result in significant compensation for victims. Medical bills, lost wages, and reimbursement for the emotional pain experienced by those injured in the wreck can all be factored into a settlement. In the event of a catastrophic injury, victims who can no longer hold down a steady job may even receive compensation for their loss of earning capacity.

Get the help you need for your car crash case by calling a Henry County car accident lawyer. By hiring an attorney, you could recruit a tireless ally who could advocate for your needs with skill and compassion. Ensure your rights are protected by scheduling a confidential consultation as soon as possible to see what options may be available to you.

pages.title: Henry County Catastrophic Injury Lawyer | Life-Altering Accidents
pages.description: If you were severely injured in an accident, speak with a Henry County catastrophic injury lawyer about your eligibility for compensation.
pages.content_md:
Accidents can lead to a wide range of injuries, some of which are severe in nature. These so-called �catastrophic injuries� tend to be more painful, expensive, and permanent than other damages. Often, these injuries are due to the reckless or careless behavior of someone else.

If you or a loved one has suffered catastrophic injuries due to the negligence of another, a compassionate Henry County catastrophic injury lawyer may be able to help you pursue a personal injury claim. In addition to identifying liable parties, a personal injury attorney could help take stock of and pursue recovery for all your short and long-term damages.

Catastrophic injuries like severely broken or shattered bones, third-degree burns, amputations of limbs, spinal cord injuries, and traumatic brain injuries can arise from numerous circumstances. Some of these incidents could result in a personal injury claim, especially those that result from motor vehicle accidents, construction site accidents, defective products, or medical mistakes.

Most personal injury claims stem from the reckless actions of another resulting in an accident. This scenario, known in legal terms as negligence, occurs when individuals fail to act in a reasonable manner with respect to the safety of others. Georgia state law measures negligence in relation to an accident according to what a reasonable person would do in the same or similar circumstances.

Sometimes, injury victims contribute in part to the accident that leads to their injuries. Georgia is a modified comparative negligence state, meaning injury victims who are less than 50 percent responsible for the accidents that led to their injuries still have the right to seek compensation from other parties.

However, a partially liable plaintiff would still have their recoverable damages reduced in proportion to the percentage of fault they personally bear. The nuances of Georgia�s modified comparative negligence pursuant to Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33 can be difficult to follow, but a dedicated Henry County catastrophic injury attorney can help an injured individual navigate its intricacies.

Under O.C.G.A. � 9-3-33, injury victims generally have deadlines for filing personal injury actions. To ensure their case remains valid in the eyes of the court, victims must file these claims within two years of the date that they sustained their injuries. There are only a few exceptions to this rule, and failing to meet this deadline might prohibit individuals from pursuing claims related to their accident damages.

Victims of catastrophic injuries often struggle to recover and may lose focus on seeking compensation for their losses when faced with paying medical bills and covering day-to-day expenses and challenges. To further complicate matters, the insurance company for the responsible party typically reaches out quickly to the injured party after an accident and may try to make a profit by not offering adequate compensation or avoiding paying out altogether.

If an injured individual is unaware of these tactics, they may inadvertently settle for a fraction of what they may actually be owed. A catastrophic injury lawyer in Henry County could work to ensure an accident victim receive adequate compensation for all their damages.

Catastrophic injuries can be devastating to all aspects of your life. Lost wages, medical expenses, and pain and suffering are only some of the potential costs that you might incur when you suffer severe harm due to the negligence of someone else.

Gathering evidence, dealing with insurance companies, and trying to keep up with unexpected bills can be stressful, particularly as you attempt to recover from serious injuries. Fortunately, a dedicated Henry County catastrophic injury lawyer could help you build a strong personal claim that could allow you to recover your damages. Call today to learn more about what may be possible in your case.

pages.title: Henry County Burn Injury Lawyer | Third-Degree Burn Injuries
pages.description: Reach out to a Henry County burn injury lawyer if you suffered injuries at the hands of a negligent or reckless individual. An attorney could represent you.
pages.content_md:
Burns are one of the most catastrophic forms of personal injuries, often causing a high level of pain and requiring extensive recovery time. The careless behavior of others could easily lead to accidents that result in severe or permanent burn damages which impair your quality of life.

If the reckless or careless actions of others have caused your burn injuries, you may have a claim against those individuals for compensation that a Henry County burn injury lawyer could help you pursue. A personal injury attorney may be able to assess the facts and circumstances surrounding your injuries and evaluate the viability of any personal injury claim you may have.

Burns can stem from a variety of sources, with scalding from fire or hot liquid being the most common. Other forms of burn injuries could include thermal burns from an oven, chemical burns from toxic spills, and electrical burns from defective or malfunctioning products.

Burns also have varying degrees of severity that lead to different types of damage. First-degree burns �cause damage to the outer layer of skin only, while second-degree burns cause damage to the top layer of skin and below it, often producing blisters and redness. Third-degree burns, the most severe type, affect all layers of skins and can even affect internal organs and bones, often resulting in permanent damage and necessitating skin graft surgeries.

All burns carry a high risk of infection, and certain burn injuries have a high chance of causing emotional distress and mental health conditions. A burn injury lawyer in�Henry County could be able to recognize the probability and severity of different damages and determine what a plaintiff could potentially recover for through civil means.

Negligence is the legal standard that forms the basis for most personal injury claims. To prove negligence, injury plaintiffs must establish:

- The actors owed a duty of reasonable care to the plaintiffs
- The actors breached that duty of care or failed to live up to the standard expected of them
- The breach of care proximately caused injury to the plaintiffs
- The injuries suffered by the victim merit compensation

In some cases, the establishment of negligence is straightforward. Drivers owe a duty of care to others on the roadway. If they break a traffic law and cause an accident that results in burn injuries to another, they could be held liable for the costs of those injuries due to their negligence.

Establishing negligence is not always simple, however, notably if there is more than one potential party at fault. A knowledgeable Henry County attorney in may able to assist with sifting through complex information and gathering evidence to support a burn injury claim.

The repercussions of severe burn injuries can be life-altering on a personal, social, professional, and financial level. You may be unable to work, face a lengthy period of recovery and rehabilitation, undergo multiple surgeries, and be flooded with medical bills and expenses.

If another individual or entity is responsible for your injuries, a Henry County burn injury lawyer may be able help you determine your potential options for seeking proper compensation. Dealing with the aftermath of these injuries can be difficult and stressful, so enlisting the assistance of an experienced attorney may help remove some your pressure and allow you to focus on what matters: your recovery.

pages.title: Henry County Paralysis Injury Lawyer | Paraplegia | Quadriplegia
pages.description: If you were paralyzed in an accident, you may be able to recover compensation with the help of a Henry County paralysis injury lawyer.
pages.content_md:
Injuries that result in partial or total paralysis can be life-changing. If you have suffered a paralyzing injury, you may be struggling to adapt to your new life and might be unable to return to work. You are likely to have medical expenses, rehabilitation costs, and other bills related to your injuries.

When the reckless or careless actions of another person cause you to suffer paralysis, you may have a cause of action for compensation that a personal injury attorney could help you explore. If retained, a compassionate Henry County paralysis injury lawyer could help you determine whether you can seek damages from negligent individuals and take appropriate action to do so.

Most paralysis injury claims are based on negligence, which is a legal concept that measures how reasonable the actions of an individual are in a situation. People may be deemed negligent if they have acted recklessly in a way that endangers the safety of others.

Sometimes, though, accident victims are partially at fault for their injuries. Pursuant to Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33, plaintiffs who bear less than 50 percent of total liability may still be able to seek compensation from other at-fault parties. Georgia law can be nuanced in this regard, but a Henry County paralysis attorney could explain its intricacies to injured individuals seeking civil damages.

A variety of different injuries can lead to paralysis, including neck and back injuries, spinal cord injuries, nerve injuries, and head or brain trauma. These damages may originate from various accidents, but most commonly one of the following:

- Motor vehicle accidents
- Workplace accidents
- Slip and falls
- Medical errors
- Defective products

Sometimes, paralysis is complete and leads to a total loss of function in some or all parts of the body. Complete paralysis often arises from a spinal cord injury, which may result in paraplegia or quadriplegia�permanent paralysis of the lower half of the body or permanent paralysis of both arms and legs, respectively.

Damages that stem from accidents causing paralysis can be extensive. Paralysis injuries often require routine medical care for the rest of an injured individual�s life, and certain complications can add even more expenses. These might include but are not limited to:

- Medical bills from hospital stays, rehabilitation costs, and ongoing care
- Wheelchairs, medical assistive devices, and modifications to homes and vehicles
- Round-the-clock nursing or personal care
- Loss of earnings

Aside from quantifiable expenses, recoverable damages also may include needed compensation for the emotional trauma, pain, and suffering associated with a catastrophic injury. A paralysis injury lawyer in Henry County could work with an individual plaintiff to determine exactly what they may be eligible to receive through a successful lawsuit or settlement.

Living with paralysis in the aftermath of a serious accident requires significant adjustments for victims and their families. If you were paralyzed due to the negligence of another person, though, you have a right to pursue compensation for the costs associated with these necessary changes.

While compensation may not restore you to your pre-accident life, obtaining some measure of financial security to pay for ongoing medical expenses could relieve some of your stress and help you maintain your normal standard of living. Call today to find out how a Henry County paralysis injury lawyer could assist you with pursuing compensation from the parties who are responsible for your injuries.

pages.title: Henry County Spinal Cord Injury Lawyer | Cervical Injuries
pages.description: If you or a loved one suffered a spinal cord injury, you may be entitled to compensation. Contact a dedicated Henry County spinal cord injury lawyer.
pages.h1: Henry County Spinal Cord Injury Lawyer
pages.content_md:
While there are many kinds of severe personal injuries, damages to the spinal cord can be one of the most life-altering varieties. On the bright side, though, you might be able to file a claim to receive compensation for your injuries with a dedicated catastrophic injury attorney�s help if you have sustained a spinal cord injury as the result of someone else�s careless or reckless behavior.

Harm to the spinal cord can result in permanent paralysis and have a devastating impact on you and your loved ones in physical, emotional, and financial terms. A compassionate Henry County spinal cord injury lawyer could work with you to evaluate your situation and determine your options to file a claim.

Vertebral and spinal damage often occurs from a sudden and traumatic blow to the spinal cord that fractures, compresses, dislocates, or crushes one or more vertebrae. Spinal cord injuries are classified as either incomplete, meaning some degree of motor or sensory function still exists below the site of the injury, or complete, where no feeling or motor function exists.

The difference between incomplete and complete paralysis often depends on the severity of the accident, as well as the length of time it takes an injured victim to receive medical care. There are two primary types of paralysis that can be incomplete or complete, both of which are often permanent:

� Quadriplegia or tetraplegia � characterized by an ability to move the arms, legs, and buttocks

� Paraplegia � involves paralysis of the legs, buttocks, and pelvic organs

Many spinal cord injury claims stem from negligence, which is a legal standard holding individuals to a duty of reasonable action in a situation. To be negligent, the individual must have breached their duty of care to keep others safe from harm.

Even if an injury victim is partially at fault for the accident which caused their spinal damage, they may still have the right to seek recovery for their injuries. The Georgia statute of limitations outlined in Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33 states that if victims are less than 50 percent accountable for the accident, they may still file an action for civil compensation, albeit their final award would be reduced by the same percentage of fault they bear.

If a victim bears more than 50 percent of the total fault, though, they may be unable to recover any damages whatsoever. A Henry County spinal cord injury lawyer could advocate on a plaintiff�s behalf to minimize comparative fault and maximize recoverable damages.

Victims suffering from vertebral and spinal injuries as a result of accidents may be entitled to recover various types of damages. These may include coverage for expenses related to:

� Current and future medical bills

� Rehabilitation treatment and devices

� Medical equipment

� Home renovations to accommodate a wheelchair

� Home health and personal care

� Lost wages and loss of future earnings

� Pain and suffering

The extent of the damages available often depends on the severity of the injuries, the policy limits of any available insurance coverage, and the age and health of the injury victim at the time of the accident. An experienced spinal cord injury attorney in Henry County may be able to assist in quantifying damages in a personal injury case.

The consequences of your spinal cord injury may feel immeasurable, but a dedicated attorney could help you take stock of your losses and take action to recover for them. If your injuries are the result of the negligent actions of another, you have a right to seek compensation.

You should not have to bear the financial and emotional toll of your injuries alone. Call today to speak to a Henry County spinal cord injury lawyer about your claim and start fighting to protect your rights and your future.

pages.title: Henry County Traumatic Brain Injury Lawyer | TBI Attorney
pages.description: If you suffered a TBI in an accident, a Henry County traumatic brain injury lawyer may be able to help you recover compensation. Call today to learn more.
pages.h1: Henry County Traumatic Brain Injury Lawyer
pages.content_md:
Of the many catastrophic injuries that can occur during an accident, one of the most severe is a traumatic brain injury (TBI). Brain damage can be the result of a motor vehicle wreck, falling accident, or numerous other incidents, and often leaves the victim seriously and permanently impaired.

If you have suffered a brain injury as the result of someone�s negligence, you have a legal right to retain a personal injury attorney and work to hold them accountable. A Henry County traumatic brain injury lawyer could advise you about your legal options and help you seek appropriate compensation for your damages.

Severe brain injuries often have disastrous results that directly impact the neural activity and functionality of the brain. The severity of a TBI can range from reasonably mild and temporary changes in brain function, to extreme impairment that affects the victim permanently. While some individuals show immediate symptoms for which they can receive treatment, other traumatic brain injuries do not surface until hours or even days after the accident.

The effects of sustaining a brain injury vary widely and often depend upon the severity and location of the injury. Some common conditions that could stem from serious brain damage include:

- Debilitating headaches
- Depression and extreme mood swings
- Nausea
- Insomnia
- Forgetfulness
- Inability to focus

Medical care for injuries to the brain can be expensive, potentially involving long hospital stays, lengthy periods of rehabilitation, and ongoing expenses for assistance in daily activities. Individuals with brain damage are also likely to be unable to return to work for significant periods of time, depending on the duties required of them and the severity of their injury.

In these cases, the injured victim could greatly benefit from the compassion and knowledge of a skilled Henry County traumatic brain injury attorney. Damages that a victim could potentially request compensation for might include medical bills, lost wages, hospital expenses, rehabilitation care, home health care, and pain and suffering.

To recover damages, an injured individual must demonstrate the presence of legal negligence�in other words, they must prove that someone else acted recklessly or carelessly, and that that person�s wanton behavior directly led to their injury. It can be difficult for a victim to show negligence without assistance. Experienced brain injury lawyers in Henry County could help seek and catalog evidence that supports a victim�s claims and negotiate with insurance companies to reach a positive outcome in their case.

The statute of limitations in Georgia establishes a two-year time limit after the incident which led to a TBI wherein victims may file a claim. If a potential plaintiff does not act within this timeframe, they may lose the right to file a claim. While there are exceptions to this time limit, injured parties generally must proceed with an action within the guidelines of this statute.

Brain injuries are severe and potentially life-altering events. If the negligence of another person has caused you or a loved one to sustain serious brain damage, you may have legal grounds to seek compensation.

By seeking a personal injury claim against those responsible for your losses, you can take proactive action toward your recovery. Retaining a compassionate Henry County traumatic brain injury lawyer could be the first key step you take toward holding others accountable. Call today to get started on your case.

pages.title: Henry County Dangerous Drugs Lawyer | Harmful Medication
pages.description: Call a Henry County dangerous drugs lawyer if you suffered injuries at the hands of a negligent or reckless drug manufacturing company to learn your rights.
pages.content_md:
Pharmaceutical companies could cut corners and distribute dangerous drugs in the market before fully testing them to identify potential long-term effects, side effects, and/or interactions with other medications. This negligence could cause serious harm to unsuspecting consumers.

If you have suffered an injury after safely taking medication, a Henry County dangerous drugs lawyer might be able to help you file an action for compensation. Companies who choose to put profits before safety should be held accountable when you sustain an injury from a defective or untested drug, and an experienced personal injury attorney could give you advice about doing so in your specific situation.

Prescription drugs use a variety of chemicals to alter the way the body operates. While powerful and generally helpful when used correctly, these drugs could also cause severe side effects and complications for consumers. Common types of drugs which have caused issues could�include but are not limited to:

- Birth control pills
- Antidepressants
- Drugs to lower cholesterol
- Arthritis medications

Drugs labeled safe for consumer use by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration could also harm consumers. Individuals injured by mislabeled or under-tested drugs may have grounds for a civil case and could benefit from contacting a knowledgeable dangerous drugs lawyer in Henry County.

While many drugs are labeled with potential side effects, users may still experience additional damages not listed. While some side effects of defective drugs may only last a short time and leave no lasting damage behind, others may contribute to serious health conditions which could include:

- Cancer
- Heart attack
- Stroke
- Kidney failure
- Impairment of liver
- Blood clots

Even if these complications are not immediately apparent or recognizable, they could still cause permanent�or fatal�impairments. These injuries are not the user�s fault so long as they used the drug as directed by their doctor, and plaintiffs injured by unsafe substances could hold the responsible parties accountable.

A skilled Henry County attorney may be able to hold multiple entities financially liable for injuries related to dangerous drugs. While the pharmaceutical company that manufactured the drugs most typically bears the majority of fault, they and other parties could face civil liability under the legal theories of strict liability, negligence, and/or a failure to warn.

In a strict liability case, the drug company is responsible for any injuries that occur when a consumer takes the drug as directed by the company. Directions could be placed on the substance�s label. There is typically no need for the claimant to show any fault or negligence on the part of the drug company to pursue a strict liability claim. An attorney could help a plaintiff determine what type of claim they could pursue.

A negligence case typically requires a plaintiff to show that the drug company was careless or reckless in testing, formulating, or otherwise producing the drug. If a person suspects there was a lack of regard for user safety by a pharmaceutical company, they could consider pursuing a negligence claim.

If a manufacturer of a drug knows about potential risks of harm, side effects, or interaction problems with other medications, they must notify consumers of those risks. If they neglect to do so, that company may be held civilly liable.

If you have taken a drug that caused unexpected side effects, harmful medication interactions, or medical conditions, you might be able to file a dangerous drugs claim. There are laws in place to hold drug companies responsible for the safety of their products, and a dedicated attorney might be able to fight for your rights.

It could be beneficial for you to contact a Henry County dangerous drugs lawyer immediately after you experience adverse symptoms or negative conditions resulting from a medication. To learn more about your legal options, call today.

pages.title: Henry County Defective Products Lawyer | Manufacturer Liability
pages.description: Call a Henry County defective products lawyer if a manufacturer's negligence or recklessness caused you injuries. An attorney could fight for you.
pages.content_md:
The general public typically learns that a product is defective only after a user suffers an injury. When this happens, manufacturers, suppliers, and other parties could be held liable for the costs of those damages.

Product manufacturers and sellers have a responsibility to the public to ensure that their products are safe. When they fail to meet this standard, consumers could work together with Henry County defective products lawyers to hold them accountable. If you have been harmed by a defective product, a skilled personal injury attorney may be able to assist in determining whether you have a case and what types of damages you could potentially recover.

All product manufacturers�and in some cases product designers, suppliers, distributors, and retailers�have a duty to make and distribute products that are safe to use in a reasonable manner. If a consumer is using a product for its intended usage, that product typically must be free of defects and could be required to contain adequate warning labels to advise consumers of any potential hazards.

When these items malfunction and cause harm, plaintiffs have a right to file a claim. A seasoned Henry County defective products attorney could give injured individuals advice about filing claims against manufacturers under product liability laws.

There are three primary types of product liability claims that a defective products attorney could help consumers in Henry County seek, which are design defects, manufacturing defects, and failure to warn claims.

Design defects entail defective designs that make all incarnations of a product inherently dangerous. Manufacturing defects could occur when something goes wrong in the production or assembly process that makes a single incarnation of a product dangerous to use. Failure to warn claims are based on the manufacturer�s duty to warn consumers of potential harms associated with using the product for its intended or foreseeable purpose. This could include providing adequate instructions and clear warnings.

Product liability claims may proceed based on legal theories of negligence, strict liability, breach of warranty, or fraudulent or false representation, based on the circumstances surrounding the incident. In most cases, plaintiffs might need to prove that the product:

- Was defective
- Directly caused their injuries
- Was in the same condition when used as it was at the time of manufacture or sale
- Was used in an appropriate or reasonably foreseeable manner

Official Code of Georgia �9-3-33 sets forth the statute of limitations for personal injury actions under Georgia law. A statute of limitations is essentially a deadline for filing a legal claim. While there are exceptions, the statute of limitations for personal injury actions typically requires a claim be filed within two years following the date of the incident where the consumer suffered injuries as a result of a defective product. Individuals are recommended to contact a dedicated attorney immediately after they detect their injury.

There is a statute of repose for product liability cases, wherein all products have a 10-year maximum limit on potential product liability claims. After this time, claimants may no longer hold a legal right to file an action against the company for a defective product. One exception to this rule is if a manufacturer failed to warn users of the known or foreseeable risks of their product. This action effectively eliminates the statute of repose.

While users are harmed by defective products frequently, consumers typically have the right to hold manufacturers and distributors responsible if their products turn out not to be safe.

If a defective product has caused you to suffer an injury, an experienced and compassionate Henry County defective products lawyer might be able to advise you about the viability of any products liability claim that you may have. Call today to schedule a consultation.

pages.title: Henry County Dog Bite Lawyer | Dangerous Canine Attacks
pages.description: If you were attacked by a vicious dog, you may be eligible for damages. Contact a Henry County dog bite lawyer to learn more.
pages.content_md:
Every year, many people in Henry County suffer injuries from dog bites, being knocked over by dogs, or attempting to escape an attacking dog. Regardless of how it plays out, any animal attack can lead to pain, serious injuries, and medical expenses.

While dogs can make great pets, any owner should be aware that they could be dangerous. Unfortunately, some people disregard the danger their pet may pose to others. If you were recently attacked by a dog, an experienced personal injury attorney could help you build a thorough case for civil damages. Once you have obtained medical attention, contact a Henry County dog bite lawyer for help evaluating your claim.

Georgia�s �dog bite� law establishes liability for injuries caused by almost any type of animal. Anyone injured by another person�s animal may be eligible for recovery, especially if the owner expressed disregard for reasonable or mandated safety measures.

O.C.G.A. �51-2-7 provides that an animal�s owner may be held liable for injuries their animal causes under the following conditions:

- The animal is determined to be dangerous
- The animal was carelessly managed or free-roaming
- The victim did not provoke injury

Georgia law holds that an owner must be aware of when their animal poses a threat. This is commonly referred to as the �one bite rule,� which implies that an owner cannot be aware their dog is dangerous until it bites someone. However, a seasoned Henry County dog bite lawyer could help establish other circumstances that may mark an animal as potentially dangerous.

For example, local laws require domestic animals to be on leashes or controlled at all terms. If the animal was not under its owner�s control during the attack, failure to follow these laws could make an owner liable for any resulting injuries.

Any claims resulting from a dog bite or other animal attack are legally classified as personal injury claims. Most states, including Georgia, impose time limits on when a potential plaintiff can file their claim. This is commonly called a statute of limitations.

Most personal injury lawsuit claims, including those centered around dog bites, must be filed within two years of the incident in question. Potential plaintiffs in Henry County may find contacting a dog bite attorney early on beneficial for their own peace of mind, just from knowing their claim will be properly filed within the time limit.

Contacting legal counsel early can also help ensure accurate and clear evidence could be collected. As more time passes, it could become increasingly difficult to acquire or preserve witness statements, photographs of injuries, and information about the scene of the attack.

While dog bite injuries may be common in Henry County, the resulting injuries could lead to life-altering consequences. Any attacking animal may cause deep cuts that could potentially damage nerves and tissues and leave lasting physical and emotional scars.

It is possible the owner of the animal that attacked you may have acted with disregard to the law and to your safety. If so, a dedicated Henry County dog bite lawyer could help you understand the applicable state and local laws and how they may apply to your situation. After seeking medical attention, reach out to a dedicated attorney to schedule a consultation and discuss the specifics of your attack.

pages.title: Henry County Medical Malpractice Lawyer | Negligent Medical Practices
pages.description: If you or someone you love has sustained grave injuries due to a neligent medical practice, contact a Henry County medical malpractice lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
Experiencing an illness or injury that requires medical care or hospitalization can be distressing. A patient�s distress may be increased if the care they receive causes further injury, illness, or complications. If you have suffered additional injury at the hands of a medical professional, it is important to remember that a medical malpractice claim can be brought against any medical professional.

It may be difficult, however, to prove a medical professional caused or exacerbated any injuries in a personal injury claim because a special set of rules has been developed to prevent claims without factual basis from being brought to courts.

A Henry County medical malpractice lawyer is experienced in handling these complex rules and could help you pursue your claim. Contact a compassionate personal injury attorney to seek a fair settlement for your injuries and losses.

The statute of limitations to file a medical malpractice lawsuit in Georgia is two years from the date the injury or death occurred. Additionally, under Georgia Code � 9-3-71, unless the medical professional committed fraud or intentionally concealed the error from the patient, a medical malpractice suit likely cannot be brought more than five years after the act that caused the injury or death.

Despite this, the statute of limitations can be extended in certain circumstances and a Henry County medical malpractice lawyer could help a plaintiff understand these rules. Fully understanding how the statute of limitations applies to a certain case could prevent a case from being barred.

Georgia imposes special requirements on medical malpractice cases because of the sensitive nature of medical malpractice lawsuits. Georgia Code � 9-11-9.1 requires an individual and potentially their attorney to file an affidavit, or a document affirming that the claim has merit, to recover damages from a medical malpractice claim.

To complete an affidavit, the plaintiff must find a field expert to support their claim. The expert must then complete the document with the requirements that:

- �An expert in the field has confirmed that the medical professional was negligent
- �The affidavit contains the factual basis for the negligence claim
- The affidavit is in writing and signed by the expert
- The affidavit is filed concurrently with the lawsuit

Since the defendant in the case does not have to respond to the complaint of medical malpractice until 30 days after the affidavit is filed, the affidavit is an important step in moving forward with a claim. For more information, get in touch with a�Henry County medical malpractice lawyer today.

A plaintiff may be entitled to compensation for economic damages such as medical expenses, lost wages, future lost wages from a reduced ability to work, and more. The plaintiff may also be able to receive compensation for noneconomic damages for their pain and suffering and loss of enjoyment of life.

A court could also award punitive damages to punish the defendant for their negligence. These damages are subject to a cap of $250,000 per case in Georgia. Punitive damages may be awarded in addition to compensatory damages depending on the circumstances.

Each medical malpractice case is unique but can quickly become complicated under the nuanced legal system. You may need to contact a Henry County medical malpractice lawyer today if you believe you have suffered under the care of a negligent medical professional. Skilled lawyers could help you regain financial losses and lessen your future pain and suffering by building a powerful case against the responsible parties.

pages.title: Henry County Birth Injury Lawyer | Injuries Sustained During Delivery
pages.description: A Henry County birth injury lawyer could help you pursue justice and compensation for your child. Call today to learn more.
pages.content_md:
Having a baby should be a joyous experience for a family, and expecting mothers and their families often place trust in their doctors and health care providers to help safely deliver their child. Unfortunately, negligent medical staff can cause a baby to suffer an injury prior to, during, or immediately after delivery.

Not every birth injury is the result of medical malpractice. However, when a birth injury does occur, it is important to consider whether a doctor, nurse, or other healthcare professional could have prevented that injury by delivering the proper care.

Compassionate personal injury attorneys understand the impact an injury from labor can have on you and your family, as well as on your newborn. If you suspect your child suffered unnecessary harm because of careless medical errors, a Henry County birth injury lawyer may be able to help you with your case.

There are a variety of factors that can contribute to or cause a birth injury. For instance, forceps or vacuums can be used to assist the birthing process, but improper use might lead to injuries for both mother and child. In the same vein, delaying or failing to perform a cesarean section can cause serious harm, and doctors should consistently check for signs of distress which may necessitate such a procedure.

In addition, medical professionals must be attentive to a baby�s heart rate for signs of decreased oxygen and closely monitor any medications that need to be administered. Failing to monitor a baby�s vital signs during labor or accurately prescribe medication may be grounds for civil liability in the event of injury to a newborn.

A dedicated Henry County birth injury lawyer could help determine whether new parents have a case based on any of the above circumstances. If they do, their attorney could work with them to determine who is liable for the injuries that have occurred and whether they are entitled to compensation.

Birth injury lawsuits in Henry County are often premised on a theory of legal negligence. Proving liability in a negligence case requires proving that a doctor or medical professional owed a mother and baby a duty of care, that they breached their duty of care, and that this breach directly caused an injury.

Proving that a doctor has breached the standard of care can be incredibly complicated. In many birth injury lawsuits, an experienced lawyer in Henry County would work with an independent medical expert to determine if a doctor has departed from accepted medical practice, a process which requires a thorough review of every aspect of a doctor�s care during each stage of delivery. If it is deemed that a medical staff deviated from the accepted medical standards, they could be held liable for a birth injury.

If you suspect you or your baby suffered a birth injury because of medical malpractice, do not hesitate to consult with a Henry County birth injury lawyer about your options. A knowledgeable attorney may be able to aggressively pursue compensation on your behalf to help cover the costs of medical care and treatment, as well as to compensate you for the emotional toll a birth injury can cause. Call today to get started on your case.

pages.title: Henry County Motorcycle Accident Lawyer | Motorbike Crashes
pages.description: Injuries from a motorbike crash are painful and expensive. Contact a Henry County motorcycle accident lawyer if you are seeking compensation for damages.
pages.content_md:
Motorcycle accidents can cause significantly more damage and more serious injuries than accidents involving only cars or trucks. The fault for these accidents can often lie with the driver of the larger vehicle because they do not see the motorcyclist.

If you have been injured or involved in a motorcycle accident that was the result of another driver�s carelessness, you may be entitled to compensation. You may need the help of a Henry County motorcycle accident lawyer to pursue financial recovery on your behalf. A seasoned motorcycle accident attorney could help you understand your post-accident rights and responsibilities.

To recover damages in a motorcycle accident in Henry County, the injured party must prove the defendant breached their duty of care by failing to use the level of caution that a reasonable person would use in the same circumstances. The claimant must also prove the other driver�s negligence caused the accident and that the accident was the actual and proximate cause of their injuries.

To prove negligence, there must be a �preponderance of the evidence,� or convincing evidence showing that the other driver acted recklessly. This behavior could include:

- Changing lanes without warning
- Speeding
- Driving between lanes of traffic
- Passing into a lane occupied by another vehicle
- Driving while tired or distracted
- Driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol

To assign fault, Georgia follows a comparative negligence rule, which means the defendant could reduce the number of damages for which they are liable by proving that the other party�s actions also contributed to causing the accident. A defendant could prove one party was 50 percent or more at fault for the accident, meaning a plaintiff would be barred from recovery.

To avoid a potential reduction in the plaintiff�s reward amount, a Henry County motorcycle accident lawyer could provide valuable assistance. Skillful lawyers experienced with negotiating and arguing with the defendant�s claims could help a plaintiff achieve a favorable outcome instead of having their potential compensation reduced.

Once a Henry County motorcycle accident lawyer establishes that the other driver caused the accident through their negligence, an injured individual could recover compensatory damages for physical injury, property damage, or even lost wages. Depending on the circumstances, the comparative negligence standard must also be considered in the calculation of the damage award.

For example, a jury may establish that one driver drove between lanes of traffic into another car and may also establish that the other driver was speeding. The jury may, therefore, determine the first driver was 70 percent responsible for the crash and the driver who was speeding was 30 percent responsible for the crash. The plaintiff may then collect a financial award that is reduced by 30 percent.

Regardless of whether you were partially at fault for a motorcycle accident, a Henry County motorcycle accident lawyer could help you establish a strong case against the party responsible for your injuries. A lawyer could help you prove that the other driver drove recklessly and breached their responsibility to watch out for others on the road. Call today to review your legal options and seek a fair compensation for your damages.

pages.title: Henry County Nursing Home Abuse Lawyer | Abuse of the Elderly
pages.description: If you or a loved one have been injured as a result of nursing home abuse, consult a Henry County nursing home abuse lawyer that can advocate for you.
pages.h1: Henry County Nursing Home Abuse Lawyer
pages.content_md:
People who put their parents and other elderly relatives in nursing homes trust that they will get the best care possible, yet nursing home abuse is shockingly common in America. Serious physical, verbal and even sexual abuse happen frequently in the nation’s nursing homes and assisted living facilities, according to recent investigations.

Fortunately, a Henry County nursing home abuse lawyer can help. Speak with an experienced personal injury attorney that can�fight for justice for your family.

Federal health and safety standards protect nursing home residents from abuse, and annual inspections by federal and state authorities are supposed to ensure these standards are met. But all too often, the standards are ignored or violations missed by inspectors.

Common problems stemming from nursing home abuse include untreated bedsores, inadequate medical care, malnutrition, dehydration, preventable accidents, and inadequate sanitation and hygiene. Many of these abuses cause significant harm to the residents. In extreme cases, they can even result in premature death.

In many cases, members of the nursing home’s staff are found to have committed physical or sexual abuse. Investigations have uncovered cases of residents being punched, slapped, choked or kicked by staff members or other residents, causing injuries such as fractured bones or lacerations. In a few instances, staffers have been cited for failing to protect people from abuse by other residents.

It is very important for individuals visiting relatives at the nursing home to keep a sharp eye out for evidence of neglect or abuse. If the facility is not providing the level of care it is required to by law, there may be grounds for family members of abused residents to bring forth a civil suit, and a Henry County nursing home abuse lawyer could help.

Some nursing home industry representatives admit to nationwide difficulty in attracting and keeping quality staff members such as licensed vocational nurses and certified nursing assistants. Nonetheless, it is the responsibility of each facility to provide the kind of care that residents and their families are entitled to expect.

Sometimes understaffed nursing homes resort to putting residents in physical restraints, a practice which is forbidden by federal health and safety standards unless there is a specific medical need for the restraints. Understaffing can also result in poor sanitation, vermin infestation, and other forms of neglect.
