pages.description: If you are suffering kidney damage after taking this defective HIV medication, speak with a Truvada lawyer to discuss your legal options.
pages.content_md:
Many people use the drug Truvada to treat HIV but there have been numerous instances of users developing serious side effects. Despite marketing this drug as potentially life-saving for individuals living with HIV, Truvada has taken a toll on the health of a number of patients who use it.

If you are living with the consequences of Truvada�s side effects, you deserve a skilled mass torts attorney who could aggressively advocate for you. Legal action that targets the makers of Truvada could yield compensation for your health issues and cover the cost of any necessary treatment. A Truvada lawyer could serve as your advocate and assist in your pursuit of justice.

The purpose of Truvada is to prevent HIV-infected cells from replicating within the human body. This drug can not only slow or halt the spread of the disease among patients who have it, but it can also have a prophylactic effect that prevents individuals from ever contracting the virus in the first place.

Truvada is made up of two main components: Emtricitabine (FTC) and Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate (TDF). Together, FTC and TDF work to inhibit the enzyme HIV-infected cells use to replicate. By inhibiting this enzyme, Truvada can slow the spread of HIV to a crawl. In some instances, it can prevent the spread of HIV entirely. This is especially true when Truvada is combined with other HIV medications.

Despite the benefits of the drug, Truvada has also shown a concerning number of serious and unexpected drawbacks. These side effects can cause harm to many different parts of the body, but the kidneys are especially impacted. Truvada has been linked to acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease in many cases. Additionally, Truvada patients have been found to be prone to renal failure, renal impairment, and end-stage renal disease.

The kidneys are not the only part of the body that can be devastated by Truvada. It has also been linked to diminished bone density, which can increase the likelihood of breaks or fractures. Some patients have also reported losing teeth after taking Truvada. An attorney could assist a person injured by Truvada pursue financial compensation for any of these serious conditions.

One of the key factors in a civil case is who is deemed liable for the losses. There are two different legal theories a lawyer could rely on when pursuing a claim against Truvada. These theories of liability are known as strict liability and negligence.

Strict liability claims are common with defective drugs. Under this legal theory, a plaintiff must show the manufacturer of Truvada made the drug in a way that was unreasonably dangerous. However, compensation could be available even without the plaintiff showing the manufacturer acted negligently.

Most personal injury cases hinge on a negligence theory. To establish this claim, a plaintiff must show that the makers of Truvada failed to take reasonable care in designing and manufacturing the drug. By showing that this lack of care resulted in their injury, a plaintiff could be entitled to compensation.

For many Truvada users, the optimism of a potential HIV treatment quickly gave way to a series of new, challenging health consequences. If you suffered medical injuries while taking Truvada, you could have a viable claim against the maker of the drug.

You do not have to pursue a lawsuit by yourself. Contact a Truvada lawyer right away to set up an initial consultation.

pages.title: TRW Airbag Failure Lawyer | Claim for Defective Airbags
pages.description: A TRW airbag failure lawyer could help file a lawsuit if you suffered significant injuries in a car crash because your airbag did not deploy.
pages.content_md:
TRW Automotive Holdings Corporation (TRW) has long served as a supplier of millions of automobile airbags across the world. However, TRW is alleged to have marketed millions of defective airbags from 2010 to 2019. Many of these airbags produced serious or even fatal injuries when they failed to deploy during an accident.

If you sustained physical injuries due to a faulty TRW airbag, you could have a strong legal claim for monetary compensation. A seasoned mass torts attorney could assist you in evaluating your claim and determine if you are entitled to monetary damages. A lawsuit filed by your TRW airbag failure lawyer could represent your opportunity to obtain compensation for your injuries.

The investigation into potential defects in TRW airbags began after a series of injuries and deaths due to airbags failing to inflate during an accident. These airbags were common in several different makes and models of vehicles, including those manufactured by:

- Toyota
- Kia
- Mitsubishi
- Honda
- Fiat
- Hyundai

Testing showed that the defect resulted from a part known as the airbag control unit, or ACU. The ACU exists to detect collisions and deploy the airbags in the event of a severe impact. These ACU relied on electronic components known as an application specific integrated circuit, or ASIC. The ASIC is essentially the central hub for signals from throughout the vehicle. It is designed to evaluate each of these signals to determine if airbag deployment is necessary.

In some cases, a crash could result in a rush of electrical signals that can overstress the ASIC. These electronic signals can overload the ASIC, resulting in the failure to deploy the airbag during a crash.

The investigation by the�National Highway Transportation Safety Administration�(NHTSA) is ongoing. To date, the NHTSA has not issued a recall for the more than 12 million vehicles they are evaluating. However, individual vehicle manufacturers that relied on TRW airbags have issued voluntary recalls. A TRW defective airbag attorney could explain to someone if their vehicle has been recalled.

The lack of airbag deployment in an accident can have a dangerous effect on the occupants within the vehicle. These failures are likely to cause severe harm, even in cases where the impact was relatively minor. As these injuries become more severe, the cost of treating them goes up as well.

Medical injury expenses are typically one of the largest costs that come out of these accidents. Not only could an injured person require ambulance transportation and emergency care, but they might also need surgical procedures or other follow-up care. A successful lawsuit against TRW could recover compensation for these expenses.

It is the role of an experienced attorney to investigate the damages that the plaintiff suffers due to a TRW airbag failure accident. In addition to medical costs, an injured motorist could face a range of losses, including pain and suffering, loss of consortium, and lost wages. Beyond their bodily injuries, these motorists could also suffer financial losses from having to repair or replace their damaged vehicle.

If you sustained bodily harm due to a defective airbag, you might be entitled to seek legal action. This could take the form of a lawsuit against the airbag manufacturer, as well as the maker of your vehicle.

If you have questions regarding your legal right to sue for damages from these defective parts, a TRW airbag failure lawyer could provide the answers. Schedule your confidential case evaluation as soon as possible.

pages.title: Zantac Lawyer | Medication Containing Carcinogen
pages.description: A Zantac lawyer could help you pursue appropriate compensation if you have suffered illnesses due to taking this defective medication.
pages.content_md:
For years, the popular antacid known as ranitidine was marketed to American consumers under the name Zantac. Millions of doses of this antacid were purchased over the counter across the county thanks to large, aggressive ad campaigns. Unfortunately, research now shows Zantac could represent a significant health threat to the public.

According to research, Zantac may contain a dangerous carcinogen. If you have gotten sick after consuming Zantac or any version of ranitidine, a skilled mass torts attorney might be able to help. Large-scale lawsuits related to these injuries could represent your best chance of recovering compensation for any harm Zantac has caused you. Let a Zantac lawyer review your medical records so you could initiate a claim as soon as possible.

Researchers studying Zantac have discovered it contains high levels of a chemical known as N-Nitrosodimethlyamine (NDMA). NDMA is believed to be a potential cause of cancer. This harsh chemical is used in a variety of other products, including pesticides. While research continues, there are a number of warning signs that NMDA could lead to certain forms of cancer. The makers of Zantac face allegations that they were aware of the dangerous nature of NDMA but failed to take any action to protect the public.

On April 1, 2020, the�United States Food and Drug Administration�(FDA) announced a formal request that makers of prescription and over-the-counter ranitidine drugs remove them from the market right away. This action was based on the findings of high levels of NDMA in these products. Additionally, the announcement from the FDA claimed that NDMA levels could grow substantially in ranitidine products that were stored in conditions above room temperate.�A Zantac attorney could further describe the risks associated with ranitidine to a claimant.

The potential compensation that comes with a successful Zantac injury claim will depend on the type of legal action a person pursues. An attorney could file a Zantac lawsuit directly against the manufacturers of the drug, or an injured person could join in with an existing class action lawsuit.

There are benefits and drawbacks to both types of cases. While class actions are often cheaper and easier to manage, an individual plaintiff has little control over the direction of the claim. Direct lawsuits, on the other hand, give plaintiffs leeway in how they proceed with a case, and they can often result in higher compensation.

The compensation that a plaintiff could win from a direct lawsuit against the manufacturer of Zantac is similar to that of any other personal injury claim. A Zantac injury lawyer must demonstrate that the plaintiff suffered measurable damages.

Medical expenses are the most common type of measurable damages in Zantac claims. Treating cancer is a long and costly process, and a successful lawsuit could recoup those costs. This includes expenses related to hospitalization, diagnosis, surgery, or medication.�Other forms of compensation that could result from a Zantac lawsuit include:

- Pain and suffering
- Lost wages
- Diminished earning power
- Future medical bills
- Disability

If you are living with the consequences of taking the dangerous drug Zantac, you are entitled to pursue monetary compensation. This process may seem complex and intimidating, but a successful claim could provide the relief that you need.

An experienced Zantac lawyer could help evaluate your claim and determine the best course of action for your situation. With their help, you could aggressively pursue compensation from the makers of Zantac. Call right away to schedule your initial consultation.

pages.title: Zofran Lawyer | GlaxoSmithKline Negligent Anti-Nausea Medicine
pages.description: If you took Zofran during your pregnancy and discovered later birth defects in your child, you need ot contact a Zofran lawyer and apply for a mass tort.
pages.content_md:
Nausea is one of the most common side effects of pregnancy. Also known as morning sickness, this minor but certainly inconvenient side effect burdens many pregnant women.

To help treat this side effect, many doctors previously prescribed Zofran, also known as Ondansetron. Unfortunately, the effects of this drug on the fetuses of pregnant women was not well-known at the time. This lapse in proper testing of the drug resulted in many children being born with congenital heart defects.

A Zofran lawyer may be able to help you seek compensation if your child was born with a heart defect after a doctor prescribed you this drug. Additionally, qualified attorneys could help you if you experienced an injury or the loss of your child, as well as help determine if you qualify to join a Zofran mass tort case.

GlaxoSmithKline, the makers of Zofran, originally designed the drug for use as an anti-nausea medication to treat symptoms after chemotherapy or surgery. However, GSK never intended for the drug to be used as a treatment for morning sickness.

Unfortunately for pregnant women, the most prominent alternative anti-nausea medication left the market in 1983. When Zofran finally received FDA approval in 1991, doctors saw the potential to use this drug as a treatment for morning sickness. The use of Zofran in this manner continues to this day.

However, since Zofran was not tested for its effects on pregnant women, the effects on their unborn children were catastrophic. In 2013, medical studies indicated that Zofran could cause abnormal heart rhythms in patients. Even worse, it could have a detrimental effect on an unborn child if taken within the first trimester.

This resulted in many children being born with a �hole-in-the-heart� birth defect, which could result in an abnormal heartbeat, an increase in the risk for stroke, and general heart failure. A Zofran lawyer could help people make the connections between their child�s heart conditions and the use of Zofran during pregnancy.

Normally, a person injured by the actions of a company such as GlaxoSmithKline must pursue their lawsuit as an individual. This is often a daunting task, as these drug companies have massive legal departments and typically fight tooth-and-nail to protect their profits.

Conversely, a mass tort allows multiple plaintiffs to join their cases together into a single lawsuit. This allows injured victims to pool their resources, select one expert witness to present evidence on behalf of all of them, and hold a single trial to decide the truth of the matter.

However, a mass tort is not always acceptable under the law. According to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23, to qualify as a mass tort, a case must:

- Involve multiple plaintiffs who suffer injuries because of the negligence of a single defendant
- Hold that a substantially identical fact pattern caused all the plaintiffs� injuries

In the case of Zofran, thousands of children were born with congenital heart defects because of the drug�s side effects. Since GSK designed this drug, both elements of a mass tort claim are present.

In fact, there is currently a mass tort underway in the U.S. District Court of Massachusetts representing Zofran victims. A Zofran lawyer could help determine if a plaintiff�s case fits the requirements for this legal action.

Not every injury that results from taking a drug stems from poor design or improper manufacture. Others result from manufacturers of a drug advertising its use for an improper manner.

A prominent example of this dynamic is GlaxoSmithKline pushing Zofran for use as an anti-nausea medication for pregnant women. This choice by the company resulted in many children suffering from congenital heart defects that affected their health for the rest of their lives.

If your child has suffered injuries after you were prescribed Zofran, you may have the right to seek compensation. Oftentimes, this could include filing a claim for compensation under the framework of a mass tort, and in some cases, you may already qualify for a mass tort already accepted in the courts. Contact a Zofran lawyer today to evaluate your legal options.

pages.title: McDonough Personal Injury Lawyer | Recovering Compensation
pages.description: If you or a loved one suffered an injury in an accident, you may be eligible to compensation. Call a McDonough personal injury lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
Everyone is expected to exercise ordinary diligence. When a person fails to exercise the degree of care typically expected under the circumstances, they can cause serious injuries to those around them. These injuries could be the basis of a personal injury claim.

Another�s careless, reckless, and negligent behavior should not leave you in financial ruin. After a painful injury, you may wish to contact a McDonough personal injury lawyer. A compassionate attorney could fight for your right to compensation so you may return to your normal life.

Personal injury is an umbrella term that encompasses a wide variety of events, including:

- Motor vehicle wrecks
- Bad medical care
- Falling accidents
- Workplace injuries
- Defective products

People have the right to recover financial compensation for their injuries and losses by filing a personal injury action. These are often based on the theory of negligence. After someone is hurt, attorneys in McDonough are uniquely situated to address different types of personal injury claims and could work to hold individuals, companies, and corporations responsible for their negligent actions.

Many successful personal injury claims are based on the theory of negligence. To recover compensation under a negligence theory, the injured person must prove:

- Duty of care
- Breach of the duty
- Causation
- Damages

First, an individual must establish that another person, corporation, or legal entity owed them a duty of care. There may be a different duty of care depending on the situation that led to the injury. Under the law, a doctor owes a different duty of care to their patients than a person driving a car owes to another driver.

Once the duty is established, the injured person, or plaintiff in a legal case, must demonstrate a breach of duty. Breaches occur when someone�s actions do not meet the proper standard of care. The plaintiff must then demonstrate a connection between the breach and any injuries that resulted. Finally, a plaintiff must prove that they have suffered some form of damage. This can include property damage, bodily injury, or even mental suffering.

In a car wreck with multiple vehicles, drivers may each hold partial fault, including the injured party themselves. This could make determining liability more complicated. A hardworking McDonough personal injury lawyer could help explain steps to take, especially with respect to Georgia�s modified comparative negligence statute.

Under Official Code of Georgia � 51-12-33, a person may recover compensation if they are 49 percent at fault for an accident. However, if they are 50 percent or more at fault for an accident, they cannot recover damages.

It may be important to demonstrate liability by collecting evidence and conducting depositions, regardless of the number of involved parties. Through negotiation with insurance companies and agents, a McDonough personal injury lawyer could help injured people recover the compensation needed to heal.

Personal injury claims are a way to recover compensation after you are hurt by another person�s negligence. Though filing a lawsuit after injury may be frightening, allowing a skilled McDonough personal injury lawyer to diligently review your case could help you heal. An attorney could handle the legal aspects of an injury, meet with you to discuss the details, and offer practical and legal guidance throughout the entire process. Reach out to an experienced attorney today to schedule a free consultation.

pages.title: McDonough Bicycle Accident Lawyer | Bike Crash Injuries
pages.description: If you have suffered injuries from a bike crash, you may be able to seek compensation with the help of a McDonough bicycle accident lawyer.
pages.content_md:
Bicycle wrecks can cause significant injuries or even death to cyclists. For everyone�s safety, it is vital that both motorists and bicycle riders obey the rules of the road. When a motorist fails to do this, bicyclists who lack the protection of a motor vehicle often face steep medical bills or even lifestyle changes.

A seasoned McDonough bicycle accident lawyer could hold a motorist accountable for their negligence. Contacting an experienced personal injury attorney who understands the basics of these cases may be in your best interests.

When a potential plaintiff consults with a McDonough legal counsel, the attorney may first want to determine if the victim�s case has merit. In order to obtain a successful outcome, a civil plaintiff and their legal counsel must prove that:

- The defendant owed a duty of care to the victim
- The negligent party breached their duty
- The victim�s injuries are a direct result of the breach
- The injuries resulted in compensable damages to the injured person

A jury cannot deliver a verdict in favor of the plaintiff and award damages if all four of these elements of legal negligence are not demonstrated. Speaking with a skilled bicycle accident attorney in McDonough could help a victim determine what the best course of action might be to facilitate this outcome.

Individuals who were in a bicycle accident may often wonder what their claim may be worth. Many different factors could impact the value of a case, but one of the most important may be whether the plaintiff bears any liability for their injuries.

Attorneys for the allegedly negligent party in bicycle wreck cases commonly use the defense of comparative fault or plaintiff liability, claiming that the victim is liable for at least some of their own damages. For instance, if the plaintiff was not wearing a helmet, was not riding in the bike lane, or was otherwise not obeying traffic laws, the defense may attempt to slant these actions or inactions as evidence of negligence by the victim.

Even if claimants believe they may have some fault in their accident, they should still contact a bicycle accident lawyer in McDonough. Under the Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33(g), if a plaintiff is less than 50 percent liable for their own damages, they may still be able to recover compensation. However, their recoverable compensation would be reduced in proportion to the percentage of fault they are assigned.

It is also essential for bike crash victims to understand that there are no damage caps in the state of Georgia. Damage caps are statutory limits placed on the amount a bicycle accident plaintiff could be awarded. In 2010, the Georgia Supreme Court ruled in favor of removing previously held damage caps.

If a bicycle wreck left you with medical expenses, lost wages, or pain and suffering calling a McDonough bicycle accident lawyer might be your best move. Hiring an attorney to advocate for your rights could be the most efficient and less stressful option for you to receive compensation for your damages. Reach out today to learn more and get your case started.

pages.title: McDonough Bus Accident Lawyer | Public Transportation Collisions
pages.description: A McDonough bus accident lawyer could help you bring your claim against the negligent party so that you can recover the damages you deserve.
pages.content_md:
Although buses are often an ideal way to transport large numbers of people, they are also dangerous vehicles. This danger, however, does not excuse the duty of care that bus operators have to their commuters or other motor vehicles on the road.

If you were recently injured in a bus wreck, a compassionate McDonough bus accident lawyer could help you pursue compensation for your damages in civil court. Reaching out to an experienced attorney may be your best option for recovering financially after a bus crash.

Bus wrecks are often complicated cases, as they often involve multiple liable parties. Negligent parties in a bus accident case might include:

- The driver
- The owner of the bus
- The company running the bus service
- Other drivers
- The bus manufacturer or bus parts manufacturer

A plaintiff�s McDonough bus accident attorney could examine the facts of the accident carefully to determine who should be held responsible in their particular case. Each negligent individual could be held liable to the victim for their own portion of the damages caused in the wreck.

As per Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33, there is no right of contribution among tortfeasors in the State of Georgia. If one defendant settles with the plaintiff, but the others do not, a reduction of the total percentage owed is not allowed. Instead, the settlement becomes a factor for the jury to consider when determining the remaining defendants� percentage of fault, and therefore compensation they owe to the plaintiff.

Individuals who are involved in bus wrecks may suffer physically, emotionally, and financially. By teaming with an experienced bus accident lawyer in McDonough, victims may be able to effectively seek compensation for these losses and inconveniences that are commonly referred to as economic or non-economic damages. Recoverable damages after a bus accident might include:

- Past and future decreased income
- Past and future medical bills
- Pain and suffering
- Mental anguish
- Loss of enjoyment of life
- Loss of consortium
- Property damage

Whereas compensable damages are designed to compensate victims for their damages, punitive damages are meant to punish defendants and to deter them and from future similar behaviors. As per O.C.G.A �51-12-5.1, a jury may only award punitive damages in cases in which there is clear and convincing evidence that a negligent party acted intentionally reckless, with willful misconduct, or with the intent to harm the case holder. It is also essential for plaintiffs to note that Georgia law also caps punitive damages at $250,000. For more information about recoverable damages following a bus crash, contact an accomplished lawyer.

After suffering injuries in a bus wreck, you may need to seek medical help from experienced healthcare providers for your physical well-being. Because of the cost of medical bills and general damages, you may also want to seek legal assistance from an experienced McDonough bus accident lawyer for your financial well-being.

By hiring an attorney to represent your interests, you could focus on getting the medical treatment you need and still pursue compensation for your damages. It may be important to act quickly, so call today to schedule a consultation today and get started on your case.

pages.title: McDonough Car Accident Lawyer | Automobile Collisions
pages.description: A skilled McDonough car accident lawyer could help you recover damages if you or a loved one were injured in a car collision.
pages.content_md:
After a serious car wreck, people often turn to an insurance company for help meeting their financial needs. However, insurance companies often use aggressive tactics to protect themselves and their drivers and could try to avoid paying after an accident. This is just one reason you may need the assistance of a McDonough car accident lawyer.

Beyond negotiating with insurance companies, an accomplished personal injury attorney could help recover compensation for your injuries from a liable driver. Through a lawsuit alleging personal injury, an attorney could hold a negligent and driver responsible for their actions and the injuries they cause.

Negligence is a legal construct that is often used in car accident litigation. Drivers have a legal obligation to exercise the same degree of care that would be used by reasonable people in similar circumstances, as set forth in Official Code of Georgia � 51-1-2. When a driver fails to use this degree of care, they may be engaging in negligent driving behavior.

Negligence is generally distilled down to four elements: duty, breach, causation, and damages. In a car wreck lawsuit, the injured driver will have to successfully prove these four elements in order to recover compensation for their injuries. Many individuals hurt in motor vehicle crashes rely on their skilled attorneys to investigate claims and help establish these elements.

One method many car wreck attorneys in McDonough will lean on to show that a driver is negligent is proof that the driver violated a traffic law. Actions that lead to citations and tickets could be used as evidence of negligent behavior, including:

- Speeding
- Following too closely
- Failing to stop at a stop sign or traffic signal
- Driving while under the influence
- Texting or using a mobile telephone

These common driving behaviors are repeatedly cited as the leading causes of accidents. By violating a rule of the road, a driver could be considered negligent under the doctrine of negligence per se. An experienced McDonough car accident lawyer could work with police and local law enforcement to collect evidence of suspected violations.

While it is often difficult to predict a potential settlement or damage amount in a car wreck injury case, determining the value of a claim can be extremely beneficial. Compensation awards typically depend on a variety of factors, such as the severity of injuries or damage, whether an injury will result in permanent impairment, and how fault is determined and distributed.

While many auto accidents are caused by speeding, distracted driving, and texting, even a minor driving mistake could cause an accident that seriously injures you. After a car wreck, you may face significant injuries and substantial property damage. Fortunately, with the guidance of an experienced McDonough car accident lawyer, you could secure the compensation you need to recover.

A car accident attorney understands that every car accident case is unique. Have an attorney address the specific details of your case, outline how to protect yourself from aggressive insurance companies, and work to maximize the value of your case. Call to schedule a free case review today.

If the negligence of another driver caused your front-end car wreck, a McDonough front-end car accident lawyer could help you pursue compensation. No matter the type of injury or its implications, a compassionate McDonough front-end car accident attorney could advocate for injured victims to receive compensation for their damages.

Common front-end car accident injuries could include:

- Whiplash caused by the sudden jerking of the head or neck that stretches the ligaments and muscles in the neck, head, or shoulders
- Brain injuries resulting from the driver�s head being violently forced into the steering wheel or another hard surface in the vehicle
- Blunt trauma to various areas of the body, most commonly the chest and abdomen from the force of the seatbelt

Many plaintiffs wanting to file a personal injury claim may be unaware that they must file their case within a certain amount of time, known as the statute of limitations. Not knowing about this deadline could invalidate their claim and cause them to lose their right to pursue compensation. Consulting with a front-end car wreck lawyer in McDonough as soon as possible after an accident may help secure the legal rights and options of many car accident victims.

As per the Official Code of Georgia �9-3-33, the statutory deadline to submit a civil lawsuit is two years from the date of the plaintiff�s accident. There are a few exceptions to the statute of limitations that may extend this limit. However, some of these exceptions may include:

- If the defendant leaves the state after the car accident but before they are provided with the official complaint (Georgia Code � 9-3-94)
- The injured person is under the age of 18 or has an intellectual disability or mental illness at the time of the accident causing them to be deemed legally incompetent (Georgia Code � 9-3-90)

Even minor car accidents have the potential to turn into complex legal cases, especially if there are multiple parties involved. Let a McDonough front-end car accident lawyer take on the legal aspects of your case while you focus on your recovery after a front-end car wreck. Do not wait, reach out to today to get your case started.

pages.title: McDonough Parking Lot Accident Lawyer | Parking Garage Collisions
pages.description: An experienced McDonough parking lot accident lawyer could help you recover damages if you were injured in a parking lot collision. Call today.
pages.content_md:
With many distractions and traffic going in different directions, motorists in parking lots may be more vulnerable to accidents. Fortunately, a McDonough parking lot accident lawyer could help you file a civil claim if you suffered injuries in a car wreck. A seasoned car wreck attorney could work to ensure that you receive fair compensation and guide you through any legal challenges.

Parking lots can cause confusion because some drivers may be unsure of who has the right of way and may not be looking out for other motorists and pedestrians. Several circumstances could cause an accident in a parking lot. Some types of accidents may include when:

- Two vehicles collide, and one is in motion
- Two vehicles collide, and both are in motion
- A driver hits a stationary object in the lot
- A motorist hits a pedestrian

Liability in these situations may be simple to determine. However, claimants who were parked or stopped illegally should consult with a McDonough parking lot accident attorney because they may run a higher risk of liability for their accident in these circumstances.

As per the Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33(b), injured claimants may be liable for a portion of their losses. The jury may evaluate the fault of each driver when the court questions the liability of the plaintiff. If the injured party is 49 percent or less for their damages, they may still recover compensation from the defendant.

In this situation, a plaintiff may receive a compensatory award that the jury reduces by their percentage of fault in the accident. With representation from a qualified parking lot collision lawyer in McDonough, the plaintiff could maximize their financial recovery.

Because parking lot accidents occur on private property, law enforcement officers may not issue citations or determine who they believe to be at-fault. Instead, the drivers involved and their insurance companies may determine the liable party. With no official determination from law enforcement, these wrecks can be complex and injured individuals could benefit from the services of an experienced lawyer.

Car wreck lawsuits may be resolved outside of a courtroom through a settlement agreement. Plaintiffs are not obligated to accept an offered settlement. After discussing a settlement offer with their parking lot accident lawyer in McDonough, a claimant can make an educated decision to either accept or deny it.

Parking lot accidents, no matter how minor they may seem, have the potential to cause significant injuries and property damage. Injured parties may incur medical expenses and lose their vehicle, leading to financial hardships and emotional trauma while trying to recover.

Individuals who are impacted by such an accident could seek the representation of a knowledgeable McDonough parking lot accident lawyer to help pursue compensation for their damages. Schedule a case evaluation today and find out what your case may be worth.

Under the Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33, there is no right of contribution among defendants in a single case. Each defendant could be liable for their proportionate share of the financial damages to the plaintiff.

A judge or jury decides what percentage of liability each defendant should be responsible for, and each party must pay damages to the plaintiff accordingly. For example, if the jury awards the plaintiff $100,000 in damages, and one defendant is 60 percent at fault, they would pay $60,000 of those damages to the plaintiff.

If one defendant reaches a settlement agreement with the plaintiff, but others do not, the court may not permit set-offs. However, when determining the remaining defendant�s degree of fault, the court considers the settlement.

Sometimes defense attorneys may attempt to place the blame for an accident on the plaintiff. State law uses the legal concept of modified comparative fault when determining fault for both parties as well as how fault may impact a plaintiff’s damages.

As explained in the Official Code of Georgia �51-12-33(b), if a plaintiff is less than 50 percent at fault for their injuries, they may still recover the remaining damages from the defendant. For instance, a jury may find a plaintiff is ten percent at fault of their injuries in a case worth $50,000. The plaintiff may still recover $45,000 in damages from the defendant in the case.

The plaintiff and the defendant may also attempt to settle their case outside of court through their attorneys. Unfortunately, if there is evidence to support that the plaintiff is partially to blame for some of their injuries, this could reduce the settlement offers they receive. pages.content_md:
If you have sustained severe second or third-degree burns or are coping with the scarring and disfigurement of permanent injuries due to another party’s negligence, a McDonough burn injury lawyer could explain to you what is required to file a lawsuit and what you could expect if you pursue litigation. The identification of liable parties should occur as early on as possible in a civil litigation claim, and your personal injury lawyer could become an important factor in gathering the necessary evidence to name another party as liable in court.

Severe burn injuries may leave the victim with problems regarding pain management and medical bills in the short term, as well as long-term damages and expenses in more severe cases. First-degree burns typically produce the mildest consequences because these only affect the outer layer of the skin, whereas third-degree burns go through the dermis and affect deeper tissues of the victim�therefore causing greater damage.

Some of the most common causes of burns include:

- Friction
- Heated objects

Because of the horrifying nature of these injuries, it can be important to have support from a reliable McDonough burn injury attorney when seeking compensation from the party responsible for causing your burn.

The time limit that a victim has to file a personal injury lawsuit after an accident depends on whether the injury claim is against a county, city, state, or another entity. For injury claims directly against a county or city in Georgia, the victim has a maximum of six months to file a formal claim.

For injury claims against the state, this time period is two years. Finally, the general statute of limitations for individual people or corporate entities enables victims to initiate a lawsuit no later than two years after the date of the accident, according to Official Code of Georgia �9-3-33.

Proving a wrongdoer’s legal negligence and how it caused the victim’s injury are crucial aspects of a personal injury lawsuit. The victim must demonstrate four different elements to show that legal negligence exists in a case.

First, the defendant must have owed a duty of care to the plaintiff. Second, that defendant must have breached their duty of care by putting the plaintiff in harm’s way.

Third, the plaintiff must have sustained direct personal injury because of the defendant breaching their duty. Finally, the plaintiff must be able to show actual economic and/or non-economic damages.

Georgia courts apply what is known as the reasonably prudent person’s standard of care to determine the severity of a civil defendant’s negligence. For example, a landlord who failed to correct a wiring issue that led to a fire or a person under the influence of alcohol who caused a serious crash and resulting burn injuries are examples of parties who could be held liable by a burn accident lawyer in McDonough.

Whereas a concussion is a form of mild TBI that is classified as a temporary injury to the brain, they could still take up to several months to heal. Unfortunately, more serious TBI injuries might never fully heal, leading to permanent�and often expensive�consequences for a victim. The specific party that a victim could file their claim with depends on who is at fault. Regardless of the defendant, though, a legal claim must be filed no later than two years after the accident happens, according to Official Code of Georgia �9-3-33.

Establishing negligence is one of the most important components of a personal injury claim. There are certain ways that a person must behave to ensure safety for themselves and others�an expectation which is known as a duty of care. Examples of duty of care could include sharing the road with bicyclists, stopping at stop signs and red lights while driving and managing property to ensure there are no hazards that would constitute an unreasonable danger for visitors.

When a claimant can show that another party has breached this duty of care and that these actions or omissions directly led to their injuries, they could seek compensation for those injuries and related effects with the help of a TBI lawyer in McDonough. To reiterate, though, showing causation requires demonstrating that the damages, injuries, and financial losses sustained are the direct result of the defendant�s breach of duty, not just coincidental.

To schedule a consultation, call today.

Under the state�s comparative fault system, each party involved in an incident could be assigned a percentage of blame.

Put simply, Georgia�s modified comparative fault law eliminates or reduces damages if a potential claim holder or party is found to be mostly or partly at fault for an accident. A McDonough paralysis accident attorney could help a plaintiff determine whether comparative fault may play a role in their case and work on their behalf to minimize their potential liability.

Not every accident will lead to a personal injury lawsuit, but a civil suit could be an option for a victim who is paralyzed due to someone else�s actions. As soon as possible after a paralyzing accident has occurred, you should begin the process of exploring your legal options. In fact, medications may sometimes be detrimental to a patient�s health. When patients or their physicians are not aware of the potential side effects or complications from taking a medication, the drug manufacturer may be held liable for the damages that ensue.

A McDonough dangerous drugs lawyer could speak with you about your experiences with a medication that caused you harm. Together, you and an experienced personal injury attorney could pursue your legal options and work to hold those responsible for your suffering accountable for their negligence.

It is often essential for a potential plaintiff to seek the assistance of a McDonough dangerous drugs attorney as soon as possible. Not doing so could potentially cause a plaintiff to lose their right to file a lawsuit or as time goes on, making their case less likely to succeed.

Under the Official Code of Georgia �9-3-33, the statute of limitations for lawsuits involving defective drugs is two years from the date of the injury or the date of discovery of the injury. Allowing this deadline to pass without filing a lawsuit could preclude the victim from taking legal action, receiving compensation, and holding the drug manufacturer liable.

These cases are time-sensitive since evidence might be lost or become more difficult to substantiate in court as time passes. The sooner an attorney could start researching a case and collecting evidence, the more reliable the evidence could be.

Unfortunately, there are times where pharmaceutical companies rush the production and marking of drugs despite the need for further testing, which can cause patients to suffer damages. Inadequate research and development could lead to pain, severe side effects, or even death in the people who take these drugs.

Compensation is usually based on the plaintiff�s damages, of which there are two categories: economic and non-economic. Damages that are related to income and expenses are objective and not generally challenging to prove. These economic damages could include loss of pay, medical expenses, or any other tangible cost.

On the other hand, subjective damages�such as pain and suffering or loss of enjoyment of life�could be more challenging to prove, as their value is not inherent. It may be in a victim�s best interest to contact a seasoned dangerous drug lawyer in McDonough who could help determine the types of non-economic damages a victim has endured.

If an injured person�s case is successful, a dangerous drugs plaintiff may either receive a settlement for their damages or an award from a civil court. Plaintiffs should note, however, that they are not required to settle. If they do not believe they have been offered a fair settlement for their injuries, their legal counsel could pursue a higher settlement or continue the process of bringing the case before a jury.

When taking medicine, you expect that the drug will help and not cause any damage to you, and you certainly do not anticipate a condition worsening by taking them. However, this expectation does not prevent medicine from sometimes making a situation worse or even outright harming you.

If you took a dangerous drug and experienced severe side effects, you may have grounds to file a lawsuit and seek restitution for your injuries. Learn how you could protect your rights by calling a seasoned McDonough dangerous drugs lawyer today.

pages.title: McDonough Defective Products Lawyer | Hazardous Products

pages.content_md:
Product manufacturers have a duty to ensure these items are reasonably designed and produced with the safety of the individuals using them in mind. Unfortunately, they do not always uphold this duty to their consumers and, as a result of negligence, harm a user of their product.

If you were harmed by a defective product, you might be wondering what recourse you have. Consider contacting a McDonough defective products lawyer who could explain your legal rights and help you analyze your potential case. With an experienced personal injury attorney by your side, you could work to hold those responsible for your damages legally liable to pay compensation.

There are many misconceptions associated with lawsuits based on injuries sustained from a defective or dangerous product. A particularly common one is that someone injured by a defective product must somehow substantiate that they either purchased the product or owned it in some financial capacity in order to bring a claim against a manufacturer.

As detailed in the Official Code of Georgia �51-1-11, injured plaintiffs are not required to provide proof that they bought a product to have a successful defective product case. With the assistance of a McDonough defective products attorney, a plaintiff could still work to hold the manufacturer of a product liable even if the injured party was merely borrowing the product when the incident occurred.

The statute of limitations is a state-specific law establishing how long a victim has to file a lawsuit. According to O.C.G.A. �9-3-33, potential defective product plaintiffs have two years from the date of their injury�or the day that their injury was discovered�to file a civil lawsuit. If they or their defective products lawyer in McDonough do not file suit within this timeframe, they might not have any legal right to pursue a lawsuit in the future.

There are exceptions to the statute of limitations, one of them being when a minor is injured or when the victim is not legally competent due to a disability or mental illness when the event occurred. In this situation, the statute would pause until the victim turns 18 or until they become legally competent.

Products can be defective for a variety of reasons, and it is up to the claimant and their attorney to substantiate these definitions in court. No matter the type of product, a defect will usually fall into one of three main categories:

- A problem with the product�s design
- A problem in the manufacturing process for a product with a non-defective design
- A failure to provide the proper consumer warnings regarding safe usage, whether on the product itself, on a tag, or in included instructions or a user�s manual

In all these cases, it is usually the manufacturer that is negligent in causing injuries to the plaintiff. However, manufacturers generally bear strict liability for their products, which means plaintiffs do not need to prove a manufacturer�s negligence in order to receive compensation for sustained damages. For help with recovering damages, consult with a knowledgeable lawyer.

Manufacturers must ensure that they are creating safe products or providing consumer warnings that a danger may be present with their product. Companies that produce defective products which lead to injury could be held accountable for their actions.

A seasoned McDonough defective products lawyer should be familiar with the defenses manufacturers may use to avoid liability and could represent your case in court, working on your behalf to hold those negligent for a defective product responsible. Reach out today to see what an experienced attorney may do for you.

pages.title: McDonough Dog bite Lawyer | Animal Attack Compensation

After a dog bite, it is imperative to seek medical attention. Also, you may want to consider seeking the assistance of a McDonough dog bite lawyer. A qualified personal injury attorney may be able to help you pursue compensation to pay for your medical bills as well as other damages you sustain.

According to the Official Code of Georgia �51-2-7, dogs must be in sight of their owner and under voice control at all times, including in off-leash dog parks. Dogs displaying aggressive or concerning behavior should be controlled or removed from the area by their owner.

In some states, the dog�s owner is liable no matter what happened leading up to the dog bite. However, Georgia does not follow this strict liability rule. Although this statute places liability for dog bites or attacks on the owner or the keeper of the animal, the plaintiff in an ensuing civil case still must prove that:

- The dog was acting dangerous or malicious before the incident, or the owner should have reasonably known that it was
- The dog�s owner was negligent by not acting to control or remove the dog

- The plaintiff sustained injury and damages

The same law applies if the dog causes injury to the plaintiff in other ways besides biting. For instance, if a dog jumps up on someone and knocks that person down, the plaintiff would still need to prove the previously mentioned points to win their civil case. A McDonough dog bite attorney may be of assistance in helping a victim prove these conditions in a civil lawsuit.

In a successful lawsuit, the plaintiff receives monetary compensation for their losses or damages. A dog bite lawyer in McDonough could help a plaintiff ascertain all the damages they suffered in relation to a dog bite incident.

Recoverable damages can be objective or subjective in nature. Some dog bite-related injuries require extensive medical care with stitches, plastic surgery, antibiotics, or even hospitalization, which result in hefty medical bills and lost wages from work. Likewise, dog bites can often be extremely painful, disfiguring, and even cause emotional trauma. In Georgia, there are no caps limiting either type of damages. Learn to more about recovering damages following a dog bite, consult with a knowledgeable lawyer.

Under Georgia law, plaintiffs in dog injury cases could be at a disadvantage. As a dog bite victim, you may want to consider protecting your rights by retaining a seasoned McDonough dog bite lawyer. For a case evaluation after a dog bite, call an attorney today.

pages.content_md:

Truck drivers have an obligation to operate their vehicles with extreme diligence. However, despite the need for more caution, truck crashes are a regular occurrence. When a truck driver breaches their duty of care, or the expected standard to which drivers are held, and causes an accident, they may be liable for the resulting injuries.

There are a variety of factors that may contribute to a collision. Some of the most common causes of tractor-trailer wrecks include distracted and drowsy drivers, DUIs, and aggressive driving. However, in a trucking accident, sometimes the trucker is not the only liable party.

If semi-truck drivers forego sleep to meet tight delivery deadlines or work additional hours at the request of their employer, their tired state could lead to a wreck. Violating hours of service could make the employer, as well as the driver, liable for an accident.

Recovering compensation for a truck accident claim first begins by proving liability, which requires demonstrating how an at-fault party departed from the expected standard of care. A traffic code violation, such as failing to stop at a stop signal, could provide evidence to prove this to the court. However, it is beneficial to have a skilled attorney investigate the cause of a crash. Even with clear evidence, a thorough review of the collision could provide a chance to identify all potentially negligent parties.

Once the injury victim, known as a plaintiff, proves liability, they may then seek to recover compensation for their injuries. Compensation typically comes from general damages and special damages.

General damages, held under the�Official Code of Georgia � 51-12-2, account for the harm that is presumably directly related to the crash. These include may a person�s physical pain, mental pain, and a diminished capacity to work. Special damages are also available after truck accidents. Unlike general damages, however, these must be specifically proven.

Special damages could include medical expenses, lost wages, and the loss of future earnings. A McDonough truck accident lawyer could work with tractor-trailer wreck victims to collect information affirming a person�s lost work hours or the cost of medical care.

Truck wrecks are more likely to cause serious injuries when compared to collisions between small passenger vehicles. The injuries you face could provide the basis for a lawsuit. pages.title: McDonough Medical Malpractice Lawyer | Doctor or Hospital Neglience
pages.description: If the negligence of a medical professional caused you harm, reach out to a McDonough medical malpractice lawyer for support and guidance.
pages.content_md:
While medical malpractice occurs in all different types of medical fields, it almost always comes as a shock to victims and their families. Patients trust in their medical providers to offer quality care, and when the services rendered fail to meet the accepted standard for their specialty, they have rights. With the help of a McDonough medical malpractice lawyer, you able to recover compensation for your damages through a claim.

If you or your loved one suffered a medical malpractice injury, an experienced personal injury attorney could help. While the medical malpractice claims process is extremely complex, an attorney may be able to serve as a guide to help you recover the compensation you deserve.

Medical malpractice injuries could occur during the course of almost any type of medical treatment. Some of the most common injuries caused by negligent healthcare professionals include:

- Misdiagnosis or delayed diagnosis
- Birth injuries
- Surgical errors
- Medication and pharmaceutical errors
- Anesthesia errors

Most of these injuries do not automatically mean that a person has an actionable claim. Consequently, it is important to determine how specifically an injury occurred to understand liability.

Depending on the circumstances of the medical malpractice injury, there are a few parties who could potentially bear liability for causing the plaintiff’s damages. The medical provider themselves, their parent corporation, hospital, practice group, or medical facility could all be liable depending on the specific circumstances. A medical malpractice attorney in McDonough could help examine the circumstances to understand fault.

In a medical malpractice claim, injured patients may be eligible for a variety of economic damages and noneconomic damages. Economic damages are financial losses that are generally relatively easy to calculate. These include medical bills, surgical repair or revision costs, hospital stays, pain medication, rehabilitation, and lost wages due to missed time at work.

Noneconomic damages are harder to calculate and include intangible losses such as pain and suffering, the loss of ability to pursue favorite hobbies, career, or educational goals, and mental anguish. If someone’s medical malpractice injuries caused them to lose their life, their family may be eligible for wrongful death damages.

There are several different factors a court may consider when determining whether medical malpractice took place. In the mere event that a medical provider made a mistake or failed to provide the best treatment does not mean they necessarily committed medical malpractice. Preferably, the court will ask whether the medical provider’s conduct breached the accepted standard of care owed to their patients.

To determine what the accepted standard of care is, the court may consult the testimony of medical experts or specialists who work in the same field of medicine about what they may have done in a similar situation. A skilled McDonough attorney could work to establish that the medical provider breached the standard of care in their treatment of the medical malpractice plaintiff.

Whatever the extent or severity of a patient’s injury, a compassionate McDonough medical malpractice lawyer could help plaintiffs and their families that seek to hold the negligent medical provider accountable. To learn more about your rights and options, call today for a free consultation.

- A negligent vehicle driver and their insurer
- A commercial parent company employing a driver who caused or contributed to a victim’s motorcycle accident
- The entity charged with maintaining safe roadways
- The motorcycle manufacturer or distributor

A well-versed McDonough motorcycle accident attorney could help individuals evaluate the circumstances of their accident and determine the possible liable parties.

Courts consider whether the injured individual wore a helmet and several other factors when determining liability for motorcycle accidents. While Georgia requires all motorcycle riders to wear protective headgear, the statute is vague when it comes to describing what exactly constitutes protective headgear.

While the penalty for violating the Georgia helmet law for motorcycle riders is only a minimal fine of around $15, it is possible that the injured individual could be found partially responsible for their injuries if they failed to wear protective headgear. This could negatively affect their claim. A seasoned attorney could explain how a case could be affected by these laws.

Georgia operates under the modified comparative negligence rule. This law allows individuals who are found to be partially at fault to still recover compensation for their injuries, so long as they were no more than 50 percent responsible.

Those who are found over 50 percent liable for the accident may be ineligible to seek compensation from the other party. For this reason, it is important to work with a knowledgeable McDonough motorcycle accident lawyer who may be able to refute claims of comparative negligence and help to prove the negligence of the other party.

Being involved in a motorcycle accident could be a jarring experience. You may be left unsure of what to do next. Even if you believe you are partially at fault for the accident, you still have rights under the law. A dedicated McDonough motorcycle accident lawyer could explain your options and be by your side throughout the legal process.

- Physical abuse � hitting, slapping, pinching, hair-pulling, pushing, kicking, and dropping residents or allowing them to fall

A compassionate nursing home abuse attorney in McDonough could help individuals file their claim and seek compensation.

With the help of a hard-working attorney, an individual could recover many types of damages depending on the specific circumstances. Non-economic damages do not have a specific monetary value. These could include:

pages.title: McDonough Premises Liability Lawyer | Negligent Property Owner
pages.description: Speak with a McDonough premises liability lawyer if you were injured due to a property owner's negligence or carelessness.
pages.content_md:
Property owners have a responsibility to maintain a reasonably safe property for visitors. When they fail to warn visitors about the potential dangers or of a hazardous condition, they could be held liable for any injuries that result.

If you or a loved one suffered an injury on the property of another person or entity, a McDonough premises liability lawyer could help. A diligent personal injury attorney could help you understand your rights and whether you are entitled to recover damages in compensation.

Premises liability accidents could occur anywhere, from sports and recreation facilities, transportation carriers, and amusement parks, to restaurants, schools, public offices, and private residences. Not every accident or injury that occurs on another person�s property will automatically result in a premises liability claim. As an alternative, the courts typically look at a variety of factors to determine whether the property owner or management acted recklessly or unreasonably. A property owner could be considered negligent if they:

- Knew or should have known about the hazard, or should have discovered the problem when regularly inspecting the property, but did nothing to correct the issue
- Failed to conduct regular inspections for potential dangers, especially hazards known to commonly occur
- Failed to take steps to remedy the hazards within a reasonable time frame
- Failed to warn customers or patrons of potential hazards, such as displaying proper warning signs

No matter how the accident occurred, a skilled attorney in McDonough could investigate and determine whether a premises liability case has merit.

There are many ways in which an individual could sustain an injury on another person�s property. Some of the ways an individual could become injured include slipping, tripping, or falling, sustaining an animal bite or food poisoning, or being exposed to fires, burns, explosions, or toxins. When a person fails to maintain their property, severe injuries could occur. These may include:

- Head trauma
- Organ damage
- Disfigurement
- Scarring
- Spinal and vertebrae injury
- Broken bones
- Fractures, sprains, and strains
- Loss of limb

A well-practiced McDonough premises liability lawyer could speak to medical professionals to understand the nature of your injuries and collect the proper documentation to help prove the responsible party�s negligence.

Georgia operates in accordance with a standard called modified comparative negligence. Under this rule, individuals who are partially responsible for causing their injuries could have their recoverable compensation reduced by the percentage of fault they shared. So long as the plaintiff is not more than 49 percent at fault for the accident, they may still be able to receive compensation from the other negligent party.

A tenacious premises liability lawyer in McDonough has experience combating claims of comparative negligence on behalf of the plaintiff. This could give a person the best chance of recovering the compensation they deserve.

When landlords, business owners, managers, and other property owners invite or allow others to visit their premises, visitors have a reasonable expectation that the property is safe for its intended use. When property owners fall short of this expectation, they may be held liable for any injury an individual may sustain.

It is best to speak to an experienced McDonough premises liability lawyer who could help analyze the accident and determine whether the property owner or management is responsible. You may be eligible to seek compensation. Call today to get started on your claim.

pages.title: McDonough Slip and Fall Lawyer | Trip and Fall Claims
pages.description: A McDonough slip and fall lawyer could help you file a claim and recover the damages you deserve following a slip and fall injury.
pages.content_md:
After you are hurt on the property of another, you may face medical expenses and the substantial pain of your injuries. However, you may have a chance to recover. In McDonough, property owners have a legal obligation to keep their property safe for visitors.

Filing a slip and fall lawsuit is a way of potentially recovering for any injuries and financial losses you incur because of an injury. After falling, a McDonough slip and fall lawyer could explain your rights, document your injuries, and help you file a premises liability lawsuit to seek compensation. Call today and set up a consultation with a dedicated personal injury attorney.

Slip and fall cases are a type of premises liability action that is usually based on the legal theory of negligence. To recover for a slipping accident, those injured are asked to prove that a property owner owed a duty of care, breached their assigned duty, and caused injuries as a result.

This legal duty of care typically includes checking for and cleaning spills, ensuring carpets and handrails are secure, and ensuring that there are not clear hazards on a property. A McDonough slip and fall attorney could help prove liability in a falling accident claim by demonstrating that, if not for the property owner�s negligence, the accident would not have occurred. This may include a detailed investigation to demonstrate that the property owner knew of a hazardous condition but failed to take reasonable care to protect those on the property.

A property owner�s duty changes depending on the status of the people who enter their property. To this effect, one of the most important steps in a slip and fall accident claim is to determine the injured person�s status at the time of the accident. The Georgia legislature has created three different classifications for purposes of premises liability. Under the law, individuals are considered invitees, licensees, or trespassers. To learn how these classifications may impact a claim, contact a knowledgeable lawyer.

Invitees are those who are invited onto the property through an express or implied invitation. For example, when a person goes to a grocery store to purchase food, they are typically considered an invitee. Under the Official Code of Georgia � 51-3-1, property owners are expected to keep property safe from hazards.

Licensees are people who are �neither a customer, a servant, nor trespasser, does not stand in any contractual relation with the owner of the premises; and is permitted, expressly or impliedly, to go on the premises merely for his own interests, convenience, or gratification� (O.C.G.A. �51-3-2). Property owners are usually not liable if a licensee is hurt unless there is evidence that a willful or wanton act of negligence caused the injury.

The final classification of those in a premises liability action is trespassers. As outlined in O.C.G.A. �51-3-3, a property owner does not owe a trespasser any obligation of care, expect to refrain from willful acts of negligence.

Slip and fall accidents are more than just an inconvenience. They may cause serious injuries such as broken bones, traumatic brain injuries, sprains, and strains. A McDonough slip and fall lawyer could help prove liability in a slip and fall case by connecting a property owner�s negligence with your injuries. Connect with an attorney today to schedule a free consultation, discuss your case, outline your classification, and determine the potential for compensation.

If another person�s negligent actions caused a loved one�s death, a compassionate McDonough wrongful death lawyer is prepared to offer guidance and legal support. Working with an experienced personal injury attorney could be the key to holding the negligent party liable for their actions.

Wrongful death is broadly defined as death caused by another�s negligent, careless, or deliberate action. Under Georgia�s wrongful death statute, wrongful demise includes homicide and any cases in which a person passes due to the negligence of another, or because of a defective product.

The laws surrounding wrongful death also detail who may bring a wrongful demise action and who could recover damages. Defined in Official Georgia Code � 51-4-2, a surviving spouse can bring forth action. In the case there is not a surviving spouse, a surviving child or children could bring forth legal claims with the assistance of a practiced wrongful death attorney in McDonough.

It may be important to properly determine the amount of damages available in a wrongful death case. To do this, an attentive McDonough wrongful death lawyer could examine the specific facts and financial impact of a case with respect to O.C.G.A. � 51-4-1 (1). Under this statue, surviving family members may seek the full value of a deceased person�s life, which is typically supported with evidence. The full value of life may include many factors, such as:

- Funeral expenses
- Loss of future wages
- Loss of companionship
- Pain and suffering
- Medical expenses

Additionally, punitive damages may be available in wrongful death actions. These damages are meant to punish the negligent party for egregious and reckless behavior. Consulting with a dedicated lawyer after a negligent death could help families determine the potential value of a legal case.

There are many scenarios that may serve as the basis of a wrongful death claim. Some of the most common include:

- Poor medical care
- Automobile wrecks
- Workplace accidents
- Drunk driving
- Broken medical devices
- Nursing home abuse and neglect

Regardless of the actual injury, every wrongful passing shares common elements. For a legal action, the deceased person must have suffered a fatal injury because of another person�s negligence.

After a period of mourning, families of the deceased may wish to contact an attorney to discuss the death. During this time, a wrongful death lawyer could help advise on when to file a lawsuit, if the family so wishes. Under Georgia�s statute of limitations, the qualifying individual has two years from the date of a person�s death to file a wrongful death claim.

Losing a loved one is always trying, but it can be easily difficult to process if the death was unexpected or due to another�s negligent behavior. In these situations, an empathetic McDonough wrongful death lawyer could help answer your questions, explain liability, and diligently pursue compensation for your lost loved one�s case. pages.title: Newnan Personal Injury Lawyer | Filing a Civil Lawsuit
pages.description: Contact a Newnan personal injury lawyer today to seek damages for injuries sustained and ensure that you know what to expect throughout the claims process.
pages.content_md:
When people become injured as the result of the act of another, they can often be confused and disoriented. Their first priority should be to make a full physical and mental recovery.

Unfortunately, mounting medical bills, lost time at work and repairing any property damage can distract people from this goal. On top of that, the very people who should be there to help in the process, the insurance companies, often add chaos to the situation.

Our firm�s Newnan personal injury lawyers are here to help. Our injury attorneys handle the details, deal with the insurance companies, and fight for the fair compensation that you deserve so that you can place your focus where it belongs: on getting your life back to normal.

The types of personal injury cases are as varied as there are ways for people to become hurt. The common thread is that a person becomes hurt as the result of another person�s actions. In some instances, the defendant is not a person but a business.

For example, if a person slips and falls on a spill in a grocery store, the proper defendant is not the clerk who failed to clean the spill, but the store itself. Identifying the proper defendant in any personal injury case is an important first step.

A second step involves identifying a cause of action. A cause of action is a legally recognized theory of a case that allows a plaintiff to sue for damages. While there are some instances of causes of action that have been created by legislative statutes, most causes of actions are created by the courts in common law.

The common law is simply a collection of court rulings passed down over the years that courts in the same jurisdiction are required to follow.

While there are certainly instances of intentional acts resulting in personal injury, such as assault or false imprisonment, most personal injury cases are the result of accidents. Accidents are usually pursued under the legal theory of negligence.

Simply put, the law creates a responsibility for some people to protect others. When that responsibility is broken, and a person is hurt, the person carrying the responsiblity is liable. Common personal injury cases such as car accidents, slip and falls, and premises liability claims are all pursued by Newnana injury attorneys using negligence.

The potential avenues for pursing damages are varied. There is the obvious route of suing for the cost of medical bills, lost wages, physical therapy and property damages. These damages are easily measured by a Newnan personal injury lawyer.

What is more nebulous are damages due to mental anguish. Pain and suffering is the most common category of mental damages, but these can also include:

- Loss of enjoyment of life,
- Loss of consortium, and
- Loss of your physical contributions at work or home.

When considering non-physical damages, attorneys often utilize the expert opinions of economists and workplace experts to determine the full value of a person�s change in life due to an injury.

People becoming injured as the result of others� actions have the absolute right to demand that the responsible party pay for the harm that they have caused. Unfortunately, defendants are often represented by insurance companies that make a profit by denying people those very payments.

Our firm�s Newnan personal injury lawyers represent clients in dealing with those insurance companies so that they can focus on their recovery.

By gathering all of the evidence, talking to witnesses and forming a strong demand package, most cases settle without needing to go to court. If a trial is necessary, our litigators are here to guide you through the process and to present your case to the jury.

Do not take any chances with your future and take a positive step towards getting the fair compensation that you deserve; contact our firm today.

pages.title: Newnan Car Accident Lawyer | Car Crash Injury Claims Attorney
pages.description: If another's negligence has caused an auto accident, seek damages for any injuries caused with the assistance of a Newnan car accident lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
When a person has the misfortune of being involved in a car accident, it is understandable that they would be confused and upset. While some accidents result in immediate apparent harm, in others, the injuries only manifest themselves in the days following the accident.

The main priority of all people involved in car accidents should be to make a full recovery. Unfortunately, the deluge of paperwork and red tape that a person must fight through makes for a powerful distraction. Our firm�s Newnan car accident lawyers are here to help.

Our experienced personal injury attorneys handle all of the paperwork and represent your interests to fight for the maximum compensation that you deserve for your injuries. Take the first step towards getting the compensation that you deserve, and contact our firm�s car accident attorneys today.

While come collisions between cars are the result of intentional acts, car accidents are usually exactly that � accidents. Because of this, most car accident cases are pursued under the legal theory of negligence.

Negligence is when a person owes a duty to protect another from harm, and through an action, or inaction, causes that protected person to come to harm. That failure to protect another person is usually the result of what we would call negligent behavior.

Consider the example of a person sitting in their car at a red light. That person is then rear-ended by a pickup truck, resulting in a strained neck. There are five parts, or elements, of a negligence claim that must be met by a Newnan car accident lawyer:

- Duty � Duty is present when a person has a responsibility to protect another from harm. This duty is imposed upon them by law, but a person does not automatically have a duty simply by existing. In car accident cases, all drivers assume a duty to drive in a careful manner. In our example, the pickup driver always has a duty to drive in a way that does not place others in harm�s way.
- Breach � The duty to protect others is broken, or breached, when a person takes an action that causes others to come to harm. In our example, the pickup driver breached his duty when he rear-ended the car at the red light because he should have stopped before the collision.
- Cause � The plaintiff needs to show that his injuries were caused by the defendant�s breach of duty. He cannot say that his neck was strained before the collision and hope to win his case.
- Scope � The injuries suffered must have been foreseeable from the facts of the case. Car accidents can cause very serious injuries or even death. As a result, scope is not usually at issue in these claims.
- Damages � The plaintiff must have suffered actual physical harm from the accident. Mental stress on its own is insufficient for a claim, but can be added on in addition to physical harms. Here, the neck strain certainly qualifies and the plaintiff may clam additional pain and suffering as a result of his injuries.

Another thing to remember is that car accident cases have a statute of limitations. This is a time limit that a plaintiff must meet to file his case in court. If the plaintiff does not meet this deadline, his case will be dismissed.

For cases involving only losses to personal property, this limit is four years from the date of loss according to GA Code 9-3-32. Plaintiffs have only two years to file a suit for all cases alleging personal injury under GA Code 9-3-33.

If you have been injured in a car accident because of another driver�s negligence, contact our firm�s Newnan car accident lawyers. We work with clients to better understand their case; from the facts of the accident, through their medical costs, to lost wages and property damage.

We will take care of the details and negotiate with the insurance company from a position of strength so that you can focus on your recovery.

Most cases settle out of court, but if a lawsuit does need to be filed, we are at your side every step of the way. Insurance companies can sometimes take advantage of unrepresented plaintiffs. They can push you to approve undervalued settlement offers, prior to your case becoming fully developed.

Our firm�s car accident attorneys present thorough and nuanced demand packages to fight for maximum compensation. Time is of the essence; contact our firm today.

pages.title: Newnan Medical Malpractice Lawyer | Medical Negligence Claims
