pages.content_md:
Patients place a large amount of trust into the hands of medical care providers, including doctors, nurses, and other healthcare specialists. In return, they expect to receive the right care from healthcare providers. When you are injured or otherwise harmed following the medical care you receive, you may want to explore legal recourse, usually in the form of suing for medical malpractice.

However, not all injuries and even deaths, are the result of actual medical malpractice, so legal action may not be feasible. If you or a close relative suffered injury and you believe the injury to be the result of medical malpractice, a skilled savvy personal injury attorney can help bring you peace of mind.

Certain injuries that are a result of medical procedures are unavoidable, even if a medical care provider has taken every step to ensure the best care possible. However, injuries can be the result of medical malpractice if they are caused by:

- Misdiagnosis, non-diagnosis, or failure to inform a patient of a diagnosis

- Surgical errors
- Infections that result from improper care

Because of the complexity of filing a successful lawsuit�including the process of discovery, filing motions, and acquiring expert research�it may be important to contact a Newnan medical malpractice lawyer who can help overwhelmed patients through the process.

Successfully demonstrating that a doctor, nurse, hospital, PPO, HMO, or any other medical professional was responsible for medical malpractice leading to injury can be quite difficult. For a successful medical malpractice case, the claim must be able to prove two elements:

- A medical professional failed to meet the medical standard reasonably expected of them, given the injured patient�s conditions
- There was a direct causation between the treatment the patient received, did not receive, or improperly received, and the resulting injury

Consulting medical experts and acquiring the documents necessary to prove what care was or was not given can require relentless advocacy. A dedicated medical malpractice attorney has the resources and personal connections needed to make successful claims possible.

Medical malpractice injuries can often have devastating long-term effects on patients, their loved ones, and close friends. Additionally, successfully demonstrating that your injuries were a result of a health care provider�s negligence can be an overwhelming process.

pages.content_md:
When motorcycle riders are involved in a collision with another vehicle, it can be a frightening situation. Bikers are placed in a vulnerable position while riding, that can lead to serious injuries. On top of this, it can take a long time for a person to make a mental recovery after such an accident.

Motorcycle riders are protected by the same legal doctrines enjoyed by all other motorists, and claims for personal injury resulting from other people�s negligence must be respected.

Our firm�s Newnan motorcycle accident lawyers work with clients who have been injured in accidents with both compassion and aggressiveness to obtain the fair compensation that they deserve for their physical and mental injuries.

Most motorcycle accident cases revolve around the legal concept of negligence. This is because most accidents between motorcycles and other vehicles are exactly that � accidents.

While there are certainly cases where a motorcyclist is hit intentionally, the vast majority of these claims are the result of accidental collisions.

Negligence is the idea that certain people owe a legal responsibility to protect others and by an action that they take or fail to take, cause harm to come to that protected party. There are five portions, or elements, that must be met by the plaintiff or their Newnan motorcycle accident lawyer for a successful negligence claim:

- Duty � In certain circumstances, people have a responsibility, or duty, to ensure that others do not come to harm. All motorists have this duty to protect other drivers and pedestrians when they are behind the wheel. This, of course, extends to bikers. Because of this, the duty element is not often contested in a motorcycle accident negligence case.
- Breach � The plaintiff must demonstrate that the defendant�s actions, or lack of actions, caused the defendant to fail in their duty to protect others from harm. Examples of this can be speeding, rear-ending, or improper lane changes. Whether or not the at-fault driver�s actions constitute a breach of the duty of care is often the central issue in negligence cases.
- Cause � It must be proven that the accident was the proximate cause of the injuries; for example, that being knocked off his bike caused the plaintiff to break his arm. Insurance companies will often attempt to argue that the injuries were not caused by the accident, but were pre-existing.
- Scope � The plaintiff must show that the injuries were foreseeable from the defendant�s negligence. This is generally not contested in a motorcycle accident case as collisions between motorcycles and other vehicles are expected to result in significant injury.
- Damages � A plaintiff must be able to show that there are physical injuries resulting from the defendant�s negligence. This can be any condition diagnosed by a doctor, but can also include property damage. Mental injuries, such as pain and suffering, can certainly be added onto the claim, but are insufficient to stand on their own.

One other thing to keep in mind is that all civil lawsuits have a statute of limitations. In short, this is a time limit that a plaintiff must meet to file his case in court. If the case is not filed within this limit, the defendant can make a motion that the case be dismissed, and the judge will almost always grant this request.

For cases involving only losses to personal property, this limit is four years from the date of loss according to GA Code 9-3-32. Plaintiffs have only two years to file a suit for all cases alleging personal injury under GA Code 9-3-33.

Victims in motorcycle collisions have enough to worry about with making a full recovery from their injuries.

Our firm�s Newnan motorcycle accident attorneys assist clients in the recuperative process by submitting required paperwork with insurance companies, gathering evidence from doctors and witnesses, and authoring demand packages in an attempt to settle the case out of court.

Utilizing this aggressive yet steady method, many cases are settled before going to court, but if a lawsuit does need to be filed, our firm�s litigators will guide you every step of the way and stand by your side.

Contact our firm today to see how we can form a comprehensive strategy to get you the compensation you deserve.

pages.content_md:
When people are involved in collisions with commercial trucks, the damages can be life-changing. Tractor trailers and construction vehicles dwarf even large SUV�s and subject people to significant forces upon impact.

Our firm�s Newnan truck accident lawyers work with clients who have been injured in collisions with commercial trucks to obtain the compensation that they deserve. For information regarding your case, call and schedule a consultation with one of our accident attorneys today.

Truck accident cases are usually based on the legal theory of negligence. Negligence applies when an injury is the result of an accident, but the at-fault person did not take proper care to protect others.

Negligence is defined as when a person has a legally conferred responsibility to protect another and that protected person comes to harm. More precisely, there are five parts, or elements, of a negligence claim that a Newnan truck accident lawyer must deal with:

- Duty � This is the legal responsibility that some people have to ensure that no harm comes to others. Duty is created by specific circumstances and is not automatically present in all negligence cases. In the case of a truck accident, the driver of the truck has a duty to drive with appropriate caution to prevent harm to passengers, drivers, and pedestrians. Therefore, cases involving truck accidents universally cover the duty requirement.
- Breach � A breach is the failure of a person who has a duty to protect others to prevent harm. A breach can occur through a person�s action, such as speeding, but also by a person�s failure to take action, such as ignoring a stop sign. Truck drivers who are speeding, fail to stop at red lights, or drive recklessly are often in breach of their duty. This is the element most often in contention in truck accident cases.
- Cause � Plaintiffs need to demonstrate that the breach of duty was the cause of their injuries. If for example, a person�s leg is broken in an accident with a truck, the plaintiff will need to prove to the jury that the accident was the cause of the broken leg. Insurance companies may try to argue that the injury was pre-existing, and therefore not caused by the accident.
- Scope � In this element, the plaintiff must show that the injuries were foreseeable based on the breach of duty. In truck accident cases, this is almost a given, as large vehicles colliding can certainly cause significant injuries or even death.
- Damages � Lastly, the plaintiff must have physical injuries that are documented by medical professionals. For this reason, consistent medical care is extremely important for a successful claim. Mental injuries, such as pain and suffering, can be added onto a claim, but are insufficient to stand on their own.

One other aspect of the law to remember is that truck accident cases have a statute of limitations. In short, this is a time limit that a plaintiff must meet to file their case in court. If the deadline expires, the defendant will argue that the case should be dismissed, and the judge will almost always accept this argument.

For cases involving only losses to personal property, this limit is four years from the date of loss according to GA Code 9-3-32. For all cases alleging personal injury, plaintiffs have only two years to file a suit under GA Code 9-3-33.

In contrast to many peoples� understanding, most truck accident cases are settled without ever going to court.

Our firm�s Newnan truck accident attorneys will gather all medical evidence, examine police reports, talk to witnesses, and negotiate with insurance companies to end cases quickly, but also with maximum compensation for our clients.

pages.title: Newnan Wrongful Death Lawyer | Survival Action Claims
pages.description: If your loved one has recently passed away as the result of another�s intentional or accidental act, our firm�s Newnan wrongful death lawyers can help.
pages.content_md:
When a family loses a loved one, it can be difficult to see a way forward. If the death was caused by a criminal act, the justice system will file charges and prosecute a case against the defendant.

But many people do not realize that regardless of the outcome of a criminal case, the family of the deceased still has a civil claim to make against the defendant. The same can be said of a death caused by an accident.

If your loved one has recently passed away as the result of another�s intentional or accidental act, our firm�s Newnan wrongful death lawyers are here to help.

By filing a civil claim for wrongful death with the assistance of an injury attorney, a family can be compensated for the suffering endured by their loved one and can take a step towards moving forward in their lives.

Georgia has passed no statute defining a wrongful death. Instead, the state�s courts have defined a wrongful death as any death that was caused by the intentional act, recklessness, or negligence of another. However, a plaintiff in these cases cannot list �wrongful death� as the core reason for their suit.

This is because civil lawsuits must allege what is known as a cause of action. These are a limited list of legal concepts, defined by the courts, that plaintiffs can use to file lawsuits. Examples of these include:

- Assault
- Products Liability
- Negligence, and
- Premises Liability

Once the plaintiff and their Newnan wrongful death attorney have chosen a cause of action that fits the facts of the case, they can then allege that this underlying cause of action resulted in the death of their loved one.

Another complicated aspect of a wrongful death claim is choosing the proper plaintiff. Of course, the person against whom the harm was inflicted cannot file a lawsuit. In general, a surviving spouse may be named as a plaintiff in a suit alleging wrongful death under GA Code 51-4-2.

Any surviving children over the age of eighteen may also be plaintiffs if the act resulted in the death of both of their parents.

However, if the children are under the age of 18, they cannot be the named plaintiff in a lawsuit. Instead, the court will require that the executor of the deceased�s estate to file the suit on behalf of the children.

Regardless of the means by which a plaintiff is found, Georgia ensures that a defendant cannot escape liability if there is a potential plaintiff who wishes to come forward.

Further complicating matters is the fact that two separate lawsuits must be filed for full compensation to be awarded. The first is defined in GA Code 51-4-2(a) as being for the �full value of the life of the decedent.� This is a somewhat nebulous concept that requires consultation with economic experts and a Newnan wrongful death lawyer.

These experts determine a person�s economic potential if they were to continue earing wages for the rest of their lives. Additionally, the full life value includes intangible things, like family interactions and life experiences.

The second suit is related, but deals with more tangible damages such as funeral costs, medical bills, and any suffering endured by the deceased prior to death. While somewhat easier to calculate due to exact costs of medical bills, pain and suffering is still open to interpretation.

Unlike in some states, there is no monetary limit imposed on a wrongful death suit.

The rule is described by Georgia�s courts as, ��the value of the child�s life must be established by the enlightened conscience of an impartial factfinder as applied to evidence of the case�� Chrysler Group, LLC v. Walden, S.E.2d (2016) quoting *Collins v. McPherson*, 91 Ga.App. 347, 349 (1) (1954). In short, it states that any verdict can be awarded as long as it is not totally unreasonable.

Nothing can bring your loved one back into your life or fully soothe the pain caused by the loss. But our firm�s Newnan wrongful death attorneys can help through handling your case with both compassion and vigor to bring your family peace of mind and future economic security.

By initiating a civil lawsuit, the deceased�s family can bring the person or corporation responsible for your loved one�s death to accountability. Regardless of whether criminal charges are filed against the defendant, or if the defendant was convicted, the decedent�s family may still file a civil suit.

This suit can claim damages for not only the medical costs and funeral expenses associated with the death, but also for future economic harm due to lost earning potential and any suffering endured by the decedent. There is a strict time limit wherein a plaintiff must file suit, so time is of the essence. Contact our firm today.

pages.content_md:

The American Burn Association finds that there were 486,000 burn injuries in the United States that required hospitalization in 2016. Over 60% of the estimated U.S. acute hospitalizations related to burn injuries required specialized treatment at one of the nation�s 128 burn centers.

Based on the severity of a burn, it can be classified into one of four different degrees.

- First degree
- Second degree
- Third degree
- Fourth degree

A first degree burn is a superficial burn that affects the outermost layers of the skin. Outwardly, the skin appears red without any blisters and lasts from days to weeks.

A second degree burn not only fully penetrates the outer�or epidermal�layer of skin, but also extends into the dermal layer of the skin. Afflicted skin will be bright red with blisters and swelling, is often painful to the touch, and may warrant significant medical treatment. Second-degree burns may leave a scar or permanently change the color of affected skin.

A third degree burn fully penetrates both the epidermis and dermis. The burn site may appear black, brown, white or yellow, and is generally not be painful to the touch, since third-degree burns usually extend deep enough into the skin to damage nerve endings.

A fourth degree burn injury is the most severe type of burn. In this case, the burn extends beyond the skin layer into muscle, bone, or even internal organs. Fourth degree burns almost always require hospitalization and surgery, and in particularly severe cases may be fatal.

Based on the severity of the burn, recoverable damages in a Phenix City burn injury case may vary. Necessary medical treatment may range from out-patient consultations to surgery to repair the damage made by the burns.

- Loss of enjoyment of life

Contact a Phenix City burn injury lawyer for experienced legal assistance today, so you can focus on making a full recovery.

If the error directly caused the harm claimed by the injured party, the party responsible for their injuries may be held liable for damages.

pages.content_md:
Alabama premises liability is governed by common law. This means that instead of a body of statutes controlling this area of the law, a Phenix City attorney and the courts will look to judicial or case law when analyzing a claim. Premises liability law can apply to accidents which occur in a variety of places, including private homes, construction sites, restaurants, and apartment buildings�any area where a landowner has a duty to keep the area safe.

If you have suffered an injury�on a private party, speak with an experienced attorney today. A Phenix City premises liability lawyer may be able to provide you with the legal counsel you deserve.

Premises liability accidents can occur due to:

- Slippery or hazardous conditions
- Unsafe common areas of an apartment complex
- Poorly lit areas
- Elevator or escalator accidents
- Children on the property
- Unmarked dangerous areas, (i.e. holes in floors or live electrical wires)

These types of hazardous or dangerous conditions on a property can lead to serious injuries such as broken or fractured bones, concussions, sprains and bruises, and�in particularly severe cases�even death. By retaining a Phenix City premises liability lawyer, you could benefit from their years of expertise in handling negotiations with the defendant�s counsel and insurance companies.

When someone is on someone else�s property, their classification under premises liability law determines the landowner�s duty of care owed to them. Under Alabama common law, there are three levels of protection a visitor may be afforded while on the premises of another person.

An invitee is a person on the premises with the landowner’s consent or as his social guests, such as a houseguest or a customer in a retail store. Here, there is a duty of the landowner to keep the premises in a reasonably safe condition.

A licensee is a person who is invited to the premises by the landowner and usually receives a material benefit, such as a contractor or a landscaper. Here, the landowner owes a duty to not willfully, wantonly, or negligently injure their visitor. For both invitees and licensees, the landowner must warn of hidden defects and dangers that exist on the premises.

A trespasser is a person who enters the premises without an invitation from the landowner. Alabama law states that a trespasser is not owed a duty of care. However, the landowner cannot intentionally set traps or create dangerous conditions to harm trespassers. Speak with a�Phenix City premises liability Lawyer to learn more.

Proving negligence of the landowner is an area of law where a premises liability attorney in Phenix City may have significant expertise. A successful claim of negligence on the basis of premises liability satisfies the following elements of legal negligence by a preponderance of evidence:

- The landowner owed their visitor a duty of care
- The duty of care was breached
- The breach of care directly caused an accident
- The accident caused damages to the visitor

Code of Alabama �6-11-1 provides that damages for personal injury can be assessed as past, future, or punitive in nature. Within these categories, a Phenix City premises liability lawyer may be able to facilitate recovery for the costs of medical bills, lost wages, lost earning capacity, and pain and suffering.

In addition, Code of Alabama �6-2-38 allows plaintiffs two years to commence a claim of personal injury for wrongful or negligent actions leading to injury.

A Phenix City premises liability lawyer is available to guide you through the process of filing your claim and help alleviate any worries you encounter while dealing with your injuries. Do not hesitate to call and get started on your case today.

- Cracked or broken walkways and sidewalks
- Dimly lit passageways, stairs, and walkways
- Carpet that is torn or loose
- Broken handholds or handrails

In these examples, a slip or fall is more likely to occur than on a property that is maintained in a clean and safe manner. A landowner who knows their premises will be visited by members of the public and does not repair these dangerous conditions may be held responsible for injuries these defects cause.

The first step in any slip and fall case is for the victim to seek out and receive any medical care they need for their injuries. It is important to document all injuries and save all medical bills and reports, as this documentation of the condition of the premises where the fall occurred may be critical to a successful case.

Slip and fall cases sometimes require a victim to hire an expert to give an opinion on the cause of the slip, trip, or fall. A medical care provider may be able to testify as to the severity of an injury suffered due to a slip and fall injury and affirm that the compensation requested by the plaintiff is reasonable and needed.

Experts could also testify that a stairway was poorly designed and likely to cause a fall, or that a walkway was so poorly lit that it caused the victims slip and fall. A Phenix City slip and fall lawyer could seek out experts on a person’s behalf, then use the information they provide to build a case.

A skilled slip and fall lawyer in Phenix City could give local and personalized attention to you and your case. Slip and fall cases can be challenging to litigate effectively, and an experienced attorney may be able to anticipate the challenges in a client�s case and develop a strategy to win full and fair compensation.

pages.content_md:
Truck accidents in Phenix City can cause serious and life-changing personal injuries. A person could suffer devastating injuries and may have an extensive amount of money to pay in terms of hospital bills and insurance payments. It may be in the person’s to file a claim for compensation.

If you suffer an injury in such an accident, an experienced attorney may be able to help you get the compensation for your injuries and pain and suffering that you deserve. Speak with a Phenix City truck accident lawyer today.

The state of Alabama has experienced a substantial increase in truck accidents in recent years. The Alabama Department of Transportation reports that in 2015 there were 8,484 truck accidents in the state, which caused 2,367 injuries and 118 deaths. This report identifies the top causes of truck accidents as:

- Improper lane change or use
- Failure to yield right of way
- Unseen object, person or vehicle
- Tailgating
- Misjudged stopping distance
- Defective equipment
- Improper turn

First and foremost, the facts of the loss should be established, and physical evidence and witness statements should be documented as close to the time of the accident as possible.

Skid marks and road debris will generally be cleaned within a few hours, so it is often a good idea to take photographs of an accident scene if possible, as these details can be critical to determining how the accident happened and which driver is at fault. Witnesses to the accident should also be contacted and have their version of events recorded before time passes and details are forgotten.

Drivers injured in truck accidents often need medical care to treat their injuries. In particularly severe cases, a truck accident victim will be transported to the emergency room and receive treatment for their critical injuries, but even if this does not happen, it is best for anyone involved in an accident to independently seek out treatment as soon as possible to ensure they are not suffering any lingering medical effects.

Follow-up medical care, doctor visits, physical therapy or chiropractic care needed to treat the long-term effects of truck accident injuries can be significantly expensive, particularly when injuries are severe. A skilled�Phenix City truck accident lawyer could help and advise people on how to document and pursue compensation for medical bills and damages.

When an accident victim fully recovers from their injuries or has reached a stage where a serious personal injury has stabilized, they could enlist the help of a Phenix City truck accident attorney to negotiate a settlement that compensates them for their injuries.

If an agreement is not reached, a lawyer could proceed to file a lawsuit against the responsible parties and advocate on a person’s behalf throughout the civil court system until satisfied that person’s best interests are met.

When presenting truck accident claims and fighting to win full compensation for a person’s losses, an experienced Phenix City truck accident lawyer typically focuses on the first hours and days after the accident, as this time is often critical to a successful outcome of an accident case.

A qualified and compassionate Phenix City truck accident lawyer is available to meet with anyone injured in a truck accident to help them understand their rights. If you need legal assistance with your truck accident case in Phenix City, you could contact an attorney today for an initial consultation and have all their questions answered with experienced legal advice.

pages.title: Phenix City Wrongful Death Lawyer | Traumatic Fatalities
pages.description: If a loved one has suffered a wrongful death in Phenix City, you may be entitled to compensation. Speak with a Phenix City wrongful death lawyer to learn more.
pages.content_md:
While monetary compensation cannot make up for the death of a family member, families that lose a loved one because of the wrongful acts of another could be entitled to a financial recovery to help manage medical and funeral expenses, as well as offer restitution for emotional and relational damages.

There is a limited time to bring a wrongful death claim in Phenix City, so you may need to contact an experienced attorney as soon as possible for help successfully pursuing compensation in your case. Speak with a Phenix City wrongful death lawyer today.

For a wrongful death case to be valid, someone�s death must be caused by the intentional, reckless, or negligent acts of another person. By the strict legal definition of the term, an intentional act is one in which the person who caused the death acted with the intent to injure the victim, such as by committing robbery or assault with a deadly weapon.

A reckless act is one in which a person is aware of the danger of their actions, but still acts without regard for the safety of others around them. Speeding more than 15 miles per hour over the posted speed would constitute a reckless act in Phenix City.

Finally, a negligent act is one in which the person owes other people around them a duty of care, disregards this responsibility, and causes the death of the victim as a direct result of their actions. A negligent act does not require the person to intend to cause harm; for example, a driver who does not stop at a red light because they were texting on their phone likely does not intend to harm anyone, but they could still be held liable under the law if they cause an accident that leads to someone�s wrongful death.

In general, the family of a wrongful death victim can bring a claim for damages. The spouse, children, and parents of the deceased are considered family for the purposes of a wrongful death case. The claim must be brought through a personal representative, such as a Phenix City wrongful death lawyer, who is a person appointed by the Court to act on behalf of the relatives bringing the wrongful death claim.

Compensation paid out in Phenix City wrongful death claims are limited to awards designed to punish who caused the death. If a driver accidentally runs a red light and causes a wrongful death, it is possible a trial jury may not award a large amount of money to punish the driver. In contrast, if someone shoots and kills the victim in a robbery, a trial jury may be more likely to require a large financial judgment. Speak with a�Phenix City wrongful death lawyer to learn more about what compensation can be won.

The family member of someone who lost their life because of the acts of another may be best served to discuss their case with an experienced Phenix City wrongful death lawyer.

An experienced and compassionate attorney could meet with you, examine your claim, and advise you on how you could pursue financial compensation for your loved one�s wrongful death. Call today to schedule a consultation.

pages.h1: I’VE HEARD THE WORD NEGLIGENCE, BUT WHAT DOES IT MEAN?
pages.content_md:
Individuals and companies act responsibly most of the time. �However, there are times that their guard is let down, and they become irresponsible. �When that happens, people may sustain injuries or even die as a result. �An individual or company neglecting responsibility is the ground level of negligence.

Lawyers tend to define negligence as the failure of a person or company to exercise reasonable care that results in an injury or death to another person. �Negligence can result in injuries or death to people in a variety of ways, including workplace accidents,�car accidents, slip and fall accidents, medical malpractice, defective products, and more.

The victim of another person or company�s negligence can take legal action against the negligent party seeking financial compensation. �Were you injured? �Do you believe a negligent person or company caused your injuries by being negligent? �The Atlanta negligence attorneys of �The Parian Law Firm, LLC have filed lawsuits for clients all over Georgia, and we are here to help you get the financial compensation you deserve!

Injury victims have to prove that a person or company neglected to exercise the care that another reasonable person or company would have under similar circumstances. �The definition can be broken down into four distinct elements

- The Responsible Person or Company Owed a Duty to the Injured Person or the Public in General
- The Responsible Person or Company Violated that Duty
- The Violation of the Duty Caused the Injury

An example would be when a driver runs a stop sign and collides with another car causing injuries. The driver owed a duty to the public to stop at the stop sign. �The driver did not stop; therefore, he or she violated that duty. �The collision that was caused by the driver running the stop sign caused injuries to people in the other car. �In this instance, you have proven all four elements of negligence.

Hit and run accidents carry high emotional and legal uncertainty. When the at-fault driver flees the scene, you’re left with serious injuries, mounting bills, and questions about who will take responsibility.

**Why You Should Get Help Immediately**

Timing matters: evidence disappears quickly—witness memories fade, and cameras may

overwrite footage. Early action helps preserve key facts and enables investigation. Collect as

much evidence as possible: Photos of damage, street signs, skid marks, nearby surveillance

cameras, and eyewitness contact info.

**How Georgia’s Insurance Laws Apply**

Georgia law requires drivers to carry uninsured motorist (UM) coverage. If the at-fault driver can’t be

found, your own insurer should provide compensation up to your UM limit. Parian Lawyers can evaluate

your policy to ensure you’re using all available benefits.

Coverage may include:

- Medical bills
- Lost wages
- Pain and suffering

**What to Expect in the Investigation**

- Hiring investigators to look for leads (broken taillights, damage matching witnesses, vehicle
 debris).
- Working with local police who may open hit-and-run reports even when the driver is
 unidentified.
- Filing UM claims with your own insurer if the other driver remains unknown.

**Building a Strong Claim**

Pursuing a hit-and-run case can sometimes be discouraging with an offender being unidentified. It is

important to be diligent in keeping track of things to build a strong case.

- Document your medical journey—from ER visits to surgeries and follow-up therapies.
- Retain records of lost income and everyday costs arising from injuries.
- A seasoned PI attorney draws a clear narrative showing how injuries impact your daily life.

**Why Parian’s Experience Makes a Difference**

Parian Lawyers have local roots in west Georgia and deep experience fighting for crash victims—even

when the other driver isn’t identified. They have handled hitandrun injury cases with compassion,

urgency, and tenacity. A hit and run can feel overwhelming—but you don’t have to go it alone. Parian

Lawyers can help gather evidence, pursue UM coverage, and demand full compensation even when the

other driver gets away.

pages.description: If you were injured in an accident, you may be eligible for compensation. Contact a Riverdale personal injury lawyer today.
pages.content_md:
Accidents can happen anywhere and at any time. Seemingly simple incidents such as motor vehicle accidents, product malfunctions, and even tripping and falling could have tremendous consequences, and the financial strain such an accident may have on an individual and their families could be monumental.

If you were injured due to another person�s negligence, you may be able to seek compensation from the responsible party with assistance from a dedicated attorney. A Riverdale personal injury lawyer could help you learn about your legal options, work to hold the negligent party responsible for their actions, and seek compensation for your damages.

After an accident that causes personal injuries, the insurance company representing the reckless or negligent party will usually come forward with an initial settlement offer. The timing and amount of this offer is designed to make it seem like a life-saver, and that it will cover all the losses the victim has sustained.

Unfortunately, this may be a well-crafted illusion. In reality, the settlement offers that insurance companies bring forward in the immediate aftermath of an accident are often designed to drastically lowball the plaintiff by providing only a tiny fraction of the compensation they really need.

These settlement offers come with a waiver that requires an accident victim to forego their legal rights to a personal injury claim as a condition for accepting the offer�leaving them without recourse once they realize the settlement leaves them without the lion�s share of the recovery they deserve. If a potential plaintiff retains a Riverdale personal injury attorney, though, an insurance company may change its tune and significantly increase its settlement offer out of fear of pending litigation.

If the insurance company still does not offer a reasonable settlement, or if there was no insurance company involved in the first place, the next step is often to file a complaint. This formal court document is served to the negligent party and states what happened, the extent of the plaintiff�s injuries, and why the plaintiff deserves to be compensated.

After the complaint, the vast majority of personal injury cases will end in settlement, typically well before the prospective trial date. However, the lack of a trial does not mean a plaintiff could not benefit from the skills and knowledge of a personal injury lawyer in Riverdale. By gathering evidence of compensable damages and the details of the accident, legal counsel could pressure the other side towards making a reasonable settlement offer and could guide a plaintiff throughout the ensuing legal processes.

In rare cases, the defendant makes no reasonable settlement offer, and a personal injury case will go to trial. There, a plaintiff�s attorney could argue why they deserves to be compensated, and how much they deserve, and the defense would respond with their own side of the story. The jury could then consider the evidence and reach a conclusion in their verdict which states whether the plaintiff should be compensated and how much they are to recover.

If you or a loved one were hurt in an accident or as the result of someone else�s negligence, hiring legal help could make a huge difference in whether you recover the compensation you need and deserve. Contact a Riverdale personal injury lawyer today for the legal representation you may need.

pages.title: Riverdale Bicycle Accident Lawyer | Cyclist Collision
pages.description: If you were hurt in a biking incident, contact a Riverdale bicycle accident lawyer to learn about possible compensation for your pain and suffering.
pages.content_md:
When you take to the road for leisurely cycling, you trust that other drivers adhere to the duty of safety they owe you. However, that does not stop negligent drivers from forsaking that duty and harming bicyclists. If you suffered an injury because of an irresponsible driver, a Riverdale bicycle accident lawyer could help you seek the compensation you need by bringing your case to court and challenging opposing counsels� defenses.

Even if your injuries and losses are extensive, a skilled personal injury attorney could seek the full amount of compensation that could be available to you. They could speak with insurance companies and attorneys for the wrongdoer to possibly settle your case without having to go to court.

There are two key elements in each injury case that a bicycle accident lawyer in Riverdale must be prepared to show and convince the jury of: the wrongdoer’s liability and the victim�s losses. The jury must agree that the defendant is the party responsible for the injuries to the victim and furthermore they must believe that the injury suffered by the victim caused the victim�s damages. If these points cannot be shown, the victim may not receive the compensation they need.

By obtaining a driver�s license and sitting behind the wheel of a car, a driver assumes a duty of care to others on the road. This duty is to drive and make decisions like other reasonably prudent drivers. If drivers breach this duty, they are liable for the injuries and damages that they cause.

Breaching the duty is negligence. When negligence causes damages to another party, a legal claim could be brought against the driver.

Sometimes, a defense attorney argues that it was the victim who was mostly if not completely responsible for an accident. Perhaps the bicyclist was not obeying the rules of the road or was distracted at the time of the accident. The defense could use this to purport that the victim is to blame for their own injuries. A competent Riverdale bicycle accident attorney could help refute these points in order to get victims the compensation they need.

Under Official Code of Georgia Annotated �51-12-33, if a plaintiff is less than 50 percent at fault for their own damages, they may still recover their remaining damages from the defendants. For example, if a jury awards the plaintiff $50,000 for their damages, but they also determine that the plaintiff holds 10 percent liability. The defendant is only liable for paying them the remaining 90 percent of the $50,000. Importantly, if a jury determines that a victim was 50 percent or more at fault for the accident, the victim would be barred completely from recovering any compensation for their claim. Because of this, it is important for victims to have by their side a bicycle accident attorney in Riverdale who could challenge these accusations of fault.

If you are facing multiple medical bills, lost wages, and physical injuries as a result of a bicycling accident, you may feel defeated. An experienced Riverdale bicycle accident lawyer understands these feelings and could help represent your legal interests. This could include asking for and receiving a fair settlement on your behalf.

Do not procrastinate in consulting with an attorney as your legal rights could be lost after a period of time. Call today to schedule your case consultation and learn how you could benefit from the services of an attorney after a bicycle accident.

When a boating accident occurs, there may be multiple liable parties. A court also could find a plaintiff partially responsible for their injuries based on their actions leading up to the accident.

If you were injured in a boating accident, you may be entitled to compensation for your medical bills, lost income, and pain and suffering, as well as various other damages. By consulting with a seasoned Riverdale boat accident lawyer, you could learn more about your legal options and increase your chances of a positive outcome. Call today to get started on your case.

pages.title: Riverdale Bus Accident Lawyer | Public Transportation Collision

pages.content_md:
Bus accidents occur far more often than many people realize. From school buses, to public transportation, and to private transport services, no bus is immune. These accidents might happen for a variety of reasons, but one thing is for sure: the injuries and damages to victims could be severe. Because of this, it is crucial for victims of these accidents to enlist the help of a knowledgeable legal representative.

No matter the type of bus accident you were in, a Riverdale bus accident lawyer could determine who was liable and help hold those parties accountable for your losses.

The first and most important aspect of filing a bus accident case that victims should be aware of is the statute of limitations. This law places a limit on the amount of time that may elapse before the victim�s case is formally filed with the courts. As per the Official Code of Georgia Annotated �9-3-33, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of the bus accident.

Bus accident victims could help ensure that their case is filed before the statute of limitations expires by hiring a knowledgeable bus accident lawyer in Riverdale. The failure to file a bus accident case within the defined time period could likely cause victims to lose their legal rights to seek compensation for their injuries forever.

Once the case is filed, the discovery process begins for both sides. During investigations, various pieces of information are gathered and shared between the legal counsel for the plaintiff and the defendant. This may include information found in:

- Depositions
- Sworn testimony
- Medical records
- Personal journals
- Medical texts
- Insurance policy documents
- Employee records
- Medical bills

At any time after the case is filed, an attempt at settling the case could be made by either party. If a fair negotiation takes places and both sides agree, the defendant would then pay a sum of money to compensate the victim for their damages. In return, the plaintiff agrees to waive their right to sue the defendant for the same accident in the future.

Settlements could benefit both sides as they decrease the amount of time, money, and resources spent on litigation. It also gives both the plaintiff and the defendant more control over how the case is resolved. However, plaintiffs should consult with their Riverdale bus accident attorney prior to making any kind of agreement.

If a settlement cannot be negotiated between the two parties, they then prepare for a trial, and a trial date is set. Each side then brings their case before the judge or jury, and they decide the outcome of the case. An accomplished lawyer will come prepared to fight for the victim’s right to compensation at trial.

Bus accidents are often quite complex. There may be multiple defendants involved such as the bus driver, bus company, bus manufacturer, and even other drivers. Many accident victims could rely on a skilled Riverdale bus accident lawyer to build their case and seek compensation on their behalf. This could allow victims peace of mind that their legal case is in good hands while they focus on their physical and emotional healing after the accident.

Placing your case in the hands of a qualified attorney could mean the difference between recouping your damages and an unfavorable outcome. To learn more about your legal options, call an attorney today.

pages.title: Riverdale Drunk Driving Car Accident Lawyer | Intoxicated Driver

pages.h1: Riverdale Drunk Driving Car Accident Lawyer
pages.content_md:
When someone gets behind the wheel of a motor vehicle drunk, they could cause a devastating accident. The injuries someone experiences after a drunk driver collision can be severe and life-changing.

If an intoxicated driver causes you to get into an accident, a skilled car accident attorney could assist you in filing a lawsuit to recover compensation for your injuries and damages. A Riverdale drunk driving car accident lawyer could help you hold the driver accountable for their reckless and careless behavior.

According to the Official Code of Georgia �40-6-391, prosecutors can pursue a driving under the influence (DUI) charge under two legal theories.

The first theory is known as an �intoxication DUI.� Under this statute, it is unlawful to operate a motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs. This statute is intentionally open-ended and allows for a successful prosecution without a breath test.

A �per se DUI� occurs when someone operates a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of .08 or more. The court may convict a drunk driver if a prosecutor uses either of these statutes to make their argument. An experienced Riverdale drunk driving car accident attorney can use a defendant’s criminal conviction against them with building a civil suit for an injured plaintiff.

The plaintiff�s Riverdale drunk driving car accident lawyer must prove that the defendant was responsible for the collision which caused injuries and damages by providing evidence for the various elements of negligence to be successful in their civil case. These elements include:

- Duty of care
- Breach of the duty of care
- Causation
- Damages

The injured claimant� attorney must establish that the defendant owed them a duty to behave reasonably given the circumstances of their case. If there was no duty of care, a defendant may not be responsible for the damages of the plaintiff. Under state law, every driver owes others on the road a duty to operate their vehicle safely.

In a collision involving a drunken driver, their intoxication proves that they recklessly disregarded the safety of others on the road and therefore breached their duty to drive safely. A well-versed Riverdale attorney with experience in handling a drunk driving accident can use a defendant�s blood alcohol content (BAC) level as evidence of intoxication and help an injured party prove that this driver breached their duty of care.

A plaintiff also must show that their injuries are a result of the intoxicated driver�s breach of duty of care. Additionally, a plaintiff may only recover compensation if they can prove that their injuries resulted in monetary or emotional damages. A seasoned lawyer could help an injured person calculate and recover damages.

The irresponsibility of drunk drivers can cause devastation and suffering for many families. If you sustained injuries from an intoxicated driver, you can seek compensation and hold them responsible for their careless actions with help from a skilled Riverdale drunk driving car accident lawyer. Call right away to schedule your initial case consultation.
