The beginning of the year is when people review budgets, update calendars, and reset routines. It’s also a good time to think about whether you’re prepared if something unexpected happens.

Being prepared doesn’t mean assuming the worst. It means knowing where you stand before you’re forced to figure it out under stress.

**Review Your Insurance Coverage**

Many people haven’t looked closely at their insurance policies in years. Minimum coverage often isn’t enough to cover serious injuries, and uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage can be more important than people realize. These gaps usually don’t become obvious until after an accident.

**Know What to Do After an Accident**

In the moments after a crash or injury, stress makes it hard to think clearly. Knowing when to call the police, when to take photos, and what information to gather can make a significant difference later. It’s also important to be careful about what you say to insurance companies before you fully understand your situation.

**Don’t Assume Minor Accidents Stay Minor**

Many injuries don’t show symptoms right away. Pain, stiffness, and other issues can take days or weeks to appear. Waiting too long to get medical care or ask questions can complicate recovery and any potential claim.

**Understand That Timing Matters**

Georgia law places limits on how long you have to take legal action after an injury. That clock often starts running sooner than people expect, even if treatment is ongoing.

**Start the Year Informed**

You don’t need to expect something bad to happen to be prepared. Having a basic understanding of your coverage, your options, and your next steps can help you feel more confident if the unexpected happens.

If an accident does happen, you don’t have to figure everything out on your own. Many people wait to ask questions because they don’t want to overreact or assume they’re entitled to anything. But understanding your rights early can help you make informed decisions and avoid costly mistakes.

#### Property Owner Responsibility and Liability

Many slip and fall accidents happen in places where property owners are responsible for keeping the premises safe, including grocery stores, retail shops, restaurants, and apartment complexes. pages.title: Why You Should Think Twice Before Accepting a Fast Settlement

pages.h1: Why You Should Think Twice Before Accepting a Fast Settlement
pages.content_md:
December is a busy time for families, and it is also a very active time for insurance companies.  
As the year comes to a close, many people notice insurance adjusters calling more often,  
pushing faster settlement offers, and encouraging them to wrap up their personal injury claims.  
While this may seem helpful, these quick settlements are rarely in the injured person’s best  
interest. In many Georgia personal injury cases, end of year settlements are designed to protect  
the insurance company, not the accident victim.

Insurance companies often try to close out as many claims as possible before the new year. This  
helps them clear accounts and improve their financial reporting. To do that, they commonly  
pressure people who were injured in car accidents, slip and fall accidents, or other personal  
injury cases to settle quickly. These offers usually arrive fast and sound appealing, especially  
when someone is dealing with medical bills, missed work, and holiday expenses. Unfortunately,  
fast settlement money is often far less than what the claim is truly worth.

The biggest danger of accepting a quick accident settlement is that once you sign, your personal  
injury case is usually closed permanently. Even if your injuries worsen, even if you later need  
surgery, and even if you miss more work than expected, you typically cannot go back and ask  
for additional compensation. Many accident victims do not realize the full impact of their  
injuries until weeks or even months later, which makes rushed settlements extremely risky.  
During the holiday season, insurance companies often use subtle pressure tactics. They may call  
repeatedly asking if you are ready to settle, suggest that the offer will expire soon, minimize  
your injuries, or blame gaps in medical treatment on the holidays. While these conversations  
may seem friendly, their goal is simple. They want to close your Georgia personal injury claim  
for as little money as possible.

In most cases, it is too early to settle if you are still in pain, still seeing doctors, unsure how long  
your recovery will take, or uncertain about the total cost of your medical treatment. Settling  
before you understand the long term impact of your injuries can leave you financially  
responsible for future medical bills, lost wages, and ongoing care that the insurance company  
should have covered.

Before accepting any settlement offer, especially in December, it is important to know the full  
cost of your medical care, understand how your injury affects your ability to work, and have the  
offer reviewed by someone who understands Georgia personal injury law. Taking this extra step  
can protect you from making a permanent decision based on short term financial pressure.  
If you were injured this year and an insurance company is suddenly pushing you to settle before  
January, take a moment before signing anything. These decisions affect your health, your  
finances, and your future, not just this holiday season.

If you or a loved one was injured in a car accident, slip and fall, or any other personal injury  
accident in Georgia, do not let an insurance company rush you into a low settlement. A  
personal injury attorney can review your case, explain your rights, and help you fight for the full  
compensation you deserve. Contact our office today to schedule a free consultation and  
protect your future.

pages.h1: Holiday Traffic in Carrollton: Tips to Avoid Accidents During the Busiest Time of Year

The holidays are one of the best times to live in Carrollton. The square is glowing with lights, families are out shopping, and there’s a little extra excitement in the air. But as joyful as the season is, it’s also one of the most dangerous times to be on the road. Between out-of-town visitors, last-minute shoppers, and unpredictable weather, holiday traffic around West Georgia can be hectic—and sometimes hazardous.

Each year, law enforcement sees a rise in car accidents during November and December, especially along busy routes like Highway 27, Bankhead Highway, and the Carrollton Bypass. More cars on the road mean more opportunities for distraction and frustration, and even a small mistake can lead to a serious collision.

So why are holiday crashes so common? Fatigue, stress, and rushing are a big part of it. Many people are juggling packed schedules—school events, shopping trips, and family gatherings—and it’s easy to lose focus behind the wheel. Add in the fact that some drivers may be celebrating with alcohol or unfamiliar with Carrollton’s roads, and you have a recipe for more accidents.

To stay safe, plan ahead. Give yourself plenty of time to reach your destination so you’re not tempted to speed or weave through traffic. Try to avoid peak travel times when the roads are busiest, and remember that even a short trip across town might take longer this time of year. If you’re heading out on I-20 or Highway 166 to visit family, check the forecast and make sure your vehicle is winter-ready—tires, wipers, and all.

And most importantly, stay alert for other drivers who may not be as careful. Distracted and impaired driving increase significantly during the holidays, and being proactive—keeping a safe following distance, using your signals, and avoiding phone use—can help you stay one step ahead.

If you do find yourself in an accident this holiday season, know that help is close by. Our firm has worked with countless Carrollton residents who were injured through no fault of their own. We understand how quickly an accident can disrupt your life, especially during a time meant for family and celebration. Our team is here to handle the legal side so you can focus on healing and getting back to what matters most.

The holidays should be about joy, not stress. By driving carefully and staying aware, we can all do our part to keep Carrollton’s roads safe this season. And if someone else’s carelessness causes a crash, you can count on your local attorneys to stand by your side every step of the way.

pages.h1: Tailgating Season in Georgia: Staying Safe on the Roads Before and After the Game
pages.content_md:
Fall in Georgia means one thing: football. Whether you’re cheering on your local high school, a Saturday  
SEC matchup, or the Falcons on Sunday, game day traffic can be a nightmare. Unfortunately, it also leads to an increase in car accidents.

#### Game Day Car Accident Risks

**Heavy Traffic:** Thousands of fans traveling to stadiums and tailgates means congested highways  
and a higher chance of fender benders.

**Distracted Driving:** Excited fans checking directions, texting friends, or blasting music often  
aren’t fully focused on the road.

**Alcohol-Related Crashes:** Tailgating often involves drinking, and sadly, some drivers still get  
behind the wheel after too many beers.

#### Tips to Stay Safe During Football Season

  * Plan your route ahead of time and allow for extra traffic delays.
  * Always use a designated driver or rideshare if alcohol is involved.
  * Stay alert in parking lots, where accidents are common after big games.

overwrite footage. Early action helps preserve key facts and enables investigation. Collect as  
much evidence as possible: Photos of damage, street signs, skid marks, nearby surveillance  
cameras, and eyewitness contact info.

**How Georgia’s Insurance Laws Apply**  
Georgia law requires drivers to carry uninsured motorist (UM) coverage. If the at-fault driver can’t be  
found, your own insurer should provide compensation up to your UM limit. Parian Lawyers can evaluate  
your policy to ensure you’re using all available benefits.

Coverage may include:

  * Medical bills

debris).
  * Working with local police who may open hit-and-run reports even when the driver is  
unidentified.

**Building a Strong Claim**  
Pursuing a hit-and-run case can sometimes be discouraging with an offender being unidentified. It is  
important to be diligent in keeping track of things to build a strong case.

urgency, and tenacity. A hit and run can feel overwhelming—but you don’t have to go it alone. Parian

pages.description: Many people involved in car accidents in Georgia walk away wondering if they still have a case if they were partially to blame. Whether it was a missed turn sig
pages.h1: Can I Still Recover Damages If I Was Partially at Fault in a Georgia Car Accident?
pages.content_md:
Many people involved in car accidents in Georgia walk away wondering if they still have a case  
if they were partially to blame. Whether it was a missed turn signal, speeding slightly, or being  
distracted by a phone, it's common for drivers to share some degree of responsibility. The good  
news is that Georgia law allows injured victims to recover damages even if they were partly at  
fault for the crash.

Under Georgia's modified comparative negligence rule, you can still receive compensation as  
long as you are less than 50% responsible for the accident. This means that even if you made a  
mistake behind the wheel, you may still be entitled to recover money for medical expenses, lost  
income, vehicle repairs, and pain and suffering.

However, your compensation will be reduced by your percentage of fault. For example, if you  
are found to be 20% responsible for the accident and your damages total $100,000, you would  
still be eligible to receive $80,000. This legal structure makes it crucial to have a knowledgeable  
car accident attorney on your side to argue your case and ensure the insurance companies  
don't unfairly shift more blame onto you than is appropriate.

At Parian Lawyers, we have extensive experience handling car accident cases throughout West  
Georgia, including Carrollton, Douglasville, and along the I-20 corridor. We know how to  
analyze accident reports, gather witness statements, and work with experts to build a strong  
case that accurately reflects what happened. If you believe you may be partially at fault in a  
recent accident, don’t assume you’re out of options.

Let our team review the details and guide you on the best path forward. Even if fault is shared,  
your right to fair compensation remains. Contact Parian Lawyers today for a free consultation  
with a car accident lawyer who understands Georgia's complex laws and will fight to protect  
your rights.

pages.h1: Bremen’s Road Work Is Picking Up—Here’s How to Drive Safely While Streets Are Being Paved
pages.content_md:
If you live in Bremen, you’ve probably seen the signs—or the road crews themselves. The city recently  
opened bids for a large street paving project to upgrade several local roads. It’s a much-needed  
improvement, but if you’re behind the wheel while it’s going on, you’ll need to take some extra  
precautions.

Fresh pavement, loose gravel, and large construction vehicles can turn an everyday drive into a  
dangerous one if you’re not paying close attention. We’ve seen plenty of accidents happen in exactly  
these kinds of conditions.

### How to Stay Safe While Bremen Streets Get Repaved

  1. Watch for detours and signs.  
It’s tempting to just follow your usual route, but if a road is closed or being worked on, don’t force it. Respect the detours and stay out of closed zones—even if it looks passable.
  2. Take it slow on fresh asphalt.  
New pavement can be slick, especially when it’s still settling or hasn’t been fully marked. Go slower than usual and be careful with turns and sudden stops.
  3. Be extra careful around construction trucks.  
They’re big, loud, and not as nimble as your car. Give them space to move, especially when backing up or turning. Don’t try to pass a paving crew unless you’re absolutely sure it’s safe and legal to do so.
  4. Expect the unexpected.  
In paving zones, lanes might shift, markings might be missing, and loose gravel could pop up out of  
nowhere. Assume the road might not behave the way it usually does.
  5. Don’t assume it’s your fault if there’s an accident.  
If you’re involved in a crash in or near a paving zone, don’t rush to take the blame. There could be other factors at play—like missing signs, dangerous drop-offs, or mismanaged traffic patterns.



### We’ve Helped Others—We Can Help You

Construction-related accidents can be tricky. Was the city responsible? The paving company? Another  
driver? These are the kinds of questions we know how to answer. If you or someone you love was hurt  
in a paving zone crash, talk to Parian Lawyers. We’re based right here in West Georgia and we  
understand how to deal with these local situations.

pages.title: Why You Shouldn’t Settle Too Quickly After a Car Accident in Carrollton, GA
pages.description: If you’ve been in a car accident in Carrollton, Georgia, you might be tempted to accept the first offer the insurance company sends your way. After all, you’re
pages.h1: Why You Shouldn’t Settle Too Quickly After a Car Accident in Carrollton, GA
pages.content_md:
If you've been in a car accident in Carrollton, Georgia, you might be tempted to accept the first offer the insurance company sends your way. After all, you're dealing with medical bills, car repairs, missed work, and a lot of stress. But settling too quickly can cost you far more than you realize — both financially and physically.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve helped many accident victims in Carroll County and surrounding areas recover the full compensation they deserve. Before you sign anything, here’s what you need to know.

## Your Injuries May Be More Serious Than You Think

Many car accident injuries — especially soft tissue injuries like whiplash or back strain — don’t show up right away. Adrenaline can mask pain for hours or even days. In some cases, symptoms may worsen over time, requiring surgery, physical therapy, or long-term care.

If you settle early, you waive the right to seek additional compensation, even if new injuries appear later. That’s why it’s crucial to wait until you understand the full scope of your injuries and medical needs.

## Insurance Companies Want to Close Cases Cheaply

It’s no secret: insurance companies want to protect their bottom line. Their goal is to settle your claim as quickly and cheaply as possible — not to make sure you’re fairly compensated.

An adjuster may pressure you into accepting a lowball offer, often before you’ve had time to consult with a personal injury lawyer. If you accept, you may be stuck with unpaid medical bills, ongoing pain, or lost income — all without any legal recourse.

## You Could Be Entitled to More Than You Think

In Georgia, car accident victims may be eligible for damages beyond just medical bills and car repairs. Depending on your case, you may be able to recover compensation for:

  * Lost wages
  * Future medical expenses
  * Pain and suffering
  * Emotional distress
  * Loss of enjoyment of life



Don’t leave money on the table. An experienced Carrollton car accident attorney can help you calculate the full value of your claim — and fight to get it.

## Evidence Takes Time to Gather

Strong cases are built on solid evidence — police reports, medical records, witness statements, and sometimes expert opinions. When you settle too soon, you miss the opportunity to build a case that reflects the full impact of the accident on your life.

By consulting an attorney early, you can make sure evidence is preserved and deadlines are met — including Georgia’s two-year statute of limitations for personal injury claims.

## Consult a Local Attorney Before You Sign Anything

A quick settlement might sound convenient now, but it could leave you struggling financially later. If you've been in a car accident in Carrollton or anywhere in West Georgia, reach out to a local law firm that knows the courts, the community, and how to win.

At Parian Lawyers, our experienced personal injury lawyers help injury victims throughout Carroll County and beyond. We offer free consultations, and you don’t pay unless we win your case.

pages.content_md:
Getting a driver’s license is a major milestone for teenagers—but for parents, it can be a source  
of anxiety. In Carroll County, Georgia, teen drivers are statistically more likely to be involved in  
car accidents than any other age group. Understanding the risks and responsibilities can help  
protect your teen—and your family—from the serious consequences of a crash.  
At Parian Lawyers, we’ve represented families across West Georgia after devastating accidents  
involving young drivers. Here’s what every parent should know.

### Teen Drivers Are at Higher Risk for Accidents

According to the CDC, motor vehicle crashes are the second leading cause of death for teens in  
the U.S. Risk factors include:

  * Inexperience behind the wheel
  * Distracted driving, especially texting or using social media
  * Speeding or reckless driving
  * Driving with teen passengers (which significantly increases risk)
  * Nighttime or weekend driving



In Carrollton and surrounding communities, we see a significant number of teen-related  
accidents on roads like Highway 27, I-20, and rural two-lane roads, where speed and visibility  
can be dangerous combinations.

### **Georgia’s Teen Driving Laws: What You Should Know**

Georgia’s Teen & Adult Driver Responsibility Act (TADRA) lays out a graduated driver’s license  
system to help teens gain experience safely:

  1. Learner’s Permit (15 years old) – Must drive with a licensed adult (21+).
  2. Intermediate License (16–17 years old) – No driving between 12 AM–5 AM; limits on  
passengers during the first year.
  3. Full License (18+) – No restrictions if all requirements are met.



Violating these rules or receiving certain traffic citations can delay a teen’s ability to move to  
the next stage—or lead to a suspension.

### **What Happens If Your Teen Causes an Accident?**

In Georgia, parents can be held financially liable for accidents caused by their minor children.  
Even if your teen is at fault, the injured party can pursue a claim against your insurance  
policy—and potentially your personal assets if coverage is insufficient.  
That’s why it’s critical to:

  * Review your auto insurance policy limits
  * Consider adding uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage
  * Make sure your teen understands the responsibility that comes with driving



#### **What If Your Teen Is Injured in a Crash?**

If your child is injured in a car accident—whether they were driving or a passenger—they may  
be entitled to compensation for:

  * Medical bills
  * Pain and suffering
  * Emotional trauma
  * Future treatment or rehabilitation



A Carrollton personal injury attorney can help your family understand your options and fight  
for what your child deserves.

#### **Tips for Parents of New Driver** s

  * Set clear rules about phone use, curfews, and speeding
  * Ride along frequently during the first few months
  * Use driving contracts to set expectations
  * Keep communication open—if they feel safe calling you for help, they’re less likely to  
take dangerous risks



### **Need Legal Help After a Teen Driving Accident?**

Whether your teen was injured or caused an accident, Parian Lawyers is here to help. We  
understand the emotional and legal complexities of these cases, and we’re committed to  
protecting your family’s future.

pages.title: The Insurance Company Isn’t On Your Side After a Car Accident—Here’s Why
pages.description: After a car accident, you expect your insurance company—or the other driver’s—to do the right thing. But here’s a hard truth: insurance companies are in the bus
pages.h1: The Insurance Company Isn’t On Your Side After a Car Accident—Here’s Why
pages.content_md:
After a car accident, you expect your insurance company—or the other driver’s—to do the right thing. But here’s a hard truth: insurance companies are in the business of paying out as little as possible.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve seen every trick in the book—and we know how quickly people get taken advantage of after a crash.

**Common Tactics Insurance Companies Use:**

  1. Fast Cash Offers – If they offer you money right away, it’s probably because they know your claim is worth _much more_.
  2. Recorded Statement Traps – They may ask you to “just describe what happened” while recording the call. These statements can later be used to reduce or deny your claim.
  3. Blame Shifting – Especially in multi-car or truck accidents, insurers may try to pin partial fault on you to reduce your payout under Georgia’s comparative fault rules.
  4. Medical Minimization – They'll question whether your injuries were serious or related to the crash, even if you’re still receiving treatment.



**This Happens a Lot on West Georgia Roads:**

From I-20 and Highway 27 to GA-61, we’ve helped clients who were hit on the way to work, church, or school—only to find out the insurance company was already working against them before they’d even left the hospital.

In truck accident cases, it’s even more aggressive. The trucking company might send out a “rapid response team” within hours of the crash to protect their driver—not you.

**What You Should Do Instead:**

  * Don’t give a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney
  * See a doctor right away and follow up on treatment
  * Document everything—medical bills, time missed from work, pain and symptoms
  * Call a car accident attorney in West Georgia who knows how to deal with insurance company tactics



Insurance companies may act friendly, but their priority isn’t your recovery—it’s their bottom line. We’re here to flip the balance of power back in your favor. If you’ve been injured in a car accident, call Parian Lawyers today.

pages.title: Dangers on I-20, I-285, and U.S. 27
pages.description: Truck and car accidents are a major concern in Georgia, especially on high-traffic highways like Interstate 20 (I-20), Interstate 285 (I-285), and U.S. Highway
pages.h1: Dangers on I-20, I-285, and U.S. 27
pages.content_md:
Truck and car accidents are a major concern in Georgia, especially on high-traffic highways like Interstate 20 (I-20), Interstate 285 (I-285), and U.S. Highway 27. These roads run through Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta, making them some of the most dangerous routes for collisions involving passenger vehicles and large commercial trucks.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve seen firsthand how devastating these accidents can be. If you or a loved one has been injured in a truck or car crash, understanding the risks and legal options is crucial.

**Why Are Truck Accidents So Dangerous in Georgia?**

Truck accidents are far more severe than regular car crashes because of the size and weight of 18-wheelers. A fully loaded semi-truck can weigh 80,000 pounds, compared to a typical passenger vehicle that weighs around 4,000 pounds. This size difference leads to:

  * Severe injuries like broken bones, spinal cord damage, and traumatic brain injuries.
  * Longer stopping distances, making it harder for trucks to avoid sudden traffic slowdowns.
  * Increased risk of jackknife accidents when truck drivers brake suddenly.
  * Deadly underride collisions, where smaller cars get trapped underneath trucks.



**Most Dangerous Highways for Truck and Car Accidents in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta**

_Interstate 20 (I-20) – High-Speed Trucking Dangers_

I-20 is one of the busiest trucking routes in Georgia, connecting Bremen, Carrollton, and Atlanta to Alabama and beyond. High speeds, heavy commercial truck traffic, and frequent congestion make it a hotspot for serious crashes.

Common I-20 Accident Causes:

  * Truckers speeding to meet tight delivery deadlines.
  * Drowsy driving—long-haul truckers often push past legal driving limits.
  * Aggressive lane changes by passenger vehicles trying to overtake slow-moving trucks.



_Interstate 285 (I-285) – The “Perimeter” Trucking Nightmare_

Known as Atlanta’s Perimeter, I-285 is a top-ranked deadly highway in the U.S. It encircles Atlanta and is heavily used by commercial trucks avoiding downtown traffic.

Why I-285 is Dangerous:

  * High volume of 18-wheelers, leading to frequent truck-car collisions.
  * Merging and exit confusion, especially at major interchanges.
  * Rear-end crashes from stop-and-go traffic.



_U.S. Highway 27 – Rural Road Risks in Carrollton and Bremen_

U.S. 27 runs through Carrollton and Bremen, serving as a major trucking corridor for local and regional deliveries. While not as busy as the interstates, it has high truck traffic combined with rural road hazards.

**Common U.S. 27 Accident Causes:**

  * Limited passing lanes, leading to risky overtaking.
  * Sudden stops at traffic lights, causing rear-end collisions.
  * Blind curves and rolling hills, making it difficult to see oncoming vehicles.



**Who is Liable in a Truck vs. Car Accident in Georgia?**

Determining liability in a truck accident is complex. Multiple parties may be responsible, including:

  * The truck driver (for speeding, distracted driving, or fatigue).
  * The trucking company (for overloading cargo or forcing drivers to work long hours).
  * The truck manufacturer (for defective brakes or mechanical failures).
  * Another driver (if they caused a chain-reaction crash).



Important: Georgia follows comparative fault laws, meaning if you’re partially at fault, your compensation may be reduced. That’s why having an experienced truck accident lawyer in Carrollton, Bremen, or Atlanta is crucial.

**What to Do After a Truck or Car Accident in Georgia**

If you’re in an accident with a truck, follow these steps to protect your rights:

Call 911 – Always report the accident and request medical attention.  
Take Photos – Capture vehicle damage, skid marks, and road conditions.  
Get Witness Statements – If anyone saw the crash, get their contact info.  
Do NOT Admit Fault – Even saying “I’m sorry” can be used against you.

Call a Personal Injury Lawyer – Trucking companies have aggressive legal teams. You need an experienced truck accident attorney fighting for you.

**Why Choose Parian Lawyers for Your Truck Accident Case?**

At Parian Lawyers, we specialize in truck and car accident cases in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta. Our team understands the complexities of Georgia trucking laws, and we fight to get our clients the maximum compensation for medical bills, lost wages, and pain & suffering.

**Have You Been Injured in a Truck or Car Accident? Call Us Today!**

If you or a loved one has been in a serious truck accident, don’t wait. Contact Parian Lawyers for a free consultation.

pages.title: Brake Failure Accidents in Georgia: Who is Liable When Brakes Fail?
pages.description: Brake failure is one of the most dangerous mechanical failures that can happen on Georgia roads, especially on highways like I-20, I-285, and U.S. 27. When a ca
pages.h1: Brake Failure Accidents in Georgia: Who is Liable When Brakes Fail?
pages.content_md:
Brake failure is one of the most dangerous mechanical failures that can happen on Georgia roads, especially on highways like I-20, I-285, and U.S. 27. When a car or 18-wheeler truck loses braking ability, the results can be catastrophic, leading to multi-vehicle pileups, rollovers, or fatal crashes.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve represented victims of brake failure accidents in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta. If you’ve been injured in a crash caused by faulty brakes, you may have a case against the driver, trucking company, or even the brake manufacturer.

**How Do Brake Failure Accidents Happen?**

Many drivers assume brake failures are rare, but they’re more common than you think—especially in commercial trucks that put heavy strain on their braking systems. Here’s why brakes fail:

  * Lack of Maintenance – Trucking companies often cut corners on brake inspections to save money.
  * Worn-Out Brake Pads – Ignoring signs of worn pads leads to reduced stopping power.
  * Overheated Brakes (Brake Fade) – Happens when a driver rides the brakes on long downhill stretches.
  * Defective Braking Systems – Faulty manufacturing can lead to sudden failures.
  * Hydraulic Brake Failure – Issues with the master cylinder or brake fluid leaks can cause a total loss of braking.



**High-Risk Areas for Brake Failure Accidents in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta**

Brake failure is especially dangerous in high-traffic and high-speed areas. Here are the most high-risk locations for these accidents:

  1. **I-20 Near Bremen – Steep Downhill Grades**



I-20 near Bremen is notorious for steep downhill sections where truckers ride their brakes, leading to overheating and failure.

**Risk Factor:** Runaway trucks that can’t stop in time for red lights or traffic slowdowns.

  2. **Carrollton Bypass – Stop-and-Go Traffic Risks**



The Carrollton Bypass (U.S. 27) has multiple stoplights and intersections, making it a dangerous area for brake failures.

**Risk Factor:** Trucks failing to stop at red lights, causing T-bone crashes.

  3. **I-285 Near Atlanta – Sudden Traffic Jams**



Atlanta’s I-285 is one of the busiest highways in the country, and sudden traffic slowdowns are common. If a truck’s brakes fail here, multi-car pileups can occur.

**Risk Factor:** High-speed truck crashes due to brake failures in bumper-to-bumper traffic.

**Who is Liable in a Brake Failure Accident?**

Determining who is responsible for a brake failure accident depends on what caused the failure. Potentially liable parties include:

  * The Truck Driver – If they ignored warning signs like grinding noises or burning smells.
  * The Trucking Company – If they failed to perform regular brake inspections.
  * The Brake Manufacturer – If the brakes were defective from the factory.
  * The Mechanic or Repair Shop – If improper maintenance caused the failure.



**What to Do If You’re in a Brake Failure Accident**

If a car or semi-truck crashes into you due to brake failure, take these steps immediately:

  * Call 911 – Report the accident and request medical assistance.
  * Document Everything – Take photos of the vehicle damage and skid marks (or lack of them).
  * Get Witness Statements – Eyewitnesses can help prove the brakes failed.
  * Do NOT Accept Blame – The trucking company may try to shift the blame onto you.
  * Contact an Attorney – A Georgia truck accident lawyer can investigate the cause of the brake failure.



**How Parian Lawyers Can Help**

At Parian Lawyers, we specialize in brake failure accident claims in Carrollton, Bremen, and Atlanta. We’ll investigate:

  * Maintenance records to see if the truck’s brakes were inspected properly.
  * Black box data to check if the truck driver attempted to brake.
  * Manufacturer defects that could make the brake company liable.



If you or a loved one has been injured in a brake failure accident, don’t wait. Call Parian Lawyers today for a free consultation.

pages.title: The Most Common Driving Mistakes Made on I-20
pages.description: Interstate 20 (I-20) is one of the busiest highways running through West Georgia, connecting cities like Bremen and Carrollton to Atlanta and beyond. With heavy
pages.h1: The Most Common Driving Mistakes Made on I-20
pages.content_md:
Interstate 20 (I-20) is one of the busiest highways running through West Georgia, connecting cities like Bremen and Carrollton to Atlanta and beyond. With heavy traffic, high speeds, and frequent congestion, I-20 is also a hotspot for accidents. Many crashes are caused by common driving mistakes that could have been avoided with more caution and awareness.

At Parian Lawyers, we’ve handled many personal injury cases involving car accidents on I-20. Here are the most frequent driving mistakes we see on this stretch of highway—and how you can avoid them.

  1. **Speeding and Aggressive Driving**



Speed limits on I-20 vary, but many drivers push past them, especially in open areas with less traffic enforcement. Speeding reduces reaction time and increases the severity of crashes. Aggressive driving behaviors—like tailgating, weaving between lanes, and road rage—only make things worse.

**Tip:** Stick to the speed limit and maintain a safe following distance. If someone is driving aggressively, don’t engage—just move over and let them pass.

  2. **Distracted Driving**



Texting, eating, adjusting GPS settings, and even talking to passengers can take a driver’s focus off the road. At 70 mph, even a few seconds of inattention can be disastrous.

**Tip:** Keep your phone on "Do Not Disturb" mode while driving and pull over safely if you need to check directions or respond to a message.

  3. **Failing to Adjust for Weather Conditions**



West Georgia experiences unpredictable weather, from sudden downpours to dense fog. Many accidents on I-20 happen when drivers fail to adjust their speed and following distance during bad weather.

**Tip:** In rainy or foggy conditions, slow down, increase your following distance, and use your headlights appropriately. Never use cruise control on wet roads.

  4. **Improper Lane Changes and Merging**



I-20 has a mix of long stretches and high-traffic interchanges, like the busy exits near Carrollton and Bremen. Failing to signal, not checking blind spots, or cutting off other drivers can easily lead to accidents.

**Tip:** Always signal well in advance, check your mirrors and blind spots, and make sure there’s enough space before changing lanes or merging.

  5. **Drowsy or Impaired Driving**



Many drivers underestimate the dangers of fatigue, but drowsy driving can be just as dangerous as drunk driving. Long-haul truckers and late-night travelers are especially at risk. Similarly, driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs remains a serious issue on I-20.

**Tip:** If you’re feeling tired, pull over at a rest stop or switch drivers. Never get behind the wheel if you’ve been drinking or using substances that impair your judgment.

**What to Do If You’re in an Accident on I-20**

Even if you drive safely, you can’t control the actions of other drivers. If you’re involved in an accident on I-20:

  * Check for injuries and call 911 immediately.
  * Move to a safe location if possible.
  * Exchange information with the other driver(s).
  * Take photos of the scene, damage, and any road conditions that may have contributed to the crash.
  * Contact a personal injury attorney before speaking with insurance companies.



At Parian Lawyers, we help accident victims navigate the legal process and fight for the compensation they deserve. If you or a loved one has been injured in a crash on I-20, contact us for a free consultation.

pages.h1: Dangerous Intersections for Car Accidents in Bremen and Carrollton
pages.content_md:
If you drive regularly in Bremen or Carrollton, you know some intersections are far riskier than others. These danger zones have seen their fair share of crashes, Whether due to high traffic volume, poor visibility, or reckless driving.

If you drive through these intersections, stay alert, knowing the risks could prevent a serious accident.

  1. **U.S. Highway 27 & Bankhead Highway (Carrollton)**



This busy intersection connects two major roads and sees heavy traffic all day long. With multiple lanes, vehicles turning, and drivers rushing to beat traffic lights, it's no surprise that accidents happen here frequently.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

  * High-speed traffic from U.S. 27 meets local traffic from Bankhead Highway.
  * Drivers often misjudge the speed of oncoming cars while making left turns.
  * Sudden lane changes and merging cause rear-end collisions.



🚦 **Safety Tip:** When making turns, wait until you have a fully clear path. If the light turns yellow, don’t rush—speeding through could lead to a T-bone accident.

  2. **Alabama Avenue & U.S. Highway 78 (Bremen)**



This intersection often sees fender benders and side-impact crashes, especially during rush hour. Many drivers fail to yield properly when entering U.S. 78, leading to dangerous collisions.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

  * High traffic volume, especially during school and work commutes.
  * Limited visibility when making turns.
  * Confusion over right-of-way rules.



🚦 **Safety Tip:** Always assume the other driver might not stop. If you're entering from Alabama Avenue, double-check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.

  3. **Maple Street & South Street (Carrollton, Near UWG)**



Located near the University of West Georgia, this intersection is a hotspot for student traffic. Pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles all share the road, increasing the risk of accidents.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

  * Heavy pedestrian crossings.
  * Distracted driving (students often use their phones while driving).
  * Sudden braking due to unexpected foot traffic.



🚦 **Safety Tip:** If you're driving here, stay extra alert for pedestrians, especially at night. For walkers and cyclists—make eye contact with drivers before crossing to ensure they see you.

  4. **Buchanan Street & Pacific Avenue (Bremen)**



Though smaller in scale, this intersection has seen an increase in accidents due to speeding and rolling stops.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

  * Many drivers fail to come to a full stop at stop signs.
  * Speeding through residential areas creates risks for nearby pedestrians and cyclists.
  * Limited lighting at night makes it hard to see approaching vehicles.



🚦 **Safety Tip:** If you're approaching a stop sign, make sure to come to a **complete stop** and check all directions before proceeding.

  5. **Carrollton Bypass & Newnan Road (Carrollton)**



This intersection connects a major bypass with a local road, leading to frequent crashes caused by sudden lane changes and speeding.

**Why it’s dangerous:**

  * Many drivers fail to merge properly.
  * Speeding from the bypass increases crash severity.
  * Red-light runners cause T-bone accidents.



🚦 **Safety Tip:** If you're merging onto the bypass, pick your lane early and stick with it—last-minute lane changes are a leading cause of crashes here.

**What to Do If You’re in an Accident at One of These Intersections**

Even if you’re a cautious driver, accidents still happen. If you find yourself in a crash at one of these locations:

  1. **Check for injuries** and call 911 if needed.
  2. **Move to safety** if the vehicle is drivable.
  3. **Take photos** of the accident scene, including street signs and vehicle damage.
  4. **Exchange information** with the other driver and any witnesses.
  5. **Contact a local personal injury lawyer** before speaking with insurance companies.



At **Parian Lawyers** , we know how dangerous these intersections can be. If you’ve been injured in a crash at one of these locations, we can help you fight for the compensation you deserve. **Call us today for a free consultation.**

pages.h1: Do You Need a Lawyer After a Minor Car Accident in Georgia?
pages.content_md:
After a minor car accident in Georgia, many drivers are unsure whether they need legal representation.  
While some accidents may seem straightforward, the decision to hire a lawyer often depends on the  
circumstances and potential consequences of the crash. Understanding your rights and the legal process  
can help you make the best choice for your situation.

**The Hidden Complexities of Minor Car Accidents**  
What might seem like a simple “fender bender” can sometimes turn into a more complicated issue. For  
example, injuries may not become apparent until days or even weeks after the accident. Soft tissue  
injuries, whiplash, or even mild concussions often develop over time and can lead to medical bills and  
lost wages that weren’t immediately obvious.

Additionally, minor accidents can still result in disputes with insurance companies. Insurers may  
downplay the severity of the damage, offer lowball settlements, or deny claims altogether. Without  
legal guidance, it can be challenging to advocate for the full compensation you deserve.

**When Should You Consult a Lawyer?**  
While not every minor accident requires legal intervention, there are specific situations where  
consulting a personal injury attorney is strongly recommended. If you or anyone else involved in the  
accident has sustained injuries, even seemingly minor ones, an attorney can help you assess the  
potential value of your claim and protect your rights. In Georgia, the comparative fault rule means your  
compensation may be reduced if you are found partially responsible for the accident. A lawyer can help  
gather evidence to minimize your liability. If the insurer is uncooperative or offers a settlement that  
doesn’t cover your expenses, an attorney can negotiate on your behalf. Sometimes, minor accidents  
lead to lingering medical issues or property damage disputes. An attorney can help you prepare for and  
address these unexpected complications.

**The Benefits of Legal Representation**  
Hiring a lawyer after a minor car accident can provide peace of mind and practical advantages. Attorneys  
bring expertise in navigating Georgia’s personal injury laws, handling paperwork, and negotiating with  
insurance companies. They also have access to resources like accident reconstruction specialists and  
medical experts who can strengthen your case.

**How Georgia’s Laws Impact Your Case**  
Georgia operates under a fault-based system, meaning the driver found responsible for the accident is  
liable for damages. However, determining fault isn’t always straightforward, especially in minor  
accidents where evidence like traffic camera footage or eyewitness accounts may be limited.  
Additionally, Georgia’s statute of limitations gives accident victims two years from the date of the crash  
to file a personal injury lawsuit, emphasizing the importance of acting promptly.

**Making the Decision**  
Deciding whether to hire a lawyer after a minor car accident depends on your specific circumstances. If  
there are no injuries, damages are minimal, and the insurance process is proceeding smoothly, you may  
not need legal assistance. However, when in doubt, it’s always wise to consult an attorney for a free evaluation of your case. This initial consultation can provide clarity and ensure you’re not leaving money  
on the table.

**Protect Your Rights**  
Even a minor car accident can have significant consequences for your health, finances, and legal  
standing. By understanding your options and seeking professional advice, you can make informed  
decisions that protect your rights and future.

If you’ve been involved in a minor car accident in Georgia and have questions about your case, Parian  
Lawyers is here to help. Contact us today for a free consultation.

pages.title: Road to Safety: What the Latest Georgia Highway Report Reveals About Our Distracted Driving Habits
pages.description: In October 2024, the Georgia Governor’s Office of Highway Safety reported that distracted driving accounted for over 53% of all vehicle traffic accidents in 202
pages.h1: Road to Safety: What the Latest Georgia Highway Report Reveals About Our Distracted Driving Habits
pages.content_md:
In October 2024, the Georgia Governor’s Office of Highway Safety reported that distracted driving  
accounted for over 53% of all vehicle traffic accidents in 2022. In the Atlanta area, the highest rates of  
distraction-related crashes occurred on principal arterial roads, such as I-75 and I-85. In more rural parts of Georgia, like Haralson and Carroll counties, most distraction-related crashes happened on collector roads, which are designed to move traffic from local streets to arterial roads.

Discussions about distracted driving often focus on cellphone use, but this is not the only form of  
distraction. There are three types of distracted driving:

  1. Manual distractions involve physically interacting with something in the vehicle, such as eating,  
drinking, smoking, or adjusting the radio.
  2. Visual distractions involve looking at something other than the road, such as checking your phone,  
reading, or looking at a billboard.
  3. Cognitive distractions involve mental engagement with thoughts that distract you from driving, such as conversations, arguments, or loud noises inside or outside the vehicle.



It’s crucial to prioritize safety while driving and to recognize that these distractions are not worth  
jeopardizing your well-being or that of others. Here are some steps you can take to prevent distracted  
driving:

Prepare Before You Drive

  * Adjust your settings: Set your GPS, climate controls, and mirrors before hitting the road.
  * Organize your belongings: Keep necessary items like water or toll money within easy reach.
  * Turn on "Do Not Disturb": Use your phone’s do-not-disturb mode or apps that block notifications while driving.



Minimize Phone Usage

  * Hands-free devices: Use Bluetooth or hands-free features if you must take a call.
  * No texting or scrolling: Never text, check social media, or browse apps while driving.
  * Plan stops for communication: If you need to send a message or call, pull over safely.



Limit Passenger Distractions

  * Set expectations: Ask passengers to respect your focus on driving.
  * Engage help when needed: Have passengers handle tasks like GPS adjustments or changing  
music.



Focus on the Road

  * Stay alert: Continuously scan the road and be aware of your surroundings.
  * Avoid multitasking: Eating, grooming, or managing tasks like paperwork should wait until you’re parked.



If you or a loved one has been injured due to the negligence of a distracted driver, Parian Lawyers is  
here to help. Don’t suffer in silence. Our experienced attorneys will evaluate your case, free of cost. Call  
us at (770) 562-7562.

pages.h1: Understanding Georgia’s Fault System: What You Need to Know After a Car Accident in Georgia
pages.content_md:
Car accidents frequently happen on Georgia's roads, often leaving victims unsure about their rights and  
what to do next. Whether you find yourself in Atlanta's busy traffic, traveling through Bremen, or  
navigating the streets of Carrollton, understanding Georgia's fault system is essential after a collision. At  
Parian Lawyers, we focus on assisting car accident victims as they navigate the complexities of personal  
injury claims, helping them secure the compensation they deserve.

**Georgia’s At-Fault Insurance System**  
Georgia follows an “at-fault” insurance system. This means the driver responsible for causing the  
accident is also responsible for covering the damages. Victims can seek compensation by:

  * Filing a claim with their own insurance company.
  * Filing a claim with the at-fault driver’s insurance company.
  * Filing a personal injury lawsuit against the at-fault driver.
  * Determining fault and proving it is essential for recovering compensation for medical bills, lost wages, property damage, and other expenses.



**How Comparative Negligence Affects Your Claim**  
Georgia follows the comparative negligence rule. This means that if you are partially at fault for an  
accident, your compensation may be reduced by the percentage of your fault. For example, if you are  
deemed 20% responsible for the accident, your compensation will be decreased by 20%. However, if you  
are found to be 50% or more at fault, you will not be eligible to receive any damages.  
This underscores the importance of having strong legal representation to ensure that fault is accurately  
assessed and that you receive the maximum compensation possible.

**Why Local Expertise Matters**  
Navigating Georgia’s fault and comparative negligence laws can be overwhelming, especially when  
dealing with the stress of injuries and property damage. Working with a local attorney ensures you  
receive personalized and expert guidance.

**Steps to Take After a Car Accident in Georgia**  
If you’ve been involved in a car accident in Georgia, taking the following steps can protect your claim:

  1. Ensure Safety First: Move to a safe location and call 911 to report the accident.
  2. Gather Evidence: Take photos of the accident scene, your injuries, and vehicle damage. Collect  
contact information from witnesses and other drivers.
  3. Seek Medical Attention: Even if injuries seem minor, get evaluated by a medical professional.
  4. Contact an Experienced Car Accident Lawyer: Reach out to Parian Lawyers for a free consultation to understand your legal options.

victims across Georgia. We take care of the legal complexities of your case so that you can concentrate  
on your recovery. Our team will work diligently to investigate your claim, gather evidence, negotiate  
with insurance companies, and represent you in court if needed.

**Contact Parian Lawyers Today**

contact Parian Lawyers for a free consultation. Call us today at (770) 562-7562. Let us help you secure  
the compensation you deserve and move forward with confidence.

pages.h1: Understanding Dog Bite Injuries in Georgia: How a Personal Injury Attorney Can Help
pages.content_md:
Dog bites can be traumatic, both physically and emotionally. While many dogs are loving and friendly, an unprovoked attack can leave victims with severe injuries, medical expenses, and long-term psychological effects. In Georgia, dog bite laws can be complex, so working with an experienced personal injury attorney is crucial to ensuring you receive fair compensation for your injuries.

**The Seriousness of Dog Bite Injuries**

Dog bites can result in more than just a few scratches. Dog attacks often cause:

  * Deep puncture wounds that can damage muscles, tendons, and nerves.
  * Infections, such as rabies or tetanus, from the bacteria in a dog’s mouth.
  * Permanent scarring or disfigurement.
  * Emotional trauma, especially for children, who are often the most vulnerable to dog bites.



In severe cases, victims may require reconstructive surgery, physical therapy, or psychological  
counseling to recover. These treatments can be costly, and victims deserve compensation for both their  
immediate medical needs and any long-term care required.

**Georgia’s Dog Bite Laws**

Georgia’s dog bite laws are based on a mixture of statutory law and common law principles, with  
certain legal nuances that can make pursuing a claim challenging without the help of an attorney.  
Georgia is considered a modified "one bite rule" state, which means that a dog owner may be held  
liable for injuries caused by their dog if:

  * The dog was known to be dangerous or had a history of aggression.
  * The owner was negligent in controlling or restraining the dog.
  * The attack occurred because the dog was not properly leashed, and the local leash laws were violated.



While it may seem straightforward, proving that the dog owner was aware of the animal’s aggressive tendencies or that they violated local laws can require substantial evidence. This is where a personal  
injury lawyer’s expertise becomes invaluable.

**Compensation for Dog Bite Victims in Georgia**

In Georgia, dog bite victims can seek various forms of compensation, including:

  * Medical Expenses: This includes costs for emergency treatment, surgeries, medications, physical  
therapy, and ongoing care.
  * Lost Wages: If your injury causes you to miss work, you can be compensated for lost income.
  * Pain and Suffering: This covers the physical pain and emotional trauma caused by the attack,  
including the psychological effects of the injury.
  * Permanent Disability or Disfigurement: If the dog bite causes permanent scarring or long-term disability, you may receive additional compensation for these lasting impacts.



**Why You Need an Attorney**

Dog bite cases can be legally complex, particularly in Georgia, where proving negligence or a dog's  
dangerous behavior may require thorough investigation and strong legal arguments. Having an  
experienced personal injury attorney on your side can significantly improve your chances of receiving  
the compensation you deserve.

pages.title: How long does it take to get divorced? – by Ryan Farmer
pages.description: The simple answer is… it depends. No two divorces are the same and if an attorney ever tells you that they can have your case wrapped up in a certain amount of
pages.h1: How long does it take to get divorced? – by Ryan Farmer
pages.content_md:
The simple answer is… it depends. No two divorces are the same and if an attorney ever  
tells you that they can have your case wrapped up in a certain amount of time or promise you a  
certain result, you should immediately run. No attorney can ever guarantee you a result or that  
they can wrap your case up in a definite period of time. Why, you might ask? First and foremost,  
neither your attorney nor the attorney on the other side have any way to control the final  
outcome. The only person that decides the ultimate outcome of your case is the trier of fact –  
either a judge or jury. Though no attorney can give you a definitive answer, most divorce or  
domestic matters take anywhere from 6 to 12 months to complete, although it can take longer  
due to the depth and intricacies of the various issues in your case.

**What can you do to ensure your case is handled timely and effectively?**

For starters, hiring the right attorney is the single most important decision you’ll make in  
any legal proceeding. Ensuring that you hire someone who is honest, driven, and prepared will  
go further to ensure a positive result than anything else. The worst thing you can do for your case  
is hire an attorney who is not honest and who is unprepared.

Second, listen to your attorney. You’ve invested time and likely substantial money into  
someone to represent your best interests and get you the best possible result, so you need to trust  
that person when they tell you what to do or not to do. At times, the advice they give you may  
not be exactly what you want to hear, but it’s important to remember that your attorney  
understands both the legal and practical issues involved in your matter. As was stated earlier,  
there are numerous factors that impact your case. Such factors involve not just the law or facts of  
your case but also the practical intricacies like strategery in the courtroom or the common  
approach an opposing counsel may take.

Finally, communication with your attorney is vital. Making sure you hire an attorney  
where you’re not just another case or number is important to ensure that communication between  
you and them is as desired. Throughout your case there will be periods where you may not hear  
much from your attorney, for instance during the discovery process, while there will be periods  
where you talk to your attorney on a weekly or even daily basis to deal with emergency matters  
or to prepare for an upcoming hearing. However, you should always be able to speak with your  
attorney within a reasonable amount of time after contacting them.

Beware of attorneys who promise you any result or tell you they can have your case wrapped up  
in a certain period of time. Our attorneys at Parian Lawyers are committed to open and honest  
communication with you in a timely fashion and will always be honest and prepared when it  
comes to your case. Give us a call today to setup an appointment to see if our office is a good fit  
for you in your matter.

pages.h1: The Dangers of Truck Driver Fatigue: What Georgia Drivers Need to Know
pages.content_md:
Driving on Georgia's highways, especially near Interstate 20, it's not uncommon to share the road with large commercial trucks. While these trucks are vital to our economy, they can also pose serious risks when the drivers behind the wheel are fatigued. Truck driver fatigue is a leading cause of accidents on the road, and if you or a loved one has been involved in an accident caused by a drowsy truck driver, it�s important to know your rights.

### What Is Truck Driver Fatigue?

Truck driver fatigue occurs when a driver operates a commercial vehicle while physically or mentally exhausted, reducing their ability to make quick decisions and react to road conditions. Long hours behind the wheel, tight delivery schedules, and pressure from employers often contribute to truck drivers pushing their limits. This fatigue impairs their judgment, slows reaction times, and increases the likelihood of an accident.

### Federal Regulations to Prevent Fatigue

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) has regulations in place to help prevent truck driver fatigue. These regulations, known as Hours of Service (HOS) rules, limit the number of hours a truck driver can be on the road before taking mandatory rest breaks. For example:

  * Truckers can drive a maximum of 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty.
  * Drivers must take a 30-minute break after 8 hours of driving.
  * There is a 60/70-hour limit for driving in a 7- or 8-day workweek.



Despite these regulations, many drivers may feel pressured to exceed these limits to meet delivery deadlines or avoid losing pay.

### How Fatigue Leads to Accidents

Fatigue affects a driver's ability to stay alert and focused. Just like driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, drowsy driving impairs decision-making and coordination. Common behaviors of fatigued truck drivers include:

  * Drifting between lanes
  * Difficulty maintaining a constant speed
  * Failing to recognize traffic signals or road signs
  * Slower reaction times



These behaviors create dangerous situations for other drivers on the road, especially on high-traffic routes like Interstate 20.

### Why Truck Driver Fatigue Is So Dangerous

Due to the size and weight of commercial trucks, accidents involving these vehicles are often catastrophic. A fatigued driver operating an 80,000-pound truck poses a serious threat to anyone on the road. Victims of these accidents may suffer severe injuries such as broken bones, traumatic brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, or even death.

### Georgia Law and Truck Driver Fatigue

Georgia law holds commercial trucking companies and their drivers accountable for negligence, including cases of driver fatigue. If a truck driver violates FMCSA regulations or drives without adequate rest, and this leads to an accident, they can be held liable for the damages caused. This includes medical bills, lost wages, pain and suffering, and more.

### What To Do If You�ve Been in a Truck Accident

If you or a loved one has been injured in a truck accident near Interstate 20 or anywhere else in Georgia, it�s crucial to act quickly. Trucking companies often have legal teams ready to defend their drivers and protect their interests. You need an experienced personal injury attorney who understands how to investigate these cases, gather evidence, and build a strong claim on your behalf.

### How We Can Help

At Parian Lawyers, we are dedicated to protecting the rights of accident victims. We understand the complexities of truck accident cases, including the role of driver fatigue, and we know how to hold trucking companies accountable. Our team will work tirelessly to ensure you receive the compensation you deserve. We offer free consultations, and if you�ve been involved in a truck accident, don�t hesitate to reach out.

**Contact us today to schedule your consultation and learn how we can help you navigate your personal injury claim.**

pages.title: Georgia Dove Season 2021 – by Tyler Paul Smith
pages.description: The 2021 Georgia Dove season is fast approaching. Opening day for the first part of the season is on September 4th, 2021 with a significant change – shooting ho
pages.h1: Georgia Dove Season 2021 – by Tyler Paul Smith
pages.content_md:
The 2021 Georgia Dove season is fast approaching. Opening day for the first part of the season is on September 4th, 2021 with a significant change - shooting hours begin a half-hour before sunrise on opening day. Perhaps one of the most satisfying hunting experiences for every sportsman/ sportswoman, dove season is the first hunting season to begin the fall hunting seasons. It comes before any other season in the fall and offers one of the most challenging experiences for any hunter. It also provides the opportunity to run afoul of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources for hunting over a baited field. Under O.C.G.A. � 27-3-9 (b)(1), it is illegal �for any person to hunt any game bird or game animal upon, over, around, or near any place where any corn, wheat, or other grains, salts, apples, or other feed or bait has been placed, exposed, deposited, distributed, or scattered so as to constitute a lure, attraction, or enticement to such birds or animals.� Placing any of the above noted materials on a field will be considered baiting as it is an attempt to attract more birds to one field over another non baited field.

## Understanding Hunting Laws for Dove Season

Some of the key language in the statute to take note of is �upon, over, around, or near any place.� This statutory language was challenged over 30 years ago as unconstitutional for being vague and ambiguous. Notwithstanding constitutional challenges, the court found it was not vague and ambiguous. The language itself sets up a scenario where you have two adjacent fields, one baited and one not baited. Due to the two fields being adjacent to each other, the baited field will prohibit the adjacent field from being hunted as the court would find such a scenario satisfies the statutory language of hunting �upon, over, around, or near any place.� Many hunters do this to be sure, even though they may know the consequences. There are several ways a hunter can be reprimanded for such action but this synopsis will focus on one in particular.

## Legal Consequences for a Baited Field During Dove Season

The most common punishment for a baited field during dove season, that is if no one is hunting over it, will usually result in the Georgia DNR rangers shutting down the field for a period of time. Georgia prohibits a field from being hunted for a period of ten days after the complete removal of such feed or bait. To clarify, if a field is found to have been baited, the bait must be removed and will not be open to hunters for a period of ten days after the bait is removed. The most common form of baiting takes the form of spreading loose corn around a field. Field corn is usually a favorite among those who use this method. The punishment for a person found to be hunting over a baited field is a misdemeanor of a high and aggravated nature with the maximum punishment resulting in 12 months in jail and a $5,000.00 fine. The Georgia DNR ranger when finding a baited field will require the land owner to remove the bait from the baited field or area.

In addition to the requirements of removing the bait from the field, DNR will require that a landowner erect signs on the area land or fields stating �No Hunting, Baited Field.� The signs must remain on the field for ten days after the removal of the bait from the field. If you are confused yet do not worry because this is not very easily deciphered at first glance. The main point is to not bait a field so close to season because it will invite more legal trouble than many wish to deal with.

Dove season is broken down into segments with the first period starting on September 4th and will run through October 10th; the second period will run from November 20th to November 28th; the third and final period will run from December 19th through January 31st. The limit is 15 per day and 45 in possession. If you are caught baiting a field remember it may very well keep you from being able to hunt that field for the majority of each period of dove season since the field will be closed for 10 days after the complete removal of bait from the field.

Many hunters in the area undoubtedly test the limits of this baiting statute. Should a hunter have engaged in baiting a field, the corn would have to be completely consumed by Tuesday August 23rd. This would allow for 10 days of no bait being on the field leading up to September 3rd. It is a very complicated process if you wish to risk baiting a field leading up to the season. The safest course of action is to refrain from baiting. It is not worth the risk of being charged and convicted of a misdemeanor.

Remember this is the first season of the year and the Georgia DNR Rangers will be patrolling to ensure everyone receives a fair hunt. They are there to enforce the law so that everyone has a chance to enjoy the great abundance of dove we have in the State of Georgia. The old adage applies to all of us dove hunters who wish to hunt and enjoy nature�s bounty without running afoul of the game warden, �Don�t go borrowing trouble.� It is not worth a misdemeanor on your record and having to shut down a good dove field because of baiting. Thanks to all the Georgia DNR Rangers who help us all to continue our good stewardship of Georgia�s Natural Resources in order for future generations to enjoy the same opportunities we enjoy today. Good luck this season and remember windage and elevation.

Tyler Paul Smith is an attorney with Parian Lawyers and practices in Carroll and Haralson Counties. A native of West Georgia with family roots going back almost 200 years, Tyler Paul is an avid hunter and wildlife conservationist. Tyler Paul is also the District 18 State House Representative for the majority of Haralson and northern Carroll Counties in the Georgia General Assembly.

pages.title: What Laws Apply if You are Hit by a Company Truck in Georgia?
pages.description: If you were hit by a company van or truck in Georgia, careful diligence is required to determine whether the vehicle is subject to key commercial vehicle regula
pages.h1: What Laws Apply if You are Hit by a Company Truck in Georgia?
pages.content_md:
If you were hit by a company van or truck in Georgia, careful diligence is required to determine whether the vehicle is subject to key commercial vehicle regulations.� It is common for inexperienced attorneys to mistakenly assume the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations do not apply to companies that solely operate intrastate or to drivers that do not hold a commercial driver�s license (CDL).

In fact, Georgia law places strict commercial regulations on any vehicle that both weighs over 10,000 pounds and is used within state lines for commercial purposes.� These regulations apply even if the driver does not hold a CDL.� Correspondingly, Georgia�s Department of Public Safety adopted several of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations.�**�**

## When Do �The Federal Safety Rules� Apply in Georgia?

Georgia applies the Federal Safety Rules to commercial vehicles that weigh over 10,000 pounds and are used in commerce. Generally, there are two weight classes of vehicles. First, vehicles weighing over 10,000 pounds but less than 14,000 pounds like a Dodge 3500, a Ford E-350, or a GMC Sierra 3500.� Alternatively, vehicles weighing 14,000 to 18,000 pounds like a Dodge 4500 or 5500; a Ford E-450 or F550; or a GMC 4500 or 5500. Drivers of either weight class of a commercial vehicle:

  1. Are forbidden from using radar detectors;
  2. Must conduct pre- and post-trip safety inspections on the vehicles;
  3. Must do annual safety inspections of the vehicle;
  4. Must take an annual DOT physical exam (Keep an eye out for drivers on duty who have serious medical issues like an insulin dependence for example); and
  5. Must maintain time records and not stay on duty beyond the Hours of Service limitations.



## Hours of Service Limitations

Drivers with an operational radius over 150 miles are considered long-haul or �over-the-road� drivers and are subject to the Federal Hours of Service Regulations. Similarly, strict rules restrict short-haul drivers from driving for over 11 hours maximum and only after 10 hours being off duty.� Additionally, employers are required to maintain accurate time records for 6 months and revisit them on a rolling basis.� These records may make or break a case. Take for example a case where a beverage company driver testified that he habitually worked more than 10 hours per day without a break.� He also testified that at the time of the subject wreck, he was on duty for 12 hours.� Since testimony may not always result in a blatant admission, it is essential to send spoliation letters and request the required time records are produced during discovery.� In the event an employer fails to retain time records, the presumption can be made that the records support that the driver was overly fatigued.

Vehicles that operate across state lines and weighing over 10,000 pounds must adhere to separate federal regulations including:

  * Drivers must undergo a valid US DOT physical exam.
  * Drivers must follow the regular Hours of Service requirements.
  * Drivers must display the DOT number on the side of the vans.
  * Drivers must have proof of the vehicle�s annual inspection.



In sum, there are several Georgia regulations an employer must comply with when operating with a larger commercial truck or van. �Our Metro Atlanta and West Georgia attorneys can answer your questions about [tractor-trailer wrecks.](https://westgalawyer.com/carrollton-truck-accident-lawyer/)

pages.title: What You Need to Know if Your Employer Wants You to Return to Work Against Your Doctor�s Order

pages.h1: What You Need to Know if Your Employer Wants You to Return to Work Against Your Doctor�s Order
pages.content_md:
Aside from friends and family, many people consider their jobs the most important aspect of their lives. Largely because their job is not only a way to pay the bills, but a source of purpose and meaning. It can be tempting to return to work against a doctor�s orders when an employer asks an injured worker to do so.� However, beware of returning to work against a doctor�s wishes, it may be not only bad for your health, but your ability to recover benefits in the future.

If your employer has asked you to return to work despite your doctor�s advice to stay home and rest, contact our�[workers� compensation lawyers](https://westgalawyer.com/carrollton-workers-compensation-lawyer/)�at Parian Injury Law to discuss your best course of action. We can advise you of the benefits and pitfalls of returning to work in your current condition.

## The Trouble with Returning to Work Before You Are Medically Cleared and Physically Ready

Even if your employer may be encouraging you to return to work, the reasons not to return to work against your doctor�s orders are innumerous. First, you may limit your eligibility to receive workers� compensation benefits in the future.� For example, if you cannot handle the physical demands of your job, and while attempting to do it anyway, you re-injure yourself, you may not be eligible for future workers� compensation benefits. Similarly, you can lose your job. Take for example if you are unable to perform your job duties, your employer may ultimately fire you. In this case, you would be out of both a job and your workers� compensation benefits. Also, considering your inability to fully function as you would normally, it may prove difficult to find a new job in your desired line of work due to your injured state.

## If Your Employer Threatens to Fire You

It is illegal for an employer to terminate you in retaliation to you for filing your workers� compensation claim. If your employer threatens to fire you while you recover from injuries, consult with an attorney. Alternatively, if you decide to return to work before reaching maximum medical improvement (MMI), you may be able to receive benefits for time lost intermittently, under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA).� Although FMLA does not apply to everyone, the federal act protects workers� positions for a maximum of 12 weeks when they must deal with caring for their own injury or a family member�s injury or illness. If FMLA applies to you, it protects your job, and you may also be entitled to lost wage compensation.**�**

## When Should You Return to Work?

After an injury, the only time you should ever return to work is once you have reached MMI and without urging, your doctor gave you the all-clear. If you must persuade your doctor to believe you are completely healed, you may be hurting both yourself and ultimately your career.

On the other hand, if your employer is pressuring you to return to work even though your doctor has not advised you to do so, you need to consult with a workers� compensation lawyer. At Parian Injury Law we can advise you on what you need to do to protect your rights to workers� compensation and your position. Call one of our attorneys�today.

pages.title: My Lawyer Won�t Call Me Back, Can I Fire Him?
pages.description: Being mad at your attorney is frustrating. When you don�t think your attorney is helping you, we recommend you pick up the phone and demand to speak to the atto
pages.h1: My Lawyer Won�t Call Me Back, Can I Fire Him?
pages.content_md:
Being mad at your attorney is frustrating. When you don�t think your attorney is helping you, we recommend you pick up the phone and demand to speak to the attorney in charge of your case. Not the case manager or the paralegal. Our [personal injury and criminal defense lawyers](/) know that when a client (or potential client) wants to talk to them, they better pick up the phone. Here are some tips written by the attorney Cade Parian on how to deal with the most common issues that come up between attorneys and clients.

## What to Do if Your Lawyer Isn�t Calling You Back

Your lawyer is responsible for communicating with his or her clients. If your attorney is not calling you back or is hard to reach, there are steps you can take.

  * Blow up the telephones � Tell the person who answers how many times you have called and not received a response. Be polite though. Kindness kills.
  * Ask for an in-person appointment with your lawyer to talk about your concerns. Clearly explain to your attorney what you need from them. Keep your expectations real though. Legal cases move at a mind-numbingly slow pace. Most of the time, that is not your lawyer�s fault.
  * To add on top of how slow things move in the legal system, you cannot expect to hear from your attorney on a daily basis (or many times even a weekly basis). Why? Nothing will have happened.
  * If your attorney will not take the time to meet with you, you have the wrong lawyer. You control the relationship. You can fire your lawyer anytime.**�**



## How Can I Tell if My Lawyer is Doing a Good Job?

It is hard to know whether your lawyer is doing a good job. The most important thing to stay on top of is whether a lawsuit is filed for your injuries before the statute of limitations expires. In Georgia, in most cases, a lawsuit must be filed within two years of the accident causing your injuries. There are exceptions, but two years is a good timeline to have in your head. Here are some other things you can do to investigate whether your lawyer is doing a good job.

  * Get in touch with your attorney and tell him or her your issues. Not the case manager. Not the paralegal. The attorney. Have the attorney explain to you what has been done on your case.
  * Obtain a copy of your file. You can either read it in your lawyer�s office or get an actual copy to read for yourself. If your lawyer refuses to let you review your file, you have the wrong lawyer.
  * Finally, there is nothing wrong or illegal about getting a second opinion.



Law firms are not all the same. In a lot of personal injury law firms, you are one of thousands of clients. A piece of the mill. That is not how it works at Parian Injury Law. Our lawyers are skilled at being brutally honest with potential clients about their claims. No-nonsense is our approach to solving problems and dealing with clients.
